mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old smoker has a bulge in the right groin through a weak posterior wall of the inguinal canal, just behind the superficial ring. Which structure reinforces the medial part of this posterior wall? [Prof 24. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior wall = fascia transversalis throughout + conjoint tendon (falx inguinalis) medially. Anterior wall = external oblique aponeurosis + internal oblique laterally. "2 Ms, 2 As, 2 Ls, 2 Ts" (MALT).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During an open hernia repair the surgeon incises the outermost layer forming the front of the inguinal canal to reach the spermatic cord. Which layer forms the anterior wall of the inguinal canal? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior wall." external oblique aponeurosis (whole length) + internal oblique fibres in the lateral third. Floor: inguinal ligament (lacunar medially). Roof: arching fibres of internal oblique and transversus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man with chronic cough has a globular swelling above the medial inguinal ligament that does not enter the scrotum; at surgery the sac lies medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. Through which area does this hernia protrude. [AMC 26 . BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hesselbach's triangle: inferior epigastric vessels (lateral), lateral border of rectus (medial), inguinal ligament (inferior). Direct hernia = MEDIAL to inferior epigastric artery. acquired weakness, wide neck, rarely strangulates.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old man has a painless oval swelling just above the left pubic symphysis and inguinal ligament that appears on coughing and walking and disappears on lying down; it does not descend into the scrotum. What is the most likely diagnosis. [KIMS 25. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reducible swelling with cough impulse = hernia. Medial, above the pubic tubercle, not entering scrotum. elderly = DIRECT. Femoral hernia lies below and lateral to the pubic tubercle.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old footballer has a reducible groin swelling descending into the scrotum. At surgery, the sac enters the canal through the deep ring. To which artery is the neck of this hernial sac lateral? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Indirect hernia passes through the deep ring LATERAL to the inferior epigastric artery along a patent processus vaginalis. "MDS don't Lle" Direct, Lateral Indirect.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon f inds a hernial sac lying lateral to the inferior epigastric artery and following the spermatic cord. What type of hernia is this? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Indirect = lateral, congenital (patent processus vaginalis), commonest hernia in both sexes, narrow neck 4 strangulation more likely.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Before surgery, a resident marks the surface position of the deep inguinal ring on a patient with an indirect hernia. Where is the deep inguinal ring located? [BWP 25]

options.A: Medial to the inferior epigastric artery
options.B: Above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament, lateral to the inferior epigastric artery
options.D: Above the inguinal ligament at the lateral border of rectus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Deep ring: oval opening in the fascia transversalis ~1.25 cm above the MID-INGUINAL point (midway between ASIS and pubic symphysis), lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man lifts a heavy load and develops a reducible left groin swelling with cough impulse entering the canal through the deep ring. In which layer is the deep inguinal ring (the weak point) formed? [CKMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Deep ring = opening in fascia transversalis (gives internal spermatic fascia). Superficial ring = opening in external oblique aponeurosis (gives external spermatic fascia). Cremaster comes from internal oblique.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A clinician reduces a groin hernia, presses firmly over a point just above the mid-inguinal point and asks the patient to cough; the swelling does not reappear. What does this deep ring occlusion test indicate. [CKMC 25. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ring occlusion test distinguishes INDIRECT from DIRECT: if controlled by pressure over the deep ring 4 indirect; if it bulges medially despite pressure direct.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman has a small tender swelling below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. At surgery the hernia passes through the femoral ring. Which structure forms the medial boundary of the femoral ring. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Femoral ring: anterior inguinal ligament," posterior pectineal ligament; medial - LACUNAR ligament (sharp edge 4 strangulation),. lateral - femoral vein. Femoral hernia is commoner in women.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old obese man has a small painful midline swelling between the xiphoid process and the umbilicus. What is this hernia called? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Epigastric hernia: protrusion of extraperitoneal fat through the linea alba above the umbilicus. Paraumbilical hernia is through the linea alba just above/below the umbilicus in adults.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old obese woman develops a bulge at the site of a midline laparotomy scar six months after surgery, more prominent on standing. Which anatomical feature of the midline explains this complication. [QIMS 25]

options.A: A rectus sheath present anteriorly and posteriorly
options.B: The linea alba is a relatively avascular aponeurotic raphe with poor healing
options.C: A rich vascular supply at the incision site
options.D: Crossing of internal oblique and transversus fibres at the midline

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Linea alba is a fibrous, relatively avascular raphe: incisions bleed little (quick access) but heal with weaker scar ￿ incisional hernia, especially with obesity. infection and coughing.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon needs rapid access to the abdomen in a trauma patient and chooses a midline incision because it bleeds very little. Through which structure does this incision pass. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Linea alba = fusion of all three aponeuroses from xiphoid to pubic symphysis. Bloodless. nerve-free 4 fast midline laparotomy; wide below-umbilicus in pregnancy (divarication of recti).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a lower midline laparotomy, the surgeon sees that below a curved line midway between the umbilicus and pubis only a thin layer lies behind rectus abdominis. Below which line is the posterior aponeurotic wall of the rectus sheath absent? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arcuate line (of Douglas): below it all three aponeuroses pass ANTERIOR to rectus; only fascia transversalis lies behind. Inferior epigastric vessels enter the sheath here.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon makes a paramedian incision between the costal margin and the arcuate line and f irst cuts the anterior wall of the rectus sheath. Which aponeuroses form the anterior wall of the rectus sheath at this level? [BWP 26. KIMS 25]

options.C: External oblique and anterior lamina of internal oblique

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the KIMS 2025 key marked "internal oblique and transversus" that is the POSTERIOR wall. Between costal margin and arcuate line: anterior = EO + anterior lamina of10," posterior = posterior lamina of10 + transversus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgical trainee asks which layer of the rectus sheath receives the aponeurosis of transversus abdominis above the arcuate line. To which layer does it contribute. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked "anterior layer"; the standard textbook answer is POSTERIOR layer above the arcuate line. Below the arcuate line transversus passes in front of rectus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An anatomy demonstrator shows the sheath enclosing rectus abdominis to students. Which aponeuroses form the rectus sheath? [BWP 25]

options.A: External oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rectus sheath contents: rectus, pyramidalis, superior & inferior epigastric vessels, lower six thoracic nerves (T7-T12) and their vessels.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old hypertensive woman on anticoagulants develops a painful tender mass in the lower anterior abdominal wall after a coughing bout; ultrasound shows a rectus sheath haematoma. Which vessel is most likely damaged? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rectus sheath haematoma usually arises from the INFERIOR epigastric vessels below the arcuate line. where there is no posterior sheath to limit spread; mimics an acute abdomen.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: In a patient with long-standing coarctation, the surgeon notes a dilated vessel inside the rectus sheath forming a collateral channel. With which artery does the superior epigastric artery anastomose? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior epigastric (from internal thoracic 4 subclavian) meets inferior epigastric (from external iliac) within rectus sheath collateral in aortic coarctation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A trauma surgeon ligates a bleeding vessel supplying the lower part of rectus abdominis below the arcuate line. Which artery is this. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inferior epigastric artery arises from the external iliac just above the inguinal ligament, runs medial to the deep ring, enters the rectus sheath at the arcuate line.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient's rectus abdominis is injured in an accident and the surgeon tests which nerves supply the muscle. Which of these nerves does NOT supply rectus abdominis. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key was unclear. Rectus abdominis is supplied by the ventral rami of T7-T12 (lower intercostal + subcostal). Iliohypogastric (Ll) supplies internal oblique/transversus and suprapubic skin, not rectus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man has an inguinal hernia repair. A fluid collection later tracks from the abdominal wall into the perineum and scrotum but not into the thigh. Which layer of superficial fascia allows this spread? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Scarpa's (membranous) fascia continues as Colles, fascia in the perineum. dartos in the scrotum, but fuses with fascia lata just below the inguinal ligament 4 fluid cannot enter the thigh.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with IVC obstruction shows dilated, tortuous superficial veins running from the groin up to the axilla on the lateral trunk. Which vein forms this superficial collateral? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thoracoepigastric vein links the superficial epigastric (￿ femoral) and lateral thoracic (4 axillary) veins: a caval-caval anastomosis; flow is upward in IVC obstruction.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During an inguinal hernia repair, a surgeon traces the nerves near the inguinal ligament. Which nerve does NOT pierce or pass beneath the inguinal ligament? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Iliohypogastric nerve runs above the canal and pierces the external oblique aponeurosis-2.5 cm above the superficial ring to supply suprapubic skin; it never crosses the inguinal ligament.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On stroking the upper medial thigh of a man, the ipsilateral testis does not rise. Which nerve supplies the cremaster muscle (efferent limb of this reflex)? [Prof 24]

options.B: Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cremasteric reflex: afferent - femoral branch of genitofemoral (+ ilioinguinal)," efferent - GENITAL branch of genitofemoral (Ll-L2). Absent in testicular torsion.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man has groin pain on extending the hip (positive psoas sign) due to a muscle that arises from the lumbar vertebrae and inserts into the lesser trochanter. Which muscle is this. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Psoas major: T12-L5 bodies, discs and transverse processes 4 lesser trochanter (with iliacus): main hip flexor," supplied by LI-L3. Lumbar plexus forms within it.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has abdominal viscera protruding through the umbilical ring into a thin, transparent sac covered by amnion; the cord inserts into the sac. What is the condition. [AMC 25. WMC 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Omphalocele: viscera in a peritoneum-amnion sac AT the umbilicus; associated with trisomies, cardiac defects, Beckwith-wiedemann. Gastroschisis." no sac, right of umbilicus, rarely associated anomalies.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neonate is born with an omphalocele containing small bowel and liver. Failure of which embryological process causes this anomaly. [WMC 26]

options.B: Return of the physiologically herniated midgut into the abdominal cavity
options.C: Fusion of the lateral body folds

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Physiological umbilical herniation occurs in week 6,. the midgut returns in week 10. Failure to return = omphalocele. Gastroschisis results from defective closure of the lateral body wall folds.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has loops of intestine lying outside the abdomen to the right of a normal umbilical cord, with no covering membrane. What is the diagnosis. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gastroschisis: full-thickness defect lateral (usually right) to the umbilicus; bowel exposed to amniotic fluid ￿ thickened, matted loops; young mothers," good prognosis after repair.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An infant has a non~healing, moist umbilicus with occasional discharge of foul-smelling faecal material. What is the most likely congenital anomaly. [AMC 26. MUL 26. BWP 26. LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Faeces from the umbilicus = patent vitello-intestinal duct (vitelline fistula). Urine from the umbilicus = patent urachus. Partial persistence: Meckel's diverticulum. vitelline cyst or fibrous band.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child has foul-smelling stool discharging through the umbilicus from a persistent f istula. With which part of the gut does the fistula communicate internally. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The vitelline duct joins the apex of the midgut loop, which becomes the ILEUM; Meckel's diverticulum lies on the antimesenteric border~2 feet (60 cm) from the ileocaecal valve.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A baby has clear fluid that smells of urine leaking from the umbilicus, worse on crying. What is the cause? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Urachus = remnant of the allantois connecting bladder apex to umbilicus ￿ median umbilical ligament. Patent urachus may present when there is bladder outlet obstruction (posterior urethral valves).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon passes a finger into the opening behind the free edge of the lesser omentum to reach the omental bursa. Which vessel lies posterior to this opening? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Epiploic foramen (of Winslow): anterior - free margin of lesser omentum (portal triad); posterior - IVC (and right crus); superior - caudate process of liver: inferior 1st part of duodenum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a cholecystectomy, bleeding is controlled by inserting a f inger into the epiploic foramen and compressing its anterior wall (Pringle manoeuvre). Which structures form the anterior boundary. [HITEC 25. BWP 25]

options.A: Hepatoduodenal ligament containing the portal triad

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Portal triad in the free edge of lesser omentum." bile duct (right, anterior), hepatic artery proper (left. anterior), portal vein (posterior). Pringle manoeuvre controls hepatic inflow.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During surgery, a surgeon applies a clamp to the right free margin of the lesser omentum to control bleeding from the liver. Which structures are compressed? [Prof 24]

options.A: Hepatic artery proper, bile duct and portal vein

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pringle manoeuvre: clamping the hepatoduodenal ligament stops hepatic arterial and portal inflow; continued bleeding suggests hepatic vein or IVC injury.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During cholecystectomy, after the cystic artery is cut, bleeding continues. The surgeon compresses the free edge of the lesser omentum. Which artery is controlled by this manoeuvre. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hepatic artery proper (from common hepatic after the gastroduodenal branch) runs in the free edge of lesser omentum and gives right and left hepatic arteries: the cystic artery usually arises from the right hepatic.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A CT scan shows a perforated duodenal ulcer; a surgeon identifies the structure just below the epiploic foramen. Which structure forms the inferior boundary of the epiploic foramen. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inferior boundary of the epiploic foramen = superior (1st) part of the duodenum and the hepatic artery as it passes forward.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Through which opening does the lesser sac normally communicate with the greater sac? Choose the opening. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The lesser sac (omental bursa) lies behind the stomach and lesser omentum." its only natural communication with the greater sac is the epiploic foramen.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with a perforated posterior gastric ulcer develops an abscess in the lesser sac. The surgeon plans the commonest open route to drain it. Which peritoneal fold is usually divided to enter the lesser sac? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked "epiploic foramen" Surgically, the lesser sac is opened widely through the gastrocolic ligament (greater omentum) below the gastroepiploic arcade," the foramen is too small for drainage.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 40~year-old alcoholic with acute pancreatitis develops a pseudocyst that pushes the stomach forward on CT. In a normal CT, the body of the pancreas lies posterior to which structure, separated from it by the lesser sac. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pancreas forms the main part of the stomach bed (posterior wall of lesser sac)," pseudocysts collect in the lesser sac behind the stomach.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student lists the derivatives of the dorsal mesogastrium. Which structure is derived from the dorsal mesentery? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dorsal mesogastrium 4 greater omentum, gastrosplenic and splenorenal ligaments, gastrophrenic ligament; spleen develops within it. Ventral mesogastrium 4 lesser omentum, falciform, coronary and triangular ligaments.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student studying stomach development asks which organ develops within the dorsal mesogastrium. Which organ is it? [LHR 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spleen arises from mesenchyme in the dorsal mesogastrium (mesodermal, not endodermal) - so it is not a gut derivative; its arterial supply is the splenic branch of the foregut (coeliac) artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Embryology viva: a student names the structures formed in the ventral mesogastrium (septum transversum). Which group is derived from the ventral mesogastrium. [LHR 25]

options.D: Liver, lesser omentum and falciform ligament

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ventral mesogastrium: liver grows into it, dividing it into lesser omentum (stomach ￿ liver) and falciform ligament (liver 4 anterior abdominal wall),. coronary and triangular ligaments also arise from it.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A trainee sees a crescentic peritoneal fold attaching the liver to the anterior abdominal wall and diaphragm, containing the ligamentum teres in its free edge. Which ligament is this. [AMC 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Falciform ligament: liver to anterior abdominal wall and diaphragm," free lower border contains ligamentum teres (obliterated left umbilical vein) and paraumbilical veins (caput medusae route).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During splenectomy, the surgeon divides the peritoneal fold passing from the spleen to the left kidney, taking care of the structures within it. What does the splenorenal (lienorenal) ligament contain. [MUL 25. MUL 26]

options.C: Splenic vessels and tail of the pancreas

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Splenorenal ligament: splenic vessels + tail of pancreas (injury 4 pancreatic fistula). Gastrosplenic ligament: short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a perforated ulcer, a 50-year-old man develops fever and right shoulder-tip pain due to pus collecting below the diaphragm. Through which nerve is this pain referred to the shoulder. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Central diaphragmatic peritoneum is supplied by the phrenic nerve (C3-C5); C4 dermatome covers the shoulder tip (Kehr's sign). Peripheral diaphragm is supplied by lower intercostal nerves.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Pus from a right subphrenic abscess tracks downward behind the peritoneum and presents as a swelling in the groin. Along which muscle does it track? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Retroperitoneal pus (e.g. tuberculous spine. perinephric abscess) tracks within the psoas sheath to the femoral triangle/lesser trochanter - psoas abscess.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a perforated anterior duodenal ulcer develops pain that shifts to the right iliac fossa, mimicking appendicitis. Along which peritoneal space does the fluid track? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Right paracolic gutter connects the hepatorenal pouch (Morison's) with the right iliac fossa and pelvis. The left gutter is limited above by the phrenicocolic ligament.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man with a perforated gastric ulcer has severe upper abdominal pain as gastric fluid spreads over the peritoneal surface. What is the source of this irritation and pain. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chemical peritonitis: parietal peritoneum is supplied by somatic nerves (lower intercostal T7-T12) 4 sharp, well-localised pain with guarding; visceral peritoneum is insensitive to cutting but sensitive to stretch.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man with a perforated gastric ulcer has severe epigastric visceral pain. Which nerves carry this visceral pain from the stomach? [KIMS 25. CKMC 26. LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gastric visceral pain afferents travel with sympathetic fibres in the greater splanchnic nerves (T5-T9) 4 referred to the epigastrium. Vagal afferents carry nausea and reflex signals, not pain. Once fluid irritates the parietal peritoneum. lower intercostal nerves give sharp localised pain.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A medical student notes that the caecum, although covered by peritoneum on all sides, has no true mesentery. Which organ is intraperitoneal but lacks a true mesentery. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The caecum is usually completely peritonealised but without a mesentery - so it is mobile; retrocaecal recess lies behind it (commonest position of the appendix).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A radiologist reviewing a CT identifies a part of the large bowel that is plastered to the posterior abdominal wall with peritoneum only on its front and sides. Which part of the colon is usually retroperitoneal? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Secondarily retroperitoneal: ascending and descending colon. duodenum (2nd-4th parts), pancreas (except tail). Intraperitoneal with mesentery: transverse and sigmoid colon.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student is asked to identify a truly intraperitoneal organ among abdominal viscera. Which of these is intraperitoneal? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Intraperitoneal: stomach, 1st 2.5 cm of duodenum, jejunum, ileum. transverse and sigmoid colon, liver, spleen. Mnemonic for retroperitoneal: SAD PUCKER (Suprarenals, Aorta/lVC, Duodenum 2-4, Pancreas, Ureters, Colon asc/desc, Kidneys, Esophagus. Rectum).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50~year-old man undergoes endoscopy; resistance is felt where the oesophagus pierces the diaphragm. At what vertebral level is this lower constriction? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oesophageal constrictions (from incisors): 15 cm - C6 (cricopharyngeus); 22.5 cm - T4 (aortic arch)," 27.5 cm - T5 (left bronchus); 40 cm - TIO (diaphragm). Common sites of impaction, strictures and carcinoma.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman with long-standing GERD has Barrett's oesophagus on biopsy. Which anatomical feature normally prevents reflux of gastric contents into the oesophagus. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Antireflux mechanisms: LES (physiological sphincter), right crus pinchcock, acute angle of His, intra-abdominal oesophagus (positive pressure), mucosal rosette at the cardia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with long-standing ref lux has a biopsy of the lower oesophagus showing Barrett's oesophagus. Which epithelium has replaced the normal lining. [Prof 24]

options.A: Simple columnar (intestinal type with goblet cells)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Barrett's = metaplasia of non-keratinised stratified squamous to columnar epithelium with goblet cells 4 precursor of adenocarcinoma of the lower oesophagus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide of the oesophagus shows mucous glands deep to the muscularis mucosae. Where are the oesophageal glands proper located? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oesophageal glands proper lie in the SUBMUCOSA (only the oesophagus and duodenum have submucosal glands in the GIT). Oesophageal cardiac glands lie in the lamina propria near the ends.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Sections from different levels of the oesophagus show skeletal muscle in the upper part, smooth muscle in the lower part and a mixture in between. Which description of the muscularis externa is correct? [WMC 25]

options.D: Upper 1/3 skeletal, middle 1/3 mixed, lower 1/3 smooth

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Upper third - skeletal (vagus via nucleus ambiguus).. lower third - smooth (enteric/dorsal vagal nucleus). Achalasia affects the smooth-muscle part,. myasthenia/bulbar palsy affect the upper part.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has excessive drooling and coughs during feeds; a nasogastric tube coils in the upper oesophagus and there is gas in the stomach. Failure of which embryological process causes this anomaly. [QIMS 25]

options.B: Normal clockwise rotation of the stomach
options.C: Complete partitioning of the foregut by the tracheo-oesophageal
options.D: Recanalization of the oesophageal lumen septum

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Commonest type (85%): proximal oesophageal atresia with distal tracheo-oesophageal fistula - defective tracheo-oesophageal septum. Maternal polyhydramnios; part of VACTERL.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn develops respiratory distress; imaging shows part of the stomach herniated into the thorax through an abnormally wide oesophageal hiatus. Which developmental process is most likely defective. [QIMS 25]

options.C: Development of the crura from the dorsal mesentery of the
options.D: Fusion of the pleuroperitoneal membranes oesophagus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Crura of the diaphragm develop from the dorsal mesentery of the oesophagus; a wide hiatus allows congenital hiatal hernia. Pleuroperitoneal membrane failure ￿ posterolateral (Bochdalek) hernia, usually left.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A barium swallow in a young man with progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids shows a dilated oesophagus tapering smoothly at the lower end. What is this "bird's beak" appearance diagnostic of? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Achalasia: loss of inhibitory myenteric neurons (NO, VIP) 4 LES fails to relax + aperistalsis. Bird's beak on barium, confirmed by manometry. Carcinoma gives an irregular "rat-tail" shouldered stricture.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology lecturer explains how the stomach comes to lie with its left surface anterior. Around which axes does the developing stomach rotate. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stomach rotates 90° clockwise around the longitudinal axis (left vagus becomes anterior, greater curvature to the left) and around the AP axis (pylorus moves up and right. cardia down and left).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student is asked about stomach development. By how much and in which direction does the stomach rotate around its longitudinal axis. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 90° clockwise rotation (viewed from above) 4 left vagus anterior, right vagus posterior," lesser sac forms behind the stomach. Midgut, in contrast, rotates 27￿ anticlockwise.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 15-day-old boy has non-bilious projectile vomiting after each feed, visible gastric peristalsis and a palpable "olive in the epigastrium. What is the most likely diagnosis. [KIMS 25 . KIMS 26. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypertrophy of the circular muscle of the pylorus." first-born males. 2-8 weeks." hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis," Ramstedt pyloromyotomy. Bilious vomiting suggests obstruction distal to the ampulla. [Prof 25. BWP 26. LHR 25]

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man has a bleeding ulcer in the fundus of the stomach. Which artery mainly supplies the fundus.
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Short gastric arteries (4-5, from splenic artery via gastrosplenic ligament) supply the fundus. Lesser curvature - left & right gastric: greater curvature - gastroepiploics," posterior wall/body - splenic branches.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old man with chronic gastritis has bleeding from severe inflammation along the lesser curvature near the cardia. Which branch of the coeliac trunk supplies this area. [KIMS 25 . AMC 25 . MUL 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Left gastric artery - smallest branch of the coeliac trunk, runs up to the cardia then along the lesser curvature; supplies abdominal oesophagus. Lesser-curvature ulcer bleeding 4 left gastric artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon ligates the artery supplying the abdominal part of the oesophagus during a gastrectomy. Which artery supplies the abdominal oesophagus. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oesophagus: cervical - inferior thyroid,. thoracic aorta & bronchial," abdominal - left gastric (+ left inferior phrenic). Venous drainage of the lower end via left gastric vein = portosystemic site.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient presents with haematemesis from an ulcer on the posterior wall of the stomach penetrating into the stomach bed. Which artery running along the upper border of the pancreas is at risk? [AMC 26. HITEC 25 . LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note: the HITEC 2025 key marked left gastric. Posterior gastric wall ulcers erode the tortuous splenic artery on the upper border of the pancreas. Posterior duodenal ulcers erode the gastroduodenal artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During total gastrectomy, the surgeon divides the gastric arteries. Which artery must NOT be ligated because it supplies the liver? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked short gastric - but these are routinely divided in total gastrectomy. The common hepatic artery (and hepatic artery proper) must be preserved for liver supply.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a partial gastrectomy, the surgeon ligates the left gastric artery. To which part of the stomach is this artery closely related? [QIMS 25]

options.C: Pyloric canal close to the duodenum
options.D: Fundus near the left dome of the diaphragm

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Left gastric artery runs in the lesser omentum along the upper lesser curvature and anastomoses with the right gastric artery (from common/proper hepatic).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A bullet lodges at the tip of the left 9th costal cartilage in the transpyloric plane. Which structure is most likely damaged? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Left 9th costal cartilage tip (transpyloric plane, Ll) overlies the body of the stomach and the fundus of the gallbladder lies at the right 9th cartilage. Pylorus lies 1-2 cm right of midline at Ll.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old man with a perforated ulcer of the lesser curvature undergoes repair; afterwards he has delayed gastric emptying because a nerve running along the lesser curvature was damaged. Which nerve was most likely injured? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior and posterior vagal trunks give the nerves of Latarjet along the lesser curvature (motor to the antrum - "crow's foot"). Highly selective vagotomy spares the crow's foot to preserve gastric emptying.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man has carcinoma of the gastric fundus; CT shows enlarged nodes along the splenic hilum and upper border of the pancreas. Which lymph nodes receive drainage from the fundus of the stomach? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gastric lymph follows the arteries: fundus/upper greater curvature 4 pancreaticosplenic nodes (along short gastric/splenic); lesser curvature 4 left & right gastric nodes; pyloric part -> pyloric and right gastroepiploic nodes." all end in coeliac nodes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient undergoes truncal vagotomy for a refractory ulcer and later develops gastric stasis. Which nerve provides the parasympathetic innervation to the stomach? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vagus (anterior = left. posterior = right trunk) - motility and acid secretion; sympathetic (T6-T9. greater splanchnic via coeliac plexus) - vasoconstriction, pain afferents.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gastroenterologist explains the stomach bed during endoscopic ultrasound. Which structure forms part of the stomach bed? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stomach bed: left crus of diaphragm, left suprarenal, upper left kidney, splenic artery. pancreas, transverse mesocolon, + spleen and splenic flexure all separated by the lesser sac.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon repairing a perforated ulcer of the posterior gastric wall must avoid injuring the organ immediately behind it. Which structure behind the stomach needs particular care. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior gastric ulcers penetrate into the pancreas (back pain, raised amylase) and may erode the splenic artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist examines the muscular coat of the stomach wall. In which part does the muscularis externa have an additional innermost oblique layer most prominently. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stomach muscularis." inner oblique, middle circular (thickest - forms pyloric sphincter), outer longitudinal. The oblique layer is best developed in the fundus/body and absent at the pylorus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gastric biopsy from the fundus shows basophilic tall cells at the base of the glands with zymogen granules. Which cells are these. [LHR 25 . BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chief cells." basal, basophilic (rich RER) 4 pepsinogen and gastric lipase. Parietal cells: eosinophilic, mid-gland 4 HCI and intrinsic factor.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A fundic biopsy in chronic atrophic gastritis shows loss of large round eosinophilic cells in the glands. Which function is primarily lost if these cells are destroyed? [QIMS 25. WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parietal (oxyntic) cells secrete HCI and intrinsic factor," autoimmune destruction 4 pernicious anaemia, achlorhydria and raised gastrin.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old with a gastric ulcer has biopsies taken from the antrum, where most gastrin-secreting cells are found. In the glands of which region of the stomach are G cells located? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: G cells lie in pyloric/antral glands (and duodenum); gastrin stimulates parietal cells mainly via ECL-cell histamine release. Antrectomy removes the gastrin source.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Some pathogenic microorganisms reach the stomach with food. Which glands actively secrete the acid that kills most of these microorganisms. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked pyloric glands, with options not matching. The antimicrobial barrier is HCI from parietal cells, located in the FUNDIC (oxyntic) glands of fundus and body.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old man with a posterior ulcer in the first part of the duodenum presents with massive haematemesis. Which artery lying behind this part is most likely eroded? [Prof 24. MUL 26. KIMS 25 . LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gastroduodenal artery descends behind the 1st part of the duodenum (with bile duct and portal vein). Posterior duodenal ulcer 4 bleeding (GDA); anterior duodenal ulcer ￿ perforation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon ligates the gastroduodenal artery to control a bleeding ulcer. Which arterial anastomosis is most directly affected? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GDA gives the superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries, which anastomose with the inferior pancreaticoduodenal (from SMA) around the head of pancreas - a coeliac-SMA (foregut-midgut) link.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a Whipple procedure, the surgeon cuts an artery supplying the proximal half of the C-shaped duodenum and head of pancreas. Which artery is this. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Duodenum proximal to the major papilla = foregut (coeliac: superior pancreaticoduodenal from GDA): distal = midgut (SMA." inferior pancreaticoduodenal).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 62-year-old man has a tumour of the first part of the duodenum. Which organ is most likely invaded by inferior/posterior spread of the tumour. [Prof 24]

options.D: Transverse colon GDA, bile duct, portal vein; inferior head of pancreas; superior - epiploic

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Relations of 1st part: anterior - liver, gallbladder; posterior foramen.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A thin young woman after rapid weight loss has bilious vomiting; imaging shows the third part of the duodenum compressed between two vessels. Which artery crosses anterior to the third part of the duodenum. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SMA syndrome (Wilkie): loss of mesenteric fat narrows the aortomesenteric angle, compressing the 3rd part of duodenum between SMA (anterior) and aorta (posterior).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On CT, the head of the pancreas is seen nestled in the concavity of the duodenal C-loop. Which part of the duodenum lies lateral to (and is related to) the head of the pancreas? [LHR 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The descending (2nd) part curves around the head of the pancreas," the bile duct and main pancreatic duct open into it at the major duodenal papilla (posteromedial wall).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a right hemicolectomy the surgeon mobilises the duodenum and sees the IVC and aorta directly behind one part of it. Which part of the duodenum crosses in front of the IVC and aorta. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked the second part. The horizontal (3rd) part crosses anterior to the right ureter, right psoas, IVC and aorta, with the SMA/SMV in front of it.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man has bilious vomiting due to obstruction at the duodenojejunal junction. Which structure attaches the duodenojejunal flexure and helps identify it at surgery. [AMC 25. QIMS 25]

options.A: Ligament of Treitz (suspensory muscle of duodenum)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ligament of Treitz: fibromuscular band from the right crus of the diaphragm to the DJ flexure,. landmark separating upper from lower Gl bleeding and for malrotation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: The suspensory ligament of the duodenum is traced upward during laparotomy. To which structure does it attach superiorly? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ligament of Treitz arises from the RIGHT crus (which passes to the left around the oesophageal hiatus) and inserts into the 3rd/4th parts and DJ flexure.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During the 10th week of development, the herniated midgut returns to the abdominal cavity. Which part returns first? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Return begins with the proximaljejunum, which lies on the left; the caecal bud returns last, initially below the liver before descending to the right iliac fossa.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology lecturer describes the normal rotation of the midgut loop. By how many degrees and in which direction does it rotate (viewed from the front)? [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Midgut rotates 270° anticlockwise around the SMA: 90° during herniation (week 6) and 180° during return (week 10).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has bilious vomiting; imaging shows midgut malrotation with volvulus. Which developmental process is defective. [QIMS 25]

options.B: Fixation of the foregut to the dorsal mesogastrium
options.D: Complete herniation and 270° anticlockwise rotation of the midgut loop

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Malrotation = incomplete 27￿ rotation (non-rotation/reversed rotation); narrow mesenteric base twists ￿ midgut volvulus, Ladd bands across the duodenum. Bilious vomiting in a neonate is surgical until proven otherwise.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn with Down syndrome has bilious vomiting and a double-bubble sign on X-ray. Which developmental process is defective. [QIMS 25. CKMC 25]

options.A: Recanalization of the duodenum after epithelial proliferation
options.C: Partitioning of the cloaca by the urorectal septum

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Duodenal atresia." solid-stage lumen fails to recanalise (weeks 8- 10), usually distal to the ampulla 4 bilious vomiting, polyhydramnios, double bubble (stomach + proximal duodenum).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old child has painless rectal bleeding; a technetium scan shows ectopic gastric mucosa in a diverticulum. In which part of the intestine is it found? [Prof 24. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Meckel's rule of 2s: 2% of people, 2 feet from the ileocaecal valve, 2 inches long, 2 types of ectopic tissue (gastric, pancreatic), presents by age 2. True diverticulum on the antimesenteric border of the ileum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A medical student identifies the remnant of the embryonic duct connecting the midgut to the yolk sac. Which structure is a remnant of the vitello-intestinal duct? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vitelline remnants: Meckel's diverticulum (commonest), vitelline fistula, cyst, fibrous band (risk of volvulus). Urachus ￿ median umbilical ligament.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: In a 5-week embryo, the apex of the midgut loop is connected to the yolk sac. Through which structure is this connection made. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vitelline duct normally obliterates by week 7," the apex of the midgut loop becomes the distal ileum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A biopsy from the terminal ileum shows large lymphoid aggregates in the mucosa and submucosa. Where are these Peyer's patches most prominent? [CKMC 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Peyer's patches: aggregated lymphoid follicles in the lamina propria/submucosa of the ileum on the ANTIMESENTERIC border." covered by M cells. Typhoid ulcers are longitudinal over them.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old with typhoid fever develops intestinal bleeding from ulcerated lymphoid tissue. Which part of the GIT contains this enlarged lymphoid tissue. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Salmonella typhi invades through M cells over Peyer's patches 4 longitudinal ulcers in the terminal ileum 4 bleeding/perforation in the 3rd week.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On which border of the terminal ileum are the Peyer's patches (first seen around the 8th-9th week of development) located? Choose the correct site. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Peyer's patches lie opposite the mesenteric attachment (antimesenteric border) - the same border that carries Meckel's diverticulum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A biopsy from the ileum shows numerous lymphoid aggregates covered by specialised epithelium. What is the main functional role of this tissue. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Immunological protection of the gut lumen

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GALT.. M cells sample luminal antigens ￿ dendritic cells ￿ B cells switch to IgA 4 secretory IgA protects the mucosa.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Electron microscopy of the follicle-associated epithelium over lymphoid aggregates shows cells with microfolds instead of microvilli that transport antigens. In which part of the gut are these M cells most numerous. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: M (microfold) cells overlie Peyer's patches in the ileum; they are the entry route for Salmonella, Shigella, poliovirus and prions.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old boy has colicky pain, "red-currant jelly stools and a sausage-shaped mass in the right upper abdomen following a viral illness. What is the most common lead point for this intussusception in children? [BWP 25]

options.A: Enlarged Peyer's patches in the ileum

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ileocolic intussusception after viral infection: hypertrophied Peyer's patches act as the lead point. Meckel's diverticulum is a lead point in older children; tumours in adults.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A small-intestinal biopsy shows cells at the base of the crypts of Lieberkuhn with large eosinophilic granules. Which cells secrete lysozyme and defensins for innate immunity. [AMC 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Paneth cells: base of crypts (small intestine, appendix), eosinophilic granules containing lysozyme, defensins (cryptdins) and TNF-a control gut flora.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist compares sections of jejunum and ileum. One has tall, finger-like villi and prominent, closely packed plicae circulares. Which part is this. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Jejunum." thicker wall, prominent plicae, tall villi, wider lumen, few arcades with long vasa recta, less fat. Ileum: fewer plicae, Peyer's patches, many arcades with short vasa recta.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During laparotomy a surgeon sees a loop of small bowel with long vasa recta and only one or two arterial arcades in its mesentery. Which part of the bowel is this. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Jejunum." long vasa recta, 1-2 arcades, translucent windows in the mesentery. Ileum." short vasa recta, 4-5 arcades. fat-laden mesentery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student explains why the small intestine has a huge absorptive area (-250 m,). Which structural adaptation increases its absorptive capacity. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Amplification." plicae circulares (x3), villi (xlo). microvilli/brush border (x20) - total -600-fold increase in surface area.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A duodenal biopsy shows villi with crypts and mucous glands in the submucosa. Which feature identifies the duodenum histologically. [WMC 25. BWP 26]

options.B: Crypts of Lieberkuhn with Brunner's glands in the submucosa

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Brunner's glands (submucosal, alkaline mucus + HCO,- + urogastrone/EGF) are characteristic of the duodenum, mainly the 1st part - protect against acid chyme.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student studies the germ-layer origin of the gut. From which germ layer are the primitive gut and the epithelial lining of the GIT derived? [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Endoderm 4 epithelium and glands of the GIT (liver, pancreas). Splanchnic mesoderm 4 muscle. connective tissue, serosa. Neural crest 4 enteric neurons. Ectoderm 4 stomodeum and lower anal canal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has acute mesenteric ischaemia of the jejunum and ileum. Which artery primarily supplies the small intestine? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SMA (Ll) supplies the midgut." duodenum distal to papilla, jejunum, ileum, caecum. appendix, ascending colon and proximal 2/3 of transverse colon. Embolism usually lodges just distal to the middle colic artery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man has a gunshot wound in the midline just above the pubic bone with severe intraperitoneal bleeding. Which hollow viscus is most likely injured? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Coils of ileum occupy the lower abdomen and pelvis (hypogastrium); jejunum lies mainly in the upper left; stomach and duodenum are in the upper abdomen.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man has dull, poorly localised epigastric pain from inflammation of a foregut organ. To which spinal segments is visceral pain from the epigastrium (foregut) commonly referred? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Referred visceral pain." foregut 4 epigastrium (T5-T9); midgut 4 umbilicus (TIO); hindgut 4 hypogastrium (Tll-Ll). Afferents travel with greater, lesser and least splanchnic nerves.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 22-year-old man has pain that begins around the umbilicus and later shifts to the right iliac fossa with tenderness at McBurney's point. What explains this pattern of pain? [LHR 26]

options.B: Parietal pain followed by visceral pain
options.C: Visceral pain followed by parietal pain
options.D: Direct irritation of the sciatic nerve

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Early: visceral afferents (lesser splanchnic, TIO) 4 periumbilical, poorly localised. Later: inflamed appendix irritates parietal peritoneum (somatic, T12/LI) 4 sharp. localised RIF pain.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During an appendicectomy, the surgeon ligates the artery running in the free edge of the mesoappendix. Which artery is this? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Appendicular artery: branch of the posterior caecal or inferior division of the ileocolic artery (SMA); an end artery ￿ gangrene and perforation in appendicitis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: MRI shows inf lammation of the caecum and appendix in a patient with right lower quadrant tenderness. Which artery supplying this region is most likely involved? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ileocolic artery (terminal SMA branch) supplies the terminal ileum, caecum and appendix (via the appendicular artery).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During an appendicectomy, the appendix cannot be found. Which structures on the caecum are followed to its base? [KIMS 26. BWP 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: All three taeniae coli converge at the base of the appendix - a reliable surgical landmark,. the base lies -2 cm below the ileocaecaljunction.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon finds the appendix lying behind the caecum during appendicectomy. What is the most common position of the appendix. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Retrocaecal ~65%, pelvic~30%. Retrocaecal appendicitis irritates psoas (psoas sign); pelvic appendicitis irritates obturator internus (obturator sign) and bladder/rectum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with appendicitis has pain on passive extension of the right hip (positive psoas sign). With which position of the appendix is this sign classically associated? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Psoas sign = retrocaecal appendix lying on psoas. Obturator sign (pain on internal rotation of flexed hip) = pelvic appendix. Rovsing sign = RIF pain on pressing LIF.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide of a hollow organ shows an irregular lumen, a thin muscular coat and numerous lymphoid follicles filling the mucosa and submucosa. Which organ is this. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Appendix: colonic-type mucosa with few crypts. no villi, abundant lymphoid follicles ("abdominal tonsil"). A star-shaped lumen with transitional epithelium suggests the ureter.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A slide shows simple columnar epithelium with straight, unbranched tubular glands full of goblet cells but no villi. Which organ is this. [Prof 24. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Colon: no villi, straight crypts packed with goblet cells, absorptive colonocytes, no Paneth cells (normally), taeniae coli and appendices epiploicae externally.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist compares mucosal goblet-cell density along the gut. In which region are goblet cells most abundant? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked small intestine. Goblet cells increase distally along the gut and are MOST numerous in the colon and rectum (lubricate faeces); stomach and oesophagus have none.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A medical student palpates a segment of colon with sacculations and longitudinal muscle bands. Haustrations and taeniae coli are features of which part of the gut? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Large intestine (except appendix, rectum, anal canal): taeniae coli, haustra, appendices epiploicae. Rectum has no taeniae - they spread into a continuous longitudinal coat.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A barium study shows a part of the large intestine hanging freely on a long mesentery that can be lifted out of the wound easily. Which part of the large intestine is freely mobile and intraperitoneal? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Transverse colon (transverse mesocolon) and sigmoid colon (sigmoid mesocolon) are mobile and intraperitoneal; ascending/descending colon are fixed retroperitoneally.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An elderly man has massive abdominal distension; X-ray shows a coffee-bean" loop arising from the pelvis - sigmoid volvulus. Which anatomical feature predisposes this part of the colon to twisting. [QIMS 25]

options.D: Long mesentery with a narrow base

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sigmoid mesocolon is long with a narrow root (inverted V) 4 torsion. especially with chronic constipation and high-fibre diets. Caecal volvulus requires a mobile caecum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has ischaemic colitis confined to the descending colon. Which artery directly supplies this segment of the colon. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: IMA (L3) supplies the hindgut: distal 1/3 transverse. descending. sigmoid colon. upper rectum. Watershed zones: splenic flexure (Griffiths, point) and rectosigmoid (Sudeck's point).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a sigmoid colectomy, the surgeon ligates several arteries running in the sigmoid mesocolon. From which artery do the sigmoid arteries arise. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: IMA branches: left colic, 2-4 sigmoid arteries, superior rectal (continuation). Marginal artery of Drummond connects SMA and IMA territories.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An aortic aneurysm repair requires ligation of the superior mesenteric artery close to its origin. Which part of the bowel is most likely to become ischaemic. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SMA supplies the caecum, appendix and right colon (via ileocolic/right colic). Sigmoid and rectum are supplied by IMA and iliac branches; 1st part of duodenum by coeliac branches.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has no anal opening; the rectum ends blindly just above a thin membrane in the anal region. Which developmental process is primarily defective. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Migration of neural crest cells to the hindgut

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low imperforate anus: persistent anal (proctodeal) membrane. High anomalies result from abnormal division of the cloaca by the urorectal septum, often with rectourethral/rectovaginal fistula.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 5-day~old neonate has failure to pass meconium and abdominal distension; contrast enema shows a massively dilated proximal colon ending in a narrow, non-distended distal segment. What is the diagnosis and its basis. [KIMS 26 . HITEC 26]

options.B: Hirschsprung disease - absent enteric ganglion cells in the distal bowel

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hirschsprung disease." failure of neural crest migration ￿ aganglionic distal segment (rectosigmoid) that cannot relax 4 functional obstruction," the DILATED segment is normal. RETgene,' diagnosis by rectal suction biopsy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man has painless bright-red bleeding from internal haemorrhoids above the pectinate line. Which artery primarily supplies this region. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Above pectinate line: superior rectal artery (IMA) and vein (portal) - internal haemorrhoids at 3, 7 and I l o'clock (lithotomy). Below: inferior rectal external haemorrhoids. vessels (internal pudendal)

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon explains the blood supply of haemorrhoids to students. Which arteries are classically associated with internal and external haemorrhoids, respectively? [HITEC 26]

options.A: Inferior rectal and superior rectal arteries
options.B: Middle rectal and superior rectal arteries
options.C: Superior rectal and inferior rectal arteries
options.D: Internal pudendal and middle rectal arteries

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Internal (above line, painless, portal venous) superior rectal," external (below line, painful, systemic) inferior rectal. The pectinate line is the portosystemic watershed.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man passes blood-stained stools and feels protrusions from his anus during defaecation; the doctor diagnoses internal haemorrhoids. Which veins are most likely involved? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Internal haemorrhoids = dilated tributaries of the superior rectal vein (internal rectal venous plexus) in the anal cushions," superior rectal vein drains into the IMV 4 portal system.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman has severe pain from an anal fissure below the pectinate line. Which nerve carries this pain. [Prof 24. LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Below the pectinate line: somatic innervation by the inferior rectal (anal) nerve, a branch of the pudendal nerve (S2-S4) 4 painful fissures, external haemorrhoids, abscesses. Above: visceral, insensitive to cutting.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man has a painful thrombosed external haemorrhoid at the anal margin. Which nerve carries the pain. [Prof 24. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: External haemorrhoids lie below the pectinate line, covered by anoderm supplied by the inferior rectal nerve 4 acutely painful when thrombosed.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a perianal operation, a patient has numbness around the anus and weak voluntary anal sphincter contraction. Which nerve has been injured? [LHR 25 . CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inferior rectal nerve: crosses the ischioanal fossa 4 external anal sphincter (motor) and perianal skin (sensory). Injury 4 faecal incontinence.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has a carcinoma at the rectosigmoid junction; the surgeon identifies where the rectum begins. At which vertebral level does the rectum begin. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rectum." begins at S3 (where the sigmoid mesocolon ends), -12 cm long, ends at the anorectaljunction 2-3 cm in front of the coccyx tip where puborectalis slings it.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During an anterior resection, the surgeon notes how much of the rectum is covered by peritoneum. Which part of the rectum is covered by peritoneum anteriorly and laterally. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Upper third - front and sides; middle third - front only; lower third - no peritoneum (below the rectovesical/rectouterine pouch).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During laparoscopic cholecystectomy the surgeon dissects the hepatocystic (Calot's) triangle to identify the cystic artery. Which structure forms the medial boundary of this triangle? [AMC 25]

options.D: Cystic artery inferior surface of liver. Content: cystic artery

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hepatocystic triangle." medial - common hepatic duct; inferior (lateral) - cystic duct; superior (from right hepatic). Calot's lymph node.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon reviews the borders of Calot's triangle before clipping structures. Which structure forms its inferior boundary? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked cystic artery. The cystic DUCT forms the inferior/lateral border," the cystic artery is the main content. "Critical view of safety" requires only two structures entering the gallbladder.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A medical historian notes that Calot's original description of the triangle differs from the modern hepatocystic triangle. In the original description, which structure formed the superior boundary. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Original Calot (1891) triangle: cystic duct, common hepatic duct and CYSTICARTERY (superior). The modern hepatocystic triangle replaces the artery with the inferior surface of the liver.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During cholecystectomy, the cystic artery is found within the triangle bounded by the ducts. Between which two ducts does the cystic artery usually run. [MUL 25]

options.A: Left hepatic artery and bile duct
options.B: Common hepatic duct and cystic duct
options.D: Common hepatic duct and right hepatic artery

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cystic artery usually arises from the right hepatic artery within Calot's triangle, behind the common hepatic duct; variations (anterior to CHD, from GDA) are common.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman has biliary colic and gallstones; cholecystectomy is planned. Which structure is most likely to be endangered during cholecystectomy? [KIMS 25 . KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Commonest serious injury: bile duct (misidentified as cystic duct). Right hepatic artery is also at risk. Prevent with the critical view of safety.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old man has progressive painless jaundice due to cancer at the porta hepatis. Which structure is compressed to cause the jaundice. [Prof 25 . MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Obstruction of the bile/hepatic ducts 4 conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia, pale stools, dark urine, pruritus. Courvoisier: palpable painless gallbladder + jaundice ￿ malignant distal obstruction.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has painless jaundice, weight loss and a palpable gallbladder from carcinoma of the head of the pancreas. Which structure is compressed? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The terminal bile duct runs in a groove on/through the posterior head of the pancreas ￿ early obstructive jaundice in head carcinoma. Body/tail tumours present late.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pancreatic carcinoma in the neck of the pancreas invades a major vessel lying directly behind it. Which vessel is formed behind the neck of the pancreas and is often invaded? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Portal vein forms behind the neck of the pancreas (L2) from the SMV and splenic vein; invasion of the portal/SMV confluence affects resectability.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has persistent jaundice beyond 2 weeks, pale stools and dark urine; the extrahepatic bile ducts are obliterated. What is the most likely diagnosis? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Biliary atresia: progressive obliteration of extrahepatic ducts 4 conjugated jaundice,. Kasai portoenterostomy before 60 days," commonest indication for paediatric liver transplant.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On CT a lobe of the liver is seen between the porta hepatis below and the inferior vena cava, bounded by the fissure for ligamentum venosum. Which lobe is this? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Caudate lobe: posterior, between IVC groove and fissure for ligamentum venosum, above the porta hepatis. Quadrate lobe: anterior, between gallbladder fossa and fissure for ligamentum teres.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: In Budd-chiari syndrome, one lobe of the liver hypertrophies while the rest atrophies because it drains independently. Into which vessel do the veins of the caudate lobe drain directly. [KIMS 26 . BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Caudate lobe (segment l) receives blood from both right and left portal/hepatic arteries and drains directly into the IVC via small veins 4 spared and hypertrophies in hepatic vein thrombosis." can be resected as a unit.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A liver surgeon plans a right hepatectomy along the functional division of the liver. Along which line is the liver divided into functional right and left lobes. [HITEC 25 . BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cantlie's line (middle hepatic vein plane) divides the liver into functional right and left halves of nearly equal size," Couinaud's 8 segments are based on portal and hepatic venous branching.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student describes the anatomical (morphological) division of the liver seen from the front. Which structure divides the liver anatomically into right and left lobes. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anatomical division." falciform ligament anteriorly, fissures for ligamentum teres and venosum on the visceral surface. Functional division." Cantlie's line.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist describes the hepatic unit centred on the portal triad and bounded by lines joining two central veins, with zones 1-3. What is this diamond-shaped functional unit? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rappaport acinus: zone I periportal (highest O,, gluconeogenesis), zone 3 centrilobular (lowest O,, CYP450 - first to suffer ischaemia and paracetamol toxicity). Classic lobule = hexagon around central vein." portal lobule = triangle around portal triad (bile drainage).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A liver biopsy in cirrhosis is examined under electron microscopy. What is the perisinusoidal space between hepatocytes and sinusoidal endothelium called? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Space of Disse." hepatocyte microvilli, plasma exchange, lymph formation," contains stellate (Ito) cells that store vitamin A and lay down collagen in cirrhosis. Space of Mall: between portal tract and limiting plate.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist studying fetal liver notes sinusoidal macrophages derived from the mesenchyme of the septum transversum. Which cells are these. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Liver." hepatocytes and bile duct epithelium from endoderm (hepatic diverticulum); Kupffer cells, haemopoietic cells, connective tissue and stellate cells from septum transversum mesoderm.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old alcoholic with cirrhosis vomits large amounts of blood from dilated veins at the lower end of the oesophagus. Which veins form this portosystemic anastomosis. [WMC 26. BWP 26 . LHR 25]

options.C: Left gastric vein and oesophageal veins of the azygos system

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Portosystemic sites: lower oesophagus (left gastric ￿ azygos), anal canal (superior ￿ middle/inferior rectal), umbilicus (paraumbilical H epigastric caput medusae), retroperitoneum (colic ￿ lumbar/renal), bare area of liver.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A radiologist traces the formation of the portal vein on CT. Which two veins unite to form the portal vein. [WMC 26]

options.A: Inferior mesenteric vein and hepatic vein
options.B: Splenic vein and inferior mesenteric vein
options.C: Superior mesenteric vein and hepatic vein
options.D: Splenic vein and superior mesenteric vein I

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Portal vein: SMV + splenic vein behind the neck of the pancreas (L2); IMV usually joins the splenic vein. Runs in the free edge of lesser omentum to the porta hepatis; carries 75% of liver blood flow.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with refractory portal hypertension undergoes a distal splenorenal (Warren) shunt. To which vein is the splenic vein connected? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Splenic vein runs behind the pancreas close to the left renal vein ￿ selective decompression of gastro-oesophageal varices while preserving portal flow to the liver.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: The coeliac trunk must be ligated during surgery for a tumour. Which organ is least likely to become ischaemic because of its rich alternative supply. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source records this answer as disputed. The pancreas also receives SMA supply (inferior pancreaticoduodenal) and arcades from the GDA: the liver also has portal venous flow and collaterals via the pancreaticoduodenal arcade.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a pancreaticoduodenectomy, the surgeon preserves an artery that supplies the pancreas from behind, arising near the coeliac/splenic origin. Which artery is this. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dorsal pancreatic artery (usually from the splenic artery near its origin) runs behind the neck and gives the transverse (inferior) pancreatic artery along the body and tail.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old chronic alcoholic has severe epigastric pain radiating to the back; MRI shows atrophy and calcif ication of the pancreatic tail. Which artery running along the pancreas is at risk of damage (pseudoaneurysm/thrombosis)? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Splenic artery runs tortuously along the upper border of the body and tail: pancreatitis causes splenic artery pseudoaneurysm and splenic vein thrombosis (sinistral portal hypertension, isolated gastric varices).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon mobilises the stomach and notes the course of the splenic artery. In which relation to the stomach does the splenic artery run. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Splenic artery runs to the left behind the stomach (posterior wall of lesser sac) along the upper border of the pancreas, then in the splenorenal ligament to the hilum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A motorcyclist fractures his left 9th-12th ribs and becomes hypotensive from intra-abdominal bleeding. Which artery may need ligation to control the bleeding. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spleen lies under the left 9th-1 Ith ribs. long axis along the 10th rib; lower left rib fractures 4 splenic rupture. Kehr's sign = left shoulder pain from diaphragmatic irritation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student studies pancreatic development. Which part of the adult pancreas is formed by the ventral pancreatic bud? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ventral bud (with bile duct) rotates behind the duodenum 4 uncinate process + inferior head + proximal main duct (Wirsung). Dorsal bud 4 upper head, neck, body, tail + accessory duct (Santorini).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old child has vomiting and upper abdominal pain; MRI shows a ring of pancreatic tissue completely encircling and compressing the second part of the duodenum. Which developmental error causes this. [KIMS 25. KIMS 26. CKMC 26. QIMS 25. HITEC 25]

options.C: Abnormal migration (failure of proper rotation) of a bifid ventral pancreatic bud
options.D: Persistence of the dorsal bud only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Annular pancreas: bifid ventral bud migrates in opposite directions around the duodenum 4 ring around the 2nd part 4 duodenal obstruction (double bubble), associated with Down syndrome," may obstruct pancreatic and bile flow.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old has gallstone ileus; imaging shows air in the biliary tree and a fistula between the gallbladder and adjacent bowel. Into which part of the gut does a gallstone most commonly erode. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked transverse colon. Commonest fistula is cholecystoduodenal; the stone then impacts at the narrowest part - the terminal ileum (Rigler's triad: pneumobilia, obstruction, ectopic stone).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man with renal colic passes a ureteric stone after it was held up where the ureter enters the bladder wall. At which site do ureteric stones most commonly lodge? [Prof 24. KIMS 26]

options.D: Ureterovesical junction / commonest impaction site). A

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ureteric constrictions: pelvi-ureteric junction. pelvic brim (crossing iliac vessels), ureterovesicaljunction (narrowest lower ureteric stone causes strangury and pain referred to the tip of the penis/labia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old office worker has sudden left loin pain radiating to the groin; IVU shows a stone in the upper ureter at its first narrowing. Where is the first site of ureteric constriction. [CKMC 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: First constriction = pelvi-ureteric junction (LI/L2), second = pelvic brim at the bifurcation of the common iliac artery, third = intramural (vesicoureteric) part.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with renal colic has a 4-mm ureteric stone. Considering the normal ureteric constrictions, where is the stone LEAST likely to be found? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stones lodge at the three natural narrowings; the middle (lumbar) ureter between PUJ and pelvic brim is relatively wide.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with renal colic has pain radiating from the flank to the groin. Which splanchnic nerves carry the sympathetic (and pain afferent) supply to the kidney. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Kidney: renal plexus from lesser (TIO-TII) and least (T12) splanchnic nerves + Ll. Pain referred to TIO-LI dermatomes - loin to groin.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with ureteric colic also has pain in the scrotum and upper anterior thigh. Irritation of which nerve explains the scrotal pain? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Genitofemoral nerve (Ll-L2) lies on psoas just behind the ureter; its genital branch supplies the scrotum/labium and cremaster - explains testicular pain in ureteric colic.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A renal biopsy shows tubules lined by cuboidal cells with a prominent brush border of long microvilli and eosinophilic cytoplasm. Which part of the nephron is this. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCT: tall cuboidal. eosinophilic (many mitochondria). brush border, indistinct cell boundaries, small lumen; reabsorbs ~65% of filtrate. DCT: lower cells. no brush border, wider lumen, more nuclei per section.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A researcher examines a nephron segment lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with abundant microvilli forming a brush border. Which function is primarily associated with this feature. [QIMS 25]

options.D: Active reabsorption of nutrients and ions

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Brush border increases surface area for reabsorption of glucose. amino acids. Na., HCO3 and phosphate in the PCT (with abundant basal mitochondria for Na'/K'_A TPase).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A kidney section shows cortical tubules lined by low cuboidal cells without a brush border, with closely packed, deeply staining nuclei and a wide lumen. Which segment is most likely being observed? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DCT cells are smaller and paler-staining than PCT, so more nuclei appear per cross-section; where the DCT touches its own glomerulus the cells become tall and crowded = macula densa.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A renal biopsy in a child with heavy proteinuria shows effacement of the cells that envelop glomerular capillaries with foot processes. Podocytes form which layer of Bowman's capsule? [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Filtration barrier: fenestrated endothelium ￿ GBM (type IV collagen, heparan sulphate) ￿ podocyte filtration slits (nephrin). Parietal layer = simple squamous epithelium.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A kidney section shows modified smooth muscle cells with secretory granules in the wall of the afferent arteriole close to the glomerulus. Which cells secrete renin? [MUL 26. WMC 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: JG apparatus: JG cells (renin," baroreceptors, Fl stimulation), macula densa (Nacl sensor in DCT), extraglomerular mesangial (lacis) cells.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An immunohistochemistry stain for aquaporin-2 lights up one segment of a kidney section. Which part of the kidney does it identify? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AQP2 is in the apical membrane/vesicles of principal cells of the collecting duct (ADH-regulated). AQPI is constitutive in PCT and thin descending limb.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A urologist explains the urothelium in a bladder biopsy, which has umbrella cells with rigid apical membrane plaques. In which epithelium do these uroplakin plaques accumulate. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Umbrella cells contain uroplakin plaques that fold into vesicles when the bladder empties and flatten when it fills 4 impermeable barrier to urine.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A slide of a tubular organ shows a star-shaped lumen lined by multilayered epithelium whose surface cells are dome-shaped. Which epithelium lines the ureter. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ureter: transitional epithelium (urothelium), star~shaped lumen, 2 muscle layers (inner longitudinal, outer circular) in upper 2/3 and an extra outer longitudinal layer in the lower third.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During nephrectomy, the surgeon identifies the structures at the renal hilum from front to back. What is the anterior-to-posterior arrangement? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hilum from front: Vein, Artery, Pelvis (VAP) - "Very Annoying Patient"; a posterior branch of the renal artery often passes behind the pelvis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A CT of a thin patient shows the posterior surface of the kidney lying on muscles of the posterior abdominal wall. Which group forms the posterior relations of the kidney. [CKMC 26]

options.B: Psoas major, quadratus lumborum and transversus abdominis

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior relations." diaphragm (12th rib above). psoas major. quadratus lumborum, transversus abdominis, subcostal vessels and nerve, iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon exploring the right kidney anteriorly sees organs covering it. Which structures are anterior relations of the right kidney. [HITEC 25]

options.A: Liver, second part of duodenum and hepatic flexure of colon
