mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Right kidney anterior: right suprarenal, liver, 2nd part of duodenum, hepatic flexure, small intestine. Left kidney anterior: suprarenal, stomach, spleen, pancreas tail, splenic flexure, jejunum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient develops bleeding into the perirenal space after a renal biopsy. In which direction can the blood track within the renal fascia. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Renal (Gerota's) fascia is fused superiorly and laterally but is open inferiorly around the ureter 4 perirenal blood/pus tracks down toward the iliac fossa and pelvis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A renal abscess ruptures into the perirenal space and pus later appears in the right iliac fossa. Which loose attachment allows this spread? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The anterior and posterior layers of renal fascia do not fuse inferiorly; they loosely surround the ureter 4 downward tracking of fluid along the ureter.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A thin woman has a kidney that descends markedly on standing (seen on X~ray in sitting posture), but the ureter is not kinked. What is the most likely cause. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nephroptosis ( floating kidney"): loss of supporting perirenal and pararenal fat in thin/cachectic women; physiological descent of up to 2.5 cm on respiration is normal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man with a left renal tumour develops a left varicocele that does not empty on lying down. Which anatomical relationship explains this. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Left renal vein passes anterior to the aorta and receives the left
options.B: Left renal vein passes behind the IVC testicular vein
options.C: Left renal artery lies anterior to the renal vein
options.D: Left renal vein drains into the portal vein

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Left testicular vein drains at a right angle into the left renal vein (which crosses in front of the aorta below the SMA); tumour thrombus or nutcracker compression 4 left varicocele.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a right nephrectomy, bleeding occurs from the short vein draining the right suprarenal gland. Into which vessel does the right suprarenal vein drain directly. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Right suprarenal and right gonadal veins drain directly into the IVC,. left suprarenal and left gonadal veins drain into the left renal vein.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist reviews pelvic anatomy before a colposcopy; the left ureter at the pelvic brim lies under a peritoneal fold. Which structure crosses the left ureter at the pelvic brim? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Left ureter lies under the apex of the inverted-v root of the sigmoid mesocolon at the bifurcation of the common iliac artery - a guide to finding it in left colectomy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Embryology: the permanent kidney forms after the pronephros and mesonephros regress. From which embryological structure is the functional tissue of the adult kidney derived? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Metanephros (week 5): ureteric bud (from mesonephric duct) 4 collecting system," metanephric blastema (intermediate mesoderm) 4 nephrons. The pronephros never functions in humans.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student asks which part of the metanephros gives rise to the nephron itself. From which structure do nephrons develop. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Each collecting tubule induces a metanephric cap 4 renal vesicle 4 S-shaped tubule 4 Bowman's capsule, PCT, loop of Henle, DCT. Ureteric bud ureter, pelvis, calyces, collecting ducts.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A stillborn baby has bilateral absent kidneys. The pathologist explains that the ureteric bud failed to reach its target. What is the embryological cause of renal agenesis. [AMC 25]

options.A: Failure of ureteric bud to induce/penetrate the metanephric tissue

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Renal agenesis: ureteric bud fails to develop or degenerates ￿ no induction of the metanephric blastema. Bilateral 4 olffgohydramnios 4 Potter sequence (incompatible with life).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A prenatal ultrasound shows oligohydramnios, absent fetal kidneys and a small chest. Which malformation causes this Potter sequence. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fetal urine is the main source of amniotic fluid after 16 weeks," no urine 4 oligohydramnios 4 compression: flattened (Potter) facies, limb deformities and pulmonary hypoplasia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has respiratory distress, flattened facies and limb deformities; the mother had oligohydramnios throughout pregnancy. Which feature is part of Potter syndrome and causes death? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Potter sequence: Pulmonary hypoplasia. Oligohydramnios, Twisted (club) feet, Typical facies, Extremity defects, Renal failure (portER). Lung hypoplasia is the cause of death.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An IVU in a child shows two ureters draining one kidney on the left. Duplication of the ureter results from which developmental event? [MUL 26. MUL 25]

options.A: Premature (early) division of the ureteric bud
options.C: Failure of the metanephric blastema to form
options.D: Failure of the mesonephric duct to develop

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bifid ureter: early splitting of the ureteric bud. Complete duplication: two separate buds: the ureter from the upper pole opens lower and medially (Weigert-meyer rule) and may be ectopic.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ultrasound shows both kidneys fused at their lower poles in front of the aorta, lying lower than normal. Which vessel prevents the ascent of this horseshoe kidney? [AMC 25. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Horseshoe kidney (l in 400, common in Turner syndrome): lower poles fuse," ascent is arrested by the root of the IMA. Higher risk of obstruction, infection, stones and Wilms tumour.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student is asked about the origin of the urinary bladder lining. From which germ layer is the epithelium of most of the urinary bladder derived? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bladder epithelium = endoderm of the vesical part of the urogenital sinus; the trigone is initially mesodermal (incorporated mesonephric ducts) but later covered by endoderm.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A bullet injury damages a structure that developed as an outgrowth of the mesonephric duct. Which urinary structure develops from the mesonephric duct (as the ureteric bud)? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ureteric bud arises from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct near the cloaca 4 ureter. pelvis. calyces and collecting ducts.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 35-week aborted fetus has an organ that, on histology, shows a very large cortex and a small medulla. Which organ is this. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fetal adrenal is very large with a thick fetal zone that produces DHEA-S (for placental oestriol); the fetal zone involutes after birth.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with retrograde ejaculation after retroperitoneal surgery is found to have damage to sympathetic nerves supplying the bladder neck. Which nerves carry sympathetic fibres to the urinary bladder. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bladder." sympathetic - TI I-L2 via lumbar splanchnic nerves and superior/inferior hypogastric plexuses (contract internal sphincter, relax detrusor)," parasympathetic - pelvic splanchnic S2-S4 (detrusor contraction)," somatic pudendal (external sphincter).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man ruptures the ligament that supports the urinary bladder and urethra anteriorly in a pelvic fracture. Which ligament is involved? [KIMS 25. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Puboprostatic (pubovesical in females) ligaments anchor the bladder neck and prostate to the pubis; their rupture in pelvic fractures allows the prostate to ride high ( floating prostate" on DRE).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During pelvimetry in a primigravida, the obstetrician assesses the inlet diameter running from the sacroiliac joint to the opposite iliopubic eminence. Which diameter is this? [Prof 24]

options.D: Oblique diameter of the pelvic inlet

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inlet diameters: AP (true conjugate 11 cm), oblique (12 cm - engagement usually in the oblique), transverse (13 cm, widest). Outlet: AP widest (coccyx moves back).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An obstetrician measures the distance from the sacral promontory to the lower border of the pubic symphysis on vaginal examination. Which conjugate is being measured? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Diagonal conjugate (12.5 cm) is clinically measurable; obstetric conjugate ~ diagonal - 1.5 cm (- 11 cm) = shortest AP diameter through which the head must pass.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A forensic expert examines a pelvis with a heart-shaped inlet, narrow subpubic angle and prominent ischial spines. Which sex is indicated? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Male (android).. heavy, heart-shaped inlet, subpubic angle ~60° (V), narrow outlet, inverted ischial tuberosities. Female (gynaecoid)." oval inlet, subpubic angle 80-90° (U), wider outlet.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A radiologist notes a wide subpubic angle and a large distance between the ischial tuberosities. Which feature is characteristic of the female pelvis. [CKMC 26]

options.C: Wider subpubic angle and greater intertuberous distance

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Female pelvis is adapted for childbirth: wider and shallower, round/oval inlet, everted ischial tuberosities, larger outlet, wider greater sciatic notch.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 36-week primigravida has a normal pelvis on pelvimetry with an oval inlet favourable for vaginal delivery. Which pelvic type is most likely. [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Caldwell-moloy." gynaecoid (50%, ideal), anthropoid (AP oval - occipitoposterior), android (heart-shaped - deep transverse arrest), platypelloid (flat rarest).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman with a coccygeal fracture after a fall asks how it affects her delivery. Which structure forms the posterior boundary of the pelvic outlet? [CKMC 26. LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Outlet (diamond): anterior lower border of pubic symphysis; anterolateral - ischiopubic rami; lateral ischial tuberosities; posterolateral sacrotuberous ligaments; posterior - tip of coccyx.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient fractures the ischial tuberosity; the surgeon reviews the boundaries of the pelvic outlet. Which structure forms the posterolateral boundary of the pelvic outlet? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sacrotuberous ligament runs from the sacrum/coccyx to the ischial tuberosity and forms the posterolateral boundary of the outlet and perineum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An anatomy demonstrator traces the pelvic brim on a skeleton. Which structure forms part of the posterior boundary of the pelvic brim. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pelvic brim: sacral promontory and ala of sacrum (posterior). arcuate and pectineal lines (lateral), pubic crest and upper border of symphysis (anterior).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a road traff ic accident, an X-ray shows a f racture of the ala of the sacrum with weakness and numbness in the leg. Which structure is most likely damaged? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sacral plexus lies on piriformis in front of the sacrum; the lumbosacral trunk (L4-L5) crosses the ala of the sacrum - vulnerable in sacral fractures and during labour (foot drop).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During diff icult labour a woman develops foot drop from compression of a nerve trunk crossing the pelvic brim. Near which structure does the lumbosacral trunk cross the pelvic brim? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lumbosacral trunk (L4 + L5) descends over the ala of the sacrum close to the sacroiliac joint to join the sacral plexus; compression by the fetal head L4/L5 deficits.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A lumbar spine X-ray shows the fifth lumbar vertebra fused with the sacrum on one side. What is this called? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sacralisation: L5 fused (partly/completely) with sacrum; lumbarisation: Sl separate, functioning as a 6th lumbar vertebra. Both alter vertebral counting before surgery.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A radiologist identifies an isolated vertebra with a large kidney~shaped body, thick transverse processes and mammillary processes but no costal facets. To which region does it belong. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lumbar: massive kidney-shaped body, no foramina transversaria or costal facets, mammillary and accessory processes, short quadrangular spine. L5 has the largest transverse processes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A stab wound in the buttock just above the piriformis causes weakness of hip abduction (Trendelenburg sign). Which structure was damaged? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Above piriformis (greater sciatic foramen)." superior gluteal nerve and vessels. Below piriformis: sciatic. inferior gluteal. posterior femoral cutaneous, pudendal nerves, nerve to obturator internus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An anatomy student identifies the components of the levator ani during dissection. Which muscle is NOT part of the levator ani. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Levator ani = puborectalis + pubococcygeus + iliococcygeus (nerve." S4 + pudendal branches). Coccygeus completes the pelvic diaphragm posteriorly but is a separate muscle.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a perineal injury, a patient loses the anorectal angle and becomes incontinent of faeces. Which muscle plays the major role in maintaining the anorectal angle. [AMC 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Puborectalis forms a U-shaped sling around the anorectal junction, pulling it forward (-80° angle); it relaxes during defaecation to straighten the angle.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist explains the active (muscular) support of the pelvic organs to a patient with prolapse. Which structure provides the major muscular support to the uterus and pelvic viscera. [CKMC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Supports of uterus: muscular - levator ani and perineal body (most important active support): ligamentous - cardinal (Mackenrodt), uterosacral, pubocervical. Broad and round ligaments give little support.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a pelvic lymph node dissection, the surgeon identifies an artery passing along the lateral pelvic wall to an opening covered by a membrane. Which artery passes through the obturator canal? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Obturator artery (anterior division of internal iliac) runs on the lateral pelvic wall to the obturator canal at the upper part of the obturator foramen; an abnormal obturator artery from the inferior epigastric may cross the femoral ring.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a transvaginal pudendal nerve block in labour, the obstetrician palpates a bony landmark. Which landmark is palpated? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pudendal nerve crosses the sacrospinous ligament just medial to the ischial spine; local anaesthetic infiltrated there anaesthetises most of the perineum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An anatomist traces a nerve that leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, hooks around the ischial spine and re-enters through the lesser sciatic foramen. Which nerve is this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pudendal nerve (S2-S4) + internal pudendal vessels and nerve to obturator internus pass out through the greater and back in through the lesser sciatic foramen into the pudendal (Alcock's) canal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient is brought after a road traffic accident with fractures near the right sacroiliac joint and sacrum. Which pelvic structure lying immediately in front of the sacrum is likely to be damaged? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The rectum follows the concavity of the sacrum and coccyx (S3 downward)," the prostate and seminal vesicles lie anterior to the rectum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old infertile man has normal testosterone but azoospermia; a defect in the cells forming the blood-testis barrier is suspected. Which cells form this barrier? [Prof 24. WMC 26]

options.A: Adjacent Sertoli cells joined by tight junctions

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tight junctions between adjacent Sertoli cells divide the seminiferous epithelium into basal (spermatogonia) and adluminal compartments, protecting meiotic/haploid cells from autoimmunity.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A testicular biopsy shows tall columnar cells extending from the basement membrane to the lumen, enveloping developing germ cells. Which cells nourish and support developing spermatozoa. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sertoli cells: nourish germ cells. phagocytose residual bodies, secrete ABP, inhibin B, AMH. tubular fluid; FSH acts on them. Leydig cells (interstitium) make testosterone under LH.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An infertile man has low testosterone with low LH on testing. Which hormone stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: LH 4 Leydig cells (CAMP 4 cholesterol side-chain cleavage) 4 testosterone; FSH 4 Sertoli cells (ABP, inhibin). Testosterone feeds back on LH: inhibin on FSH.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student studying gonadal development traces the origin of the supporting cells of the seminiferous cords. From which embryological tissue are Sertoli cells derived? [AMC 26]

options.C: Surface (coelomic) epithelium of the gonadal ridge

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sertoli cells come from the proliferating coelomic epithelium of the gonadal ridge (primitive sex cords); primordial germ cells migrate from the yolk sac wall (endoderm).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histologist asks where the interstitial cells of the testis originate. From which embryological structure do Leydig cells develop. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Leydig cells develop from mesenchyme of the gonadal ridge between the testis cords (week 8) and secrete testosterone under placental hCG.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: In an infant with persistent Mullerian duct syndrome, a uterus and tubes are found in a phenotypic male. Which cells normally secrete anti-mullerian hormone. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AMH (Mullerian inhibiting substance) from fetal Sertoli cells causes regression of the paramesonephric ducts; testosterone from Leydig cells maintains the mesonephric ducts.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student studies testicular development. From which structures is the rete testis formed? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Testis cords (medullary) ￿ seminiferous tubules, tubuli recti and rete testis," efferent ductules come from mesonephric tubules. Cortical cords form in the female (follicles).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Genetic testing in a 46,XX phenotypic male shows translocation of a gene from the short arm of the Y chromosome. Which gene determines male sex. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SRY (testis-determining factor) on Ypll triggers Sertoli cell differentiation 4 testis formation," without it the gonad becomes an ovary.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 2~year-old boy has an empty right scrotum; the testis is felt along its normal path of descent. What is the most common site of an undescended testis. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Undescended testis lies along the normal path (abdomen ￿ inguinal canal 4 superficial ring): commonest site is the inguinal canal. Ectopic testis lies off the path (perineum, femoral, pubopenile). Orchidopexy by 12- 18 months.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 6-month-old boy is brought with an undescended testis. Which developmental process is defective. [QIMS 25]

options.C: Descent of the testis through the inguinal canal (gubernaculum
options.D: Formation of the processus vaginalis guidance)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Testicular descent." transabdominal phase (INSL3. gubernaculum) then inguinoscrotal phase (androgens, genitofemoral nerve) during the 7th- 9th months; incomplete descent = cryptorchidism.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old man undergoes surgical sterilisation through a small scrotal incision. Which structure is divided during vasectomy. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vas deferens is palpable in the spermatic cord as a firm cord: dividing it stops sperm but semen volume is almost unchanged (seminal vesicles and prostate provide -95¥0 .

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A bullet passes through the lower half of the inguinal ligament and damages a structure in the spermatic cord that developed f rom the mesonephric duct. Which structure is involved? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mesonephric duct derivatives in the male: epididymis (duct), ductus deferens, seminal vesicle, ejaculatory duct (+ ureter, pelvis, collecting ducts via ureteric bud).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Electron microscopy of a tubule lined by pseudostratified columnar cells shows very long, non-motile microvilli projecting into a lumen full of sperm. In which organ are these stereocilia found? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stereocilia (long microvilli) on principal cells of the epididymis and ductus deferens absorb fluid and secrete glycerophosphocholine," sperm acquire motility in the epididymis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Semen analysis in an infertile man shows absent fructose and low volume. Which gland normally contributes fructose~rich fluid to semen. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Seminal vesicles: _60-70% of volume - fructose (sperm energy), prostaglandins, semenogelin (coagulation). Prostate: citrate, zinc, acid phosphatase, PSA (liquefaction).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A prostate biopsy shows concentric lamellated eosinophilic bodies in the gland lumina, increasing with age. In which gland are corpora amylacea characteristically seen. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Corpora amylacea: condensed prostatic secretion, may calcify (prostatic calculi). Prostate also shows tubuloalveolar glands with papillary infoldings and fibromuscular stroma.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man with urinary hesitancy has benign prostatic hyperplasia. From which zone of the prostate does BPH arise. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: BPH - transitional (periurethral) zone 4 urethral obstruction early. Carcinoma - peripheral zone (70%) 4 palpable posteriorly on DRE, late urinary symptoms.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man with BPH undergoes TURP; the surgeon removes the enlarged part projecting into the bladder neck. Which anatomical lobe is classically responsible for urethral obstruction in BPH? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Median lobe lies between the urethra and ejaculatory ducts; its hypertrophy raises the uvula vesicae and obstructs the internal urethral orifice. Lateral lobes also enlarge in BPH.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A urologist performing TURP identifies the elevation on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra as a landmark, staying above it to protect the external sphincter. Which landmark is this. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The verumontanum marks the distal limit of TURP resection; the external urethral sphincter lies just distal to it. The utricle and ejaculatory ducts open on its summit.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student studies the internal features of the prostatic urethra. Where do the numerous prostatic ducts open. [CKMC 25]

options.C: Prostatic sinuses on either side of the urethral crest

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prostatic ducts open into the prostatic sinuses (grooves beside the urethral crest): the utricle (Mullerian remnant) and two ejaculatory ducts open on the seminal colliculus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student is asked the origin of the prostatic urethra lining. From which tissue does the prostatic urethra develop. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prostatic and membranous urethra = pelvic part of the urogenital sinus (endoderm); prostate glands bud from this endoderm. Distal glandular urethra (navicular fossa) is ectodermal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On digital rectal examination of a man, a firm, rubbery organ with a central sulcus is felt anteriorly. Which organ is this. [CKMC 26. MUL 25 . LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DRE - male: prostate (most prominent), seminal vesicles (if enlarged), bladder base; female: cervix and posterior vaginal wall. Laterally: ischioanal fossae." posteriorly: coccyx.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man has a dragging scrotal ache and a "bag of worms above the left testis that empties on lying down. Dilatation of which structure causes this. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Varicocele (left in 90A): pampiniform plexus drains via the left testicular vein into the left renal vein at a right angle without a valve. Sudden right varicocele 4 suspect IVC/renal tumour.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for testicular cancer, a surgeon traces the testicular artery upward. From which vessel does the testicular artery arise. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gonadal arteries arise from the anterior abdominal aorta at L2 (testis develops in the lumbar region); testicular tumours spread first to para-aortic nodes at LI-L2.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has loss of sensation over the lateral side of the scrotum after a groin and thigh operation. Which nerves supply the anterolateral scrotal skin. [CKMC 25]

options.A: Perineal branch of posterior femoral cutaneous only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Scrotum." anterior - ilioinguinal + genital branch of genitofemoral (Ll): posterior - perineal branches of pudendal (S3) and posterior femoral cutaneous (S2).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man had radical prostatectomy for carcinoma; a year later he has back pain and lumbar vertebral metastases without lung involvement. Through which venous route did the cancer most likely reach the vertebrae. [KIMS 25. HITEC 25]

options.C: Prostatic venous plexus ￿ valveless vertebral (Batson's) plexus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prostatic venous plexus communicates with the valveless internal vertebral venous plexus (Batson); raised intra-abdominal pressure drives blood (and tumour cells) to the vertebrae ￿ osteoblastic metastases.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn with a 46,XX karyotype has ambiguous genitalia with clitoromegaly and fused labioscrotal folds. What is the most likely cause. [AMC 25]

options.A: Increased androgen production from the fetal adrenal (congenital

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CAH (21-hydroxylase deficiency).. I cortisol 4 t ACTH 4 excess adrenal androgens 4 virilised 46,XX female with normal internal female organs,. salt-wasting in severe forms.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn boy has the urethral opening on the dorsal (upper) surface of the penis, often with bladder exstrophy. What is the developmental basis of this epispadias. [AMC 25]

options.A: Failure of closure of the urethral folds
options.B: Abnormal (more caudal) position of the genital tubercle

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note: the source key marked failure of urethral folds - that causes HYPOSPADIAS (ventral opening). Epispadias results from the genital tubercle forming in the region of the urorectal septum, so the urogenital sinus opens on the dorsal surface; associated with exstrophy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 24-year-old infertile woman is found to have two separate uterine cavities and two cervices because the paramesonephric ducts failed to fuse completely. What is this condition. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mullerian anomalies." didelphys - complete failure of fvsion (2 uteri, 2 cervices + double vagina); bicornuate - partial fusion failure (heart-shaped. one cervix); septate - failure of septum resorption: unicornuate one duct fails to develop.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Imaging in a woman with recurrent miscarriages shows a heart-shaped uterus with two horns and a single cervix. Which condition is this and what is the defect? [HITEC 26. QIMS 25]

options.B: Bicornuate uterus - incomplete fusion of the paramesonephric ducts
options.D: Septate uterus - failure of septal resorption

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bicornuate uterus: partial failure of fusion of the upper paramesonephric ducts," external fundal cleft (distinguishes it from septate uterus on MR1/3D ultrasound).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old girl has primary amenorrhoea with normal breasts and pubic hair; the uterus and upper two-thirds of the vagina are absent. Which embryological defect is responsible. [AMC 26]

options.C: Agenesis of the paramesonephric ducts (MRKH syndrome)
options.D: Failure of fusion of the ureteric buds

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser: Mullerian agenesis, 46,XX. normal ovaries (so normal secondary sex characters); lower vagina (from urogenital sinus) present as a short blind pouch.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student lists derivatives of the paramesonephric ducts. From which ducts do the uterine tubes develop. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Paramesonephric ducts." cranial unfused parts 4 uterine tubes; fused caudal parts ￿ uterus, cervix and upper vagina (uterovaginal primordium).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student asks about the origin of the vaginal fornices. From which structure are the vaginal fornices derived? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Upper vagina including the fornices (around the cervix) = uterovaginal primordium (Mullerian); lower vagina = vaginal plate from sinovaginal bulbs (urogenital sinus).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student studies formation of the vagina. What do the sinovaginal bulbs give rise to. [MUL 25]

options.B: Vaginal plate 4 lower part of the vagina

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sinovaginal bulbs (from urogenital sinus) proliferate to form the solid vaginal plate, which canalises by month 5," the hymen separates the vaginal lumen from the sinus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student studies female external genital development. From which structures do the labia minora develop. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Female: genital tubercle 4 clitoris," urethral folds 4 labia minora: labioscrotal swellings 4 labia majora. Male: urethral folds 4 penile urethra; swellings ￿ scrotum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman has a tubal ectopic pregnancy; the surgeon ligates vessels supplying the tube. From which arteries does the fallopian tube receive its blood supply? [LHR 26 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uterine tube: lateral 2/3 - ovarian artery," medial 1/3 - uterine artery (anastomosing in the mesosalpinx). Ovary." ovarian artery mainly.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman with an ectopic pregnancy in the middle/lateral part of the uterine tube has ligation of the artery supplying that segment. Which artery supplies the middle and lateral part of the uterine tube. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ovarian artery (from aorta at L2) runs in the suspensory ligament and mesosalpinx to supply the ovary and lateral tube; the uterine artery supplies the medial tube and uterus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman has severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding; ultrasound shows a tubal ectopic pregnancy. What is the most common site of ectopic pregnancy. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ampulla -75-800A," isthmus- 12A0 (ruptures early)," interstitial (cornual) rupture causes massive bleeding. Risk factors: PID, previous tubal surgery, IUCD, IVF.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist explains to a patient with an ampullary ectopic pregnancy why this site is most often involved. Which feature of the ampulla is responsible. [QIMS 25]

options.B: It opens directly into the uterine cavity
options.C: It is the narrowest part of the tube
options.D: It is the longest, widest and most tortuous part, where fertilisation occurs

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fertilisation occurs in the ampulla," damaged cilia/mucosal folds (after salpingitis) delay transport so the blastocyst implants there.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide of an organ shows simple columnar epithelium with ciliated cells and non-ciliated secretory "peg" cells. Which organ is this. [KIMS 26. KIMS 25 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uterine tube: highly folded mucosa (ampulla), ciliated cells (beat toward uterus) and peg cells (nutritive secretion). Vagina - stratified squamous; endometrium - simple columnar with glands.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A uterine tube biopsy shows ciliated and non-ciliated columnar cells. What is the functional significance of the ciliated cells. [QIMS 25]

options.D: Propel the ovum toward the uterus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ciliary beating (increased by oestrogen) plus peristalsis moves the ovum/zygote toward the uterus in -3-4 days," immotile cilia (Kartagener) infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An ovarian section shows a follicle with multiple layers of granulosa cells and fluid-filled spaces forming an antrum. What type of follicle is this. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primordial: single layer of flat cells; primary." cuboidal granulosa + zona pellucida," secondary/antral: antrum with liquor folliculi, theca interna/externa; Graafian: mature with cumulus oophorus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An endometrial biopsy shows coiled glands with saw-toothed lumens containing secretion and oedematous stroma. In which phase of the menstrual cycle is this endometrium. [MUL 26. AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Secretory phase (progesterone): tortuous. saw-tooth glands. subnuclear then supranuclear glycogen vacuoles, stromal oedema, spiral arteries. Proliferative phase (oestrogen): straight tubular glands with mitoses.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A colposcopy shows the junction where the epithelium of the ectocervix meets the endocervical canal. What change in epithelium occurs at this transformation zone. [WMC 25]

options.D: Stratified squamous non-keratinised ￿ simple columnar mucus~secreting

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vagina and ectocervix: non-keratinised stratified squamous; endocervix." simple columnar mucus-secreting. The transformation zone is the site of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (HPV).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman has a Pap smear taken from the area most prone to cervical cancer. Where is the squamocolumnar junction (transformation zone) usually located in adult women. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note: the source key marked "internal os" The squamocolumnar junction lies at or near the EXTERNAL os (moves out in puberty/pregnancy/OCP use, recedes into the canal after menopause).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology question: the lining of the endocervix and stomach produces mucus. Which type of epithelium typically secretes mucus. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mucus-secreting simple columnar epithelium lines the stomach (surface mucous cells) and endocervix," goblet cells are scattered in intestinal columnar epithelium.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide shows simple columnar ciliated epithelium in a female reproductive organ. Where is this epithelium found? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ciliated simple columnar." uterine tube (and endometrium partly), bronchioles, ependyma. Ductus deferens." pseudostratified columnar with stereocilia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist demonstrates the peritoneal fold extending from the lateral margins of the uterus to the lateral pelvic walls. Which ligament is this: [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Broad ligament: double fold of peritoneum - mesosalpinx (tube), mesovarium (ovary), mesometrium," contains uterine vessels, ureter at its base, round and ovarian ligaments.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Which peritoneal fold attaches the ovary to the posterior layer of the broad ligament? Choose the correct structure. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mesovarium carries vessels to the hilum; suspensory (infundibulopelvic) ligament carries the ovarian vessels from the pelvic wall,. ligament of ovary joins ovary to uterine cornu.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During oophorectomy, the surgeon clamps the peritoneal fold running from the lateral pelvic wall to the ovary to secure its main artery. In which structure does the ovarian artery run. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Infundibulopelvic ligament contains ovarian artery, vein, lymphatics and nerves: the ureter lies close to it at the pelvic brim - risk during ligation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old multipara with uterine prolapse is told that a particular ligament is the main passive support of the cervix. Which ligament mainly supports the cervix and upper vagina. [CKMC 26. MUL 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cardinal (Mackenrodt's) ligaments." condensations of pelvic fascia from cervix/upper vagina to lateral pelvic wall; with uterosacral and pubocervical ligaments they form the main passive support.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman has descent of the cervix into the vagina after multiple vaginal deliveries. Weakness of which ligaments causes cervical prolapse. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Level I support (DeLancey): cardinal-uterosacral complex suspends the cervix/vault; its failure 4 uterine/vault prolapse.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old multipara feels lower abdominal heaviness and a mass protrudes from the vagina when she lifts heavy weights. What is the diagnosis? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uterovaginal prolapse: risk factors - multiparity, prolonged labour, menopause (oestrogen loss), chronic cough, obesity; graded by descent relative to the hymen.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A radiologist doing a hysterosalpingogram notes the normal position of the uterus. What is the most common position of the uterus? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked anteverted-retroflexed. Normal uterus is ANTEVER TED (cervix-vagina angle - 90°) and ANTEFLEXED (body-cervix angle ~170°); _15-20% are retroverted.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During hysterectomy, the surgeon ligates the uterine artery and must protect a structure passing beneath it about 2 cm lateral to the cervix. Which structure must be preserved? [AMC 26. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: "Water under the bridge": the ureter passes BELOW the uterine artery at the base of the broad ligament-2 cm lateral to the supravaginal cervix - commonest site of iatrogenic ureteric injury.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a hysterectomy, a clamp is placed on the cardinal ligament near the lateral pelvic wall. Which structure is most likely to be damaged? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The ureter runs through the cardinal ligament (ureteric tunnel) beneath the uterine artery; clamping too laterally or low on the cardinal ligament risks ureteric ligation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student describes the relationship of the ureter and uterine artery in the base of the broad ligament. How does the ureter pass in relation to the uterine artery? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ureter passes under (posteroinferior to) the uterine artery, then anteromedially to the bladder near the lateral fornix - palpable through the lateral fornix.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During laparoscopy, a gynaecologist examines the ovarian fossa on the lateral pelvic wall. Which artery forms its posterior boundary (with the ureter)? [KIMS 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ovarian fossa: anterior - obliterated umbilical artery," posterior - internal iliac artery and ureter," floor - obturator nerve and vessels -> ovarian pathology may cause pain along the medial thigh.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old woman has ovarian carcinoma. To which lymph nodes does ovarian cancer first spread? [MUL 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ovarian lymphatics follow the ovarian vessels to para-aortic nodes at LI-L2 (the ovary develops in the lumbar region). Peritoneal seeding is the commonest spread overall.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old woman has carcinoma of the lower third of the vagina. To which nodes does lymph from this part drain first? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vagina: upper third ￿ external/internal iliac; middle 4 internal iliac; lower third (below hymen) and vulva 4 superficial inguinal nodes. Fundus of uterus 4 para-aortic." uterine cornu 4 superficial inguinal via round ligament.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A carcinoma of the labium majus spreads along the round ligament of the uterus. Toward which canal may it extend? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Round ligament runs from the uterine cornu through the deep ring and inguinal canal to the labium majus; lymphatics along it explain spread between uterus, labium and superficial inguinal nodes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist explains the routes of spread of a uterine tumour along structures in the broad ligament. Which structure running in the broad ligament may provide a route for cancer spread to the peritoneal cavity. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The uterine tube opens into the peritoneal cavity through its abdominal ostium - a route for spread of infection (PID) and tumour cells from the uterus to the peritoneum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist plans culdocentesis to aspirate blood from the pouch of Douglas in a suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Through which part of the vagina is this done. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior fornix is deepest and is related to the rectouterine pouch (lowest part of the peritoneal cavity in the upright female) - used for culdocentesis and posterior colpotomy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: In severe pelvic inflammatory disease, a posterior incision is made through the vaginal wall to drain pus from the pelvic peritoneal cavity. Which peritoneal pouch is accessed? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior colpotomy enters the pouch of Douglas through the posterior fornix. Vesicouterine pouch lies anterior to the uterus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A gynaecologist examines the anterior fornix and feels the structure lying directly in front of it. To which structure is the anterior vaginal fornix related? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vaginal relations." anterior - bladder base and urethra; posterior - pouch of Douglas (upper), rectum (middle), perineal body (lower),. lateral - ureter, levator ani.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A cystoscopy in a woman shows the base of the bladder lying on a structure posteriorly. To which structure is the base of the urinary bladder related in females? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Female bladder base: anterior wall of vagina and cervix (vesicovaginal fistula after obstructed labour)," in males: rectum with seminal vesicles and ductus deferens between.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman at 36 weeks feels faint when lying flat on her back and develops swollen legs. Compression of which vessel by the gravid uterus causes these effects? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Supine hypotensive syndrome." the gravid uterus compresses the IVC (and aorta) ￿ I venous return, hypotension, lower-limb oedema and varicose veins," relieved by left lateral tilt.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man with a pelvic fracture has a urethral injury. Which part of the male urethra lies in the deep perineal pouch? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Deep pouch (male): membranous urethra, external urethral sphincter, deep transverse perineal muscles, bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands, dorsal nerve and artery of penis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student lists the contents of the deep perineal pouch. Which muscle is located in the deep perineal pouch? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superficial pouch." ischiocavernosus, bulbospongiosus, superficial transverse perinei, crura and bulb of penis/clitoris, (female) Bartholin glands. Deep pouch: sphincter urethrae, deep transverse perinei.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a pelvic fracture ruptures the membranous urethra above an intact perineal membrane. Into which space does urine primarily extravasate? [AMC 26]

options.A: Deep perineal pouch / extraperitoneal pelvic space
options.D: Under Scarpa's fascia of the thigh

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Membranous (posterior) urethral rupture: urine collects in the deep pouch and extraperitoneally around the bladder/prostate (retropubic space); the high-riding prostate is felt on DRE. No scrotal swelling if the perineal membrane is intact.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man falls astride a bar and ruptures his urethra; urine extravasates into the scrotum and lower anterior abdominal wall but not the thighs. In which space does the urine collect? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bulbar/spongy urethral rupture below the perineal membrane with Buck's fascia torn 4 urine in the superficial pouch, deep to Colles, fascia scrotum, penis. anterior abdominal wall (under Scarpa's): limited in the thigh by fusion with fascia lata.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 52-year-old man injures the penile urethra at the bulb in a straddle injury. Where does his extravasated urine spread? [KIMS 26]

options.D: Anterior abdominal wall (deep to Scarpa's fascia)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Colles, fascia is continuous with dartos and Scarpa's fascia; it is attached to the ischiopubic rami, posterior border of the perineal membrane and fascia lata 4 urine reaches the abdominal wall but not the thigh or anal triangle.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: While passing a catheter, a medical officer ruptures the spongy (penile) urethra. Into which space will urine extravasate. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spongy urethra lies in the corpus spongiosum within the superficial pouch,. false passage during catheterisation is commonest at the bulb.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a straddle injury, urine extravasates into the scrotum. Rupture of which part of the urethra (with Buck's fascia torn) is indicated? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: If Buck's fascia is intact. extravasation is limited to the penile shaft," if torn. it spreads in the superficial pouch to scrotum and abdominal wall ( butterfly" perineal bruising).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student describes the boundaries of the superficial perineal space. What forms its superior (deep) boundary. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superficial pouch lies between Colles, fascia (inferiorly/superficially) and the perineal membrane (superiorly); it is open anteriorly toward the abdominal wall.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student identifies the muscles of the superficial perineal pouch. Which muscle is contained in the superficial perineal pouch? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superficial pouch muscles (all pudendal nerve): ischiocavernosus, bulbospongiosus, superficial transverse perinei. Deep transverse perinei and sphincter urethrae lie in the deep pouch.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has erectile diff iculty after a perineal injury damaging a muscle that compresses the crura and the deep dorsal vein to maintain erection. Which muscle is involved? [MUL 25. MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the MUL 2025 key marked deep transverse perinei. Erection is maintained by ISCHIOCAVERNOSUS (compresses the crura) with bulbospongiosus (compresses the bulb, ejaculation); both are supplied by the perineal branch of the pudendal nerve.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has loss of tone in the bulbospongiosus and external urethral sphincter after a pelvic injury. Which nerve supplies these muscles. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pudendal nerve branches." inferior rectal (external anal sphincter, perianal skin), perineal (perineal muscles, sphincter urethrae, scrotal/labial skin), dorsal nerve of penis/clitoris.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man suffers trauma to the lower anal region with loss of perianal sensation, yet his erectile function is preserved. Which plexus carrying the parasympathetic erectile fibres must be intact? [AMC 25]

options.D: Inferior hypogastric (pelvic) plexus via pelvic splanchnic nerves

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked "pudendal plexus Erection = parasympathetic (pelvic splanchnic S2-S4 4 inferior hypogastric plexus 4 cavernous nerves); "Point" (parasympathetic erection) and "Shoot" (sympathetic emission). The pudendal nerve gives sensation and perineal muscle supply.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A perianal abscess spreads laterally into the ischioanal fossa. Which muscle forms the lateral wall of the ischioanal (ischiorectal) fossa. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ischioanal fossa: lateral obturator internus fascia (contains pudendal canal); medial - levator ani and external anal sphincter," posterior - gluteus maximus and sacrotuberous ligament. Fossae communicate behind the anal canal ￿ horseshoe abscess.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman has a painful wound over the mons pubis. Which nerve carries pain from this area. [KIMS 26]

options.B: Anterior labial branches of the ilioinguinal nerve

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mons pubis and anterior labia majora: ilioinguinal (anterior labial nerves, Ll) + genital branch of genitofemoral. Posterior labia: posterior labial branches of pudendal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 20-year-old with progressive myopia and irregular astigmatism has a cone-shaped cornea on slit-lamp examination. In keratoconus, which corneal layer thins first? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Keratoconus: progressive central/inferior stromal thinning -> conical protrusion, Fleischer ring, Vogt striae; treated with corneal collagen cross-linking. (Block 6 topic asked in a Block 4 paper.)

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 6~week-old baby has severe constipation; rectal biopsy shows absent ganglion cells between the circular and longitudinal muscle layers. What is the main function of the myenteric (Auerbach) plexus. [Prof 24]

options.A: Control of mucosal blood flow only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Myenteric plexus (between muscle layers) 4 motility: tone, rhythmic contractions, peristalsis. Submucosal (Meissner) plexus 4 secretion. absorption, local blood flow.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology student stimulates the plexus lying in the submucosa of an isolated gut segment. What does the submucosal (Meissner) plexus mainly regulate. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Meissner's plexus controls the inner wall: epithelial secretion, absorption and submucosal blood flow, responding to local mucosal stimuli.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient's gut biopsy is stained for inhibitory motor neurons of the myenteric plexus that relax sphincters and the receiving segment during peristalsis. Which neurotransmitter is associated with inhibitory signalling in the myenteric plexus. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inhibitory enteric transmitters: VIP, NO, ATP - relax LES, pylorus and the segment ahead of a bolus (receptive relaxation). Excitatory: Ach, substance P.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient given an anticholinergic drug develops constipation and dry mouth. Which neurotransmitter is the major excitatory mediator of gastrointestinal motility and secretion. [AMC 26 . MUL 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ach (muscarinic M3 on smooth muscle and glands) is the main excitatory transmitter of the ENS and vagus. Serotonin initiates the peristaltic reflex (from enterochromaffin cells) but is not the main motor transmitter.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient receives atropine before surgery. What is the effect of blocking acetylcholine in the enteric nervous system. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Antimuscarinics reduce peristalsis, secretions and gastric acid 4 constipation, urinary retention, dry mouth; used as antispasmodics (hyoscine).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During a stressful accident, a patient's bowel sounds disappear. Which neurotransmitter released during sympathetic stimulation inhibits gut motility. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Noradrenaline inhibits ENS neurons (presynaptic a2) and relaxes smooth muscle, but contracts sphincters," strong stimulation can block food movement (paralytic ileus).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man in a fight-or-f light state has reduced bowel activity. What is the effect of strong sympathetic stimulation on the Gl tract? [MUL 26]

options.C: Decreased motility (with constricted sphincters and reduced blood

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sympathetic (T5-L2): I motility, I secretion, I splanchnic blood flow, t sphincter tone. Parasympathetic." t motility and secretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old boy has early satiety and slow gastric emptying. Increased activity of which nerve fibres slows gastric emptying. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked parasympathetic. Vagal (parasympathetic) activity increases antral contractions and gastric emptying." sympathetic activity and enterogastric reflexes slow it.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Electrogastrography records rhythmic undulating changes in membrane potential of gastric smooth muscle. What is the normal frequency range of Gl slow waves. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Slow waves are not action potentials; they set the maximum rate of contraction. Spike potentials on their crests (Ca"_Na' channels) trigger contraction.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher studies the pacemaker cells responsible for slow waves in gastric smooth muscle. What generates the basic electrical rhythm (BER) of Gl smooth muscle? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked acetylcholine (with option B missing). Slow waves are generated by the interstitial cells of Cajal (electrical pacemakers. c-Kit positive); Ach only increases spike frequency on the slow waves.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with motor neurone disease has difficulty initiating swallowing and frequently chokes on liquids, with nasal regurgitation. Which phase of deglutition is most likely affected? [AMC 26. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pharyngeal phase is an involuntary reflex controlled by the medullary swallowing centre (nucleus ambiguus, CN IX, X): soft palate closes the nasopharynx, larynx elevates, epiglottis tilts, UES relaxes. Bulbar palsy disrupts it 4 aspiration.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman has progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids; manometry shows high LES pressure with failure to relax and absent peristalsis. Which physiological abnormality is characteristic? [BWP 26. BWP 25]

options.B: Failure of lower oesophageal sphincter relaxation

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Achalasia: incomplete LES relaxation + aperistalsis 4 dilated oesophagus, regurgitation. bird's-beak barium. Treatment: pneumatic dilatation, Heller myotomy, POEM, botulinum toxin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with achalasia cardia undergoes a myotomy. What is the main underlying defect in achalasia? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Degeneration of inhibitory myenteric neurons in the lower oesophagus (autoimmune/viral; Chagas disease in South America) 4 unopposed cholinergic tone at the LES.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher studies the neurotransmitters lost in achalasia. Defective release of which substances causes failure of LES relaxation? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NO and VIP from inhibitory neurons mediate receptive relaxation of the LES during swallowing; their loss keeps the sphincter closed.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman has heartburn, regurgitation of sour fluid, water brash and belching; endoscopy shows an incompetent lower oesophageal sphincter. Which condition and abnormality best describe her problem. [KIMS 25. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GERD: transient LES relaxations or low LES tone allow acid reflux; complications - oesophagitis. stricture, Barrett's metaplasia, adenocarcinoma. Aggravated by fatty meals, smoking. obesity, hiatus hernia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient receives a large fatty meal and gastric emptying slows markedly. Which hormone is the most potent inhibitor of gastric emptying. [HITEC 26. BWP 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the WMC 2025 key marked secretin. CCK (released by fat and protein in the duodenum) is the most potent hormonal inhibitor of gastric emptying; secretin (acid) and GIP also inhibit. This prevents duodenal overload.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Acidic chyme enters the duodenum of a patient with a duodenal ulcer. Which hormone released in response inhibits gastric motility (among the options)? [Prof 24 . BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Secretin (S cells, pH < 4.5) inhibits gastric motility and acid secretion and stimulates pancreatic HCO,-. Gastrin, motilin and ghrelin all increase motility.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Distension of the duodenum by chyme reduces the strength of antral contractions. What triggers the enterogastric reflex. [BWP 25 . QIMS 25]

options.B: Distensionfirritation of the duodenum (acid, fat, hyperosmolar chyme)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Enterogastric reflex (via ENS, sympathetic and vagal afferents): duodenal distension. irritation, acidity. osmolality, protein/fat breakdown products inhibits antral peristalsis and increases pyloric tone.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a large meal, the stomach volume increases f rom 50 ML to l L with little rise in intragastric pressure. Which reflex is mainly responsible for this storage function. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Receptive relaxation: swallowing and gastric stretch trigger a vagovagal reflex (VIP/NO) that relaxes the fundus and body. Lost after vagotomy early satiety.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During antral peristalsis, most chyme is squirted back toward the body of the stomach because the pylorus closes. What is this mixing movement called? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Antral "mill": peristaltic constrictor rings + pyloric closure 4 retropulsion grinds food into chyme.. only a few ML pass with each wave.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with peptic ulcer is given omeprazole, which blocks the final step of acid secretion. Inhibition of the H'/K'_ATPase reduces HCI secretion because it prevents: [AMC 26]

options.B: Hydrogen ion secretion into the gastric lumen
options.D: Chloride entry into the parietal cell

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Proton pump (H'/K'.ATPase) on the canalicular membrane exchanges H" for K.; Cl- follows through channels. HCO,- leaves basolaterally in exchange for Cl- (alkaline tide after meals).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A hungry student smells and sees food and his gastric secretion rises before eating. Which mechanism primarily stimulates gastric secretion during the cephalic phase. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cephalic phase (-30%): sight, smell, taste, thought 4 vagus ￿ Ach on parietal cells + GRP on G cells. Gastric phase (-60Yo).. distension and peptides. Intestinal phase (- 10%).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome has very high acid output. Which hormone stimulates gastric parietal cells to secrete hydrochloric acid? [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gastrin (G cells, antrum) acts on CCK-B receptors of ECL cells (histamine release) and parietal cells. Somatostatin and secretin inhibit acid,. acid in the antrum inhibits gastrin (negative feedback).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old with autoimmune gastritis has achlorhydria and markedly raised serum gastrin. Which mechanism explains the hypergastrinaemia. [KIMS 26]

options.A: Loss of acid negative feedback on G cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Antral acid (pH < 3) normally stimulates D-cell somatostatin, which inhibits G cells. Achlorhydria (atrophic gastritis, PPIS) removes this brake hypergastrinaemia ￿ ECL hyperplasia/carcinoids.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old woman with fatigue, glossitis and a smooth red tongue has atrophic gastritis of the body. With which condition is atrophic gastritis most often associated? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Autoimmune (type A) atrophic gastritis destroys parietal cells (anti-parietal cell and anti-intrinsic factor antibodies) 4 loss of intrinsic factor ￿ B12 deficiency (megaloblastic anaemia, neuropathy).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man on chronic NSAIDS for arthritis develops a gastric ulcer. Which protective factor decreases. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NSAIDS inhibit COX-I ￿ I prostaglandins 4 I mucus, l HCO,- I mucosal blood flow and t acid. Misoprostol (PGEI analogue) protects.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old banker has a peptic ulcer due to Helicobacter pylori. What is the main mechanism of ulcer formation? [KIMS 25]

options.B: Breakdown of the gastroduodenal mucosal barrier

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: H. pylori: urease (ammonia). proteases. phospholipases. cytotoxins (CagA. VacA) damage the mucus-bicarbonate barrier and epithelium," antral infection t gastrin 4 t acid 4 duodenal ulcer.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology lecture discusses why the stomach does not digest itself despite pH 1-2 in the lumen. Which physical factor protects the gastric mucosa from acid damage. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Surface mucous cells secrete a viscous alkaline gel layer that traps HCO,- (pH -7 at the epithelial surface); tight junctions, rapid cell renewal and mucosal blood flow add protection.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A motorcyclist has a head injury damaging the chemoreceptor trigger zone (area postrema) in the floor of the 4th ventricle. Vomiting due to which cause will still occur. [KIMS 25]

options.D: Gastric irritation (vagal afferents to the vomiting centre)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked vestibular disturbance. Drugs (morphine, apomorphine. chemotherapy) and motion sickness act via the CTZ,. GI irritation sends vagal/sympathetic afferents directly to the medullary vomiting centre. so it persists after CTZ damage.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient vomits greenish f luid containing bile repeatedly after surgery. Where is the obstruction most likely located? [WMC 25]

options.B: Distal to the ampulla of Vater (duodenum/proximal small bowel)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked the pyloric sphincter. Bilious vomiting means obstruction distal to the major duodenal papilla (bile enters there). Pyloric stenosis causes NON-bilious vomiting.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A barium study shows ring-like contractions dividing the jejunum into sausage~like segments that alternate rhythmically. Which movement is mainly responsible for mixing in the jejunum? [CKMC 26. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Segmentation contractions (mixing) follow the slow-wave frequency (12/min duodenum, 8-9/min ileum); peristalsis propels at- I cm/min, so small-bowel transit takes 3-5 hours.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A lesion abolishes segmentation movements of the small intestine but preserves peristalsis. What is the most likely consequence? [KIMS 26]

options.A: Reduced mixing of enrymes with food and poor absorption

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Segmentation mixes chyme with digestive juices and brings it into contact with the mucosa; peristalsis moves it forward. Loss of segmentation impairs digestion and absorption.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Between meals a fasting patient has bursts of intense contractions sweeping from the stomach to the ileum every 90 minutes. Which hormone regulates this migrating motor complex. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Motilin (M cells of duodenum/jejunum) triggers the MMC ("housekeeper") that clears residue and bacteria," erythromycin is a motilin agonist (prokinetic).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In a diabetic patient with gastrointestinal neuropathy, migrating motor complexes are absent. An increase in which of the following results. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MMCS sweep undigested residue and bacteria into the colon," their loss ￿ bacterial overgrowth, bloating, B12 deficiency and malabsorption.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with severe infectious diarrhoea has powerful waves sweeping long distances along the small intestine within minutes. What is this movement called? [KIMS 25. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Peristaltic rush: a prolonged series of powerful peristaltic waves triggered by intense irritation or distension (infection) 4 rapid evacuation into the colon 4 diarrhoea.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A tourist has acute infectious diarrhoea with very rapid intestinal transit. Which mechanism explains the watery stools. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rapid transit shortens contact time between chyme and mucosa 4 less water and electrolyte absorption; most water (-8 L/day) is absorbed in the small intestine, the rest in the colon.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a meal, the ileum empties its contents into the caecum more rapidly. Which reflex is responsible. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gastroileal reflex: gastric filling (via gastrin and ENS) increases ileal peristalsis and relaxes the ileocaecal sphincter.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a right hemicolectomy that removes the ileocaecal junction, a patient develops bacterial overgrowth in the ileum. What is the principal function of the ileocaecal valve? [QIMS 25 . CKMC 26]

options.A: Control the rate of entry of chyme into the caecum
options.B: Prevent entry of chyme into the caecum
options.D: Prevent reflux of faecal contents from the colon into the ileum

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ileocaecal valve lips close when caecal pressure rises (prevents backflow of colonic bacteria)," the ileocaecal sphincter slows ileal emptying, prolonging absorption.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Intestinal epithelial cells absorb Na" from the lumen; the ion must then be pumped out into the interstitial fluid. Which transporter moves Na. across the basolateral membrane. [MUL26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Basolateral Na"/K'_ATPase keeps intracellular Na" low. creating the gradient for apical Na. entry (SGLTI, NHE3, ENaC in colon)," water follows osmotically.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 22-year-old has sudden painless rice-water stools and vomiting after drinking contaminated water. What is the mechanism of this diarrhoea. [KIMS 25]

options.C: Inhibition of CAMP in intestinal cells
options.D: High chloride secretion from intestinal crypts (cAMP-mediated)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cholera toxin ADP-ribosylates Gsa ￿ persistent adenylyl cyclase activation ￿ t CAMP 4 CFTR Cl- secretion from crypts, Na. and water follow," SGLTI is spared 4 ORS works.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with cholera loses litres of fluid daily. Which function of the bowel (including the large intestine) is most directly overwhelmed? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Secretory diarrhoea exceeds the colon's absorptive capacity (-5-8 L/day maximum)," stool volume continues despite fasting, distinguishing it from osmotic diarrhoea.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with ulcerative colitis has bloody diarrhoea with pus. What is the primary mechanism of diarrhoea in inflammatory bowel disease. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inflammatory (exudative) diarrhoea: mucosal damage leaks blood, protein and pus, with reduced absorption." contrast secretory (cholera - CAMP) and osmotic (lactose intolerance).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A medical student has loose stools every time before examinations. What type of diarrhoea is this. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Psychogenic (nervous) diarrhoea." emotional tension 4 excessive parasympathetic stimulation of the distal colon 4 t motility and mucus secretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man feels the urge to defaecate shortly after breakfast as a large segment of colon contracts and pushes faeces into the rectum. What is the main propulsive movement in the large intestine? [HITEC 26 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mass movements: 20 cm or more of colon contracts as a unit, 1-3 times daily (often after meals via gastrocolic/duodenocolic reflexes), moving faeces into the rectum ￿ defaecation urge.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A barium enema shows sacculations of the colon formed by combined contractions of circular muscle and taeniae coli. Which movement occurs in the large intestine for mixing. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Haustrations mix and slowly roll faecal matter over the mucosa so water and electrolytes are absorbed; a colon transit takes 8- 15 hours to 3 days.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A toddler opens his bowels soon after every meal. Which reflex causes increased colonic motility after food enters the stomach? [CKMC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gastrocolic reflex: gastric distension (via ENS, gastrin, CCK) triggers colonic mass movements; prominent in infants and in irritable bowel syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with a sacral spinal lesion loses the strong parasympathetic component of defaecation. Which nerves carry the extrinsic (parasympathetic) defaecation reflex? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rectal distension 4 sacral cord ￿ pelvic nerves intensify peristalsis and relax the internal sphincter (parasympathetic defaecation reflex). External sphincter is voluntary via the pudendal nerve.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: At rest, the internal anal sphincter remains tonically contracted, preventing faecal leakage. Which autonomic input mainly maintains this tone. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: IAS (smooth muscle) tone is maintained mainly by intrinsic myogenic activity and sympathetic (Ll-L2, al) excitation." parasympathetic (pelvic) and VIP/NO relax it during defaecation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old with a lumbar spinal cord injury cannot defaecate voluntarily but occasionally passes stool reflexly when the rectum is distended. Which mechanism explains this. [KIMS 25]

options.D: Sacral reflex arc intact but voluntary (cortical) control lost

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lesion above the sacral segments." the sacral defaecation reflex persists (automatic emptying) but voluntary control of the external sphincter via descending pathways is lost.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old has infrequent hard stools. Which change is mainly responsible. [KIMS 26]

options.C: Increased colonic motility with rapid transit
options.D: Prolonged colonic transit causing excess water absorption

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Slow transit allows the colon to absorb more water ￿ hard stools; causes include low fibre, inactivity, opioids, hypothyroidism, ignoring the urge.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman undergoes total colectomy and passes frequent loose stools afterwards. Which primary function of the colon has been lost? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Proximal colon absorbs water and Na" (aldosterone T ENaC) and secretes K, and HCO,-; distal colon stores faeces. Loss 4 watery output (ileostomy - l L/day).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 20-year-old woman in sickle cell crisis has yellow sclera, raised unconjugated bilirubin and normal liver enzymes; urine is free of bilirubin. What is the cause of her jaundice? [Prof 24. BWP 26]

options.A: Carcinoma of the head of pancreas
options.D: Obstruction of the common bile duct

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pre-hepatic: t unconjugated (water-insoluble, albumin-bound) bilirubin 4 acholuric jaundice; urine urobilinogen t, stools darker. Seen in haemolysis, Gilbert and Crigler-Naiiar syndromes.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old has jaundice with raised conjugated bilirubin, clay-coloured stools and dark urine. What type of jaundice is most likely? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Obstructive: conjugated bilirubin regurgitates into blood 4 bilirubinuria (dark urine); no bilirubin reaches the gut 4 pale stools. absent urine urobilinogen," t ALP, pruritus (bile salts).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A medical student develops jaundice and vomiting from obstruction of the common bile duct. What is the main cause of jaundice in bile duct obstruction. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hepatocytes still conjugate bilirubin, but it cannot be excreted into bile 4 leaks back into blood as conjugated (direct) bilirubin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology exam tests interpretation of jaundice. Which statement correctly links the type of jaundice with its finding? [QIMS 25]

options.A: CBD obstruction if aminotransferases are high and ALP is low
options.B: Haemolytic disease if there is bilirubin of either type in the urine
options.C: Hepatic disease if plasma albumin is low and serum bilirubin is mainly
options.D: Haemolytic disease if prothrombin is low unconjugated

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hepatocellular disease impairs both uptake/conjugation and synthesis (low albumin, prolonged PT). Haemolysis causes NO bilirubinuria; obstruction raises ALP markedly.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a fatty meal, CCK stimulates gallbladder contraction, but the response fails in a patient with a diseased gallbladder. Which function is directly affected? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CCK contracts the gallbladder and relaxes the sphincter of Oddi 4 bile enters the duodenum to emulsify fat. storage and concentration occur between meals.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist stimulates the vagus nerve and observes the gallbladder. What is the effect of parasympathetic (vagal) stimulation on the gallbladder. [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vagal Ach causes weak gallbladder contraction (cephalic phase); CCK is the main stimulus. Sympathetic activity relaxes the gallbladder.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman develops loose fatty stools after cholecystectomy. What is the most likely reason. [KIMS 25]

options.C: Decreased bile production by the liver
options.D: Loss of bile storage and concentration (continuous dilute bile flow)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Without a gallbladder, bile trickles continuously and cannot be delivered in a concentrated bolus with fatty meals; bile acid diarrhoea may follow.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A medical student with obstruction of the common bile duct asks about bile composition. Which substance makes up the largest proportion of bile solids. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bile solids: bile salts (~50-65%). phospholipids/lecithin, cholesterol. bilirubin; electrolytes and water. Bile salts are concentrated 5-20x in the gallbladder.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old woman has cholesterol gallstones. What predisposes to cholesterol gallstone formation. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cholesterol is kept in solution by bile salts and lecithin (micelles): excess cholesterol, too little bile salt, gallbladder stasis or excess water absorption precipitation. "Fat, female, forty, fertile"

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A baby fed high-fat milk develops pale, clay-coloured stools. Which component of bile is most likely def icient in the gut? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Brown stool colour comes from stercobilin derived from bilirubin," absence of bile pigments in the gut (biliary atresia, obstruction) ￿ pale/clay stools. Bile salt deficiency causes steatorrhoea.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old with alcoholic cirrhosis has massive ascites and splenomegaly. What is the main cause of ascites in cirrhosis. [BWP 25]

options.B: Portal hypertension (increased hydrostatic pressure in hepatic sinusoids/splanchnic bed)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ascites: portal hypertension + hypoalbuminaemia + splanchnic vasodilatation 4 RAAS activation and Na'/water retention. Treated with salt restriction, spironolactone and paracentesis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Acidic chyme enters the duodenum of a healthy volunteer. Which stimulus primarily releases secretin from duodenal S cells. [AMC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the AMC 2025 key marked "protein digested fats" Secretin is released mainly by ACID in the duodenum." CCK by fats and proteins.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic pancreatitis has reduced duodenal bicarbonate. Which hormone primarily stimulates bicarbonate secretion from pancreatic ductal cells. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Secretin 4 CAMP in ductal cells 4 CFTR Cl- channel + Cl-/HCO3 exchange 4 watery HCO3 -rich juice (up to 145 mEq/L) that neutralises acid. CCK potentiates it.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic pancreatitis and long-term high-dose PPI therapy is found to have reduced secretin release after meals. Which change explains the decreased secretin secretion. [KIMS 25]

options.D: Decreased acid delivery to the duodenum

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Secretin release depends on duodenal acidity; achlorhydria or reduced acid delivery reduces secretin and thus pancreatic HCO,

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with pancreatic duct obstruction has decreased bicarbonate secretion into the duodenum. What is the consequence. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Without HCO,- the duodenal pH stays low 4 mucosal injury (ulcers) and inactivation of pancreatic enzymes (lipase is irreversibly inactivated at low pH) ￿ steatorrhoea.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
