mcqs.question: A researcher finds that after a meal rich in fats and proteins there is a sustained increase in enzyme-rich pancreatic juice. Which mechanism best explains this. [KIMS 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CCK (I cells," stimulated by fatty acids, monoglycerides, peptides and amino acids) 4 acinar enzyme secretion and gallbladder contraction.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology student asks which hormone most powerfully controls meal-stimulated pancreatic enzyme secretion. Which hormone is this? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pancreatic enzyme secretion: CCK (=70-80A), Ach (vagal), gastrin (minor). Fluid/HCO3 secretin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A newborn with a congenital enzyme defect has severe protein malabsorption because pancreatic zymogens are not activated. What normally activates pancreatic zymogens. [AMC 25]

options.C: Enterokinase (enteropeptidase) of the duodenal brush border

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Enteropeptidase converts trypsinogen 4 trypsin, which activates other zymogens (chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidase, proelastase. prophospholipase). Trypsin inhibitor protects the pancreas.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with pancreatic exocrine insufficiency has bulky, foul-smelling, floating stools. Deficiency of which enzyme is most responsible for the steatorrhoea. [AMC 26 . KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pancreatic lipase (with colipase) hydrolyses triglycerides to 2-monoglycerides and fatty acids; steatorrhoea appears when < IOA of lipase output remains. Treated with pancreatic enzyme replacement.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man has severe epigastric pain radiating to the back that improves when he sits up and leans forward; serum lipase is very high. What is the most likely diagnosis. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Acute pancreatitis (gallstones. alcohol): premature intrapancreatic trypsin activation 4 autodigestion. Lipase/amylase > 3x normal; Grey-Turner and Cullen signs in haemorrhagic cases.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 70-kg man is evaluated for fluid therapy; the resident estimates his total body water. What is the approximate total body water of a 70-kg adult man. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 60Yo rule: TB W ~ 0.6 x 70 = 42 L - ICF 2/3 (28 L), ECF 1/3 (14 L: interstitial 11 L, plasma 3 L). Women and the elderly have less (more fat).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man loses 1.5 L of whole blood after trauma; ECF volume falls with no change in osmolarity. What type of fluid change is this. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Darrow-yannet: loss of isotonic fluid (haemorrhage, diarrhoea, burns) ￿ ECF volume I, osmolarity unchanged, ICF unchanged.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A post-operative patient has signif icant whole-blood loss f rom bleeding. What is the immediate effect on body fluid compartments? [KIMS 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Whole blood is isotonic, so only ECF (plasma) volume falls initially; ICF is unaffected because there is no osmotic gradient.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with gastroenteritis loses large volumes of isotonic fluid through severe diarrhoea and vomiting. Which compartment is primarily depleted? [WMC 25]

options.A: Both compartments equally with t osmolarity

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Isotonic losses deplete ECF 4 hypovolaemia, tachycardia, hypotension; untreated, renal hypoperfusion may progress from prerenal azotaemia to acute tubular necrosis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A desert traveller loses water through sweating and has no access to drinking water (pure water loss). What happens in primary (hypertonic) dehydration. [WMC 25]

options.B: I ECF volume, I ICF volume, t osmolarity of both

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypertonic contraction: water loss raises ECF osmolarity 4 water moves out of cells 4 both compartments shrink and osmolarity rises (cellular dehydration, thirst, ADH).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A severely dehydrated patient has raised plasma osmolality. In which direction does water shift between compartments. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: In hypertonic dehydration the ECF becomes hyperosmotic, drawing water out of cells - brain cells shrink (confusion. risk of venous tearing); correct slowly to avoid cerebral oedema.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient receives an infusion of 3% hypertonic saline. What is the expected effect on ECF and ICF volumes after equilibration. [AMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypertonic saline stays in the ECF (Nacl is excluded from cells) 4 ECF osmolarity t 4 water leaves cells." ECF volume t, ICF volume I, osmolarity of both t . total body water t.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient is given a large volume of a hypotonic solution intravenously. What is the expected effect on ECF and ICF volumes. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypotonic expansion: ECF osmolarity falls, water enters cells 4 both compartments expand and osmolarity falls (risk of cerebral oedema - hyponatraemia).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child is given 0.45% Nacl (half-normal saline). What happens to the cells? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 0.45% Nacl ~ 154 mOsm/L (hypotonic) 4 water enters cells ￿ swelling. 0. 9A Nacl (308 mOsm/L) is isotonic; 3% Nacl is hypertonic (shrinkage).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher wants to measure the extracellular fluid volume using a substance that crosses capillaries but not cell membranes. Which substance is commonly used? [MUL 26. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Indicator-dilution: TBW - D,0, tritiated water, antipyrine; ECF - inulin, mannitol, sucrose, 'Na, 'Cl; plasma - Evans blue, ECF; interstitial = ECF - plasma.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A biochemist measures the ionic composition of intracellular fluid. Which is the most abundant intracellular anion. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ICF: K, (main cation), Mg"; phosphates (organic) and proteins (main anions). ECF.. Na., Cl-, HCO,

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student analyses the major extracellular cation responsible for ECF osmolality. Which is the chief extracellular cation. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Na. (- 142 mEq/L) with its anions accounts for~90% of ECF osmolality." Posm = 2[Na'] + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with severe vomiting and diarrhoea is admitted with dehydration and low serum sodium. Why does hyponatraemia develop. [BWP 25]

options.C: Hypovolaemia stimulates ADH, causing water retention

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Volume depletion is a powerful non-osmotic ADH stimulus; if losses are replaced with water/hypotonic fluids, free water is retained 4 hypovolaemic hyponatraemia (urine Na, < 20 if extrarenal losses).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with renal artery stenosis has high renin levels. Which cells secrete renin and where are they located? [LHR 25 . AMC 25]

options.A: Juxtaglomerular cells in the afferent arteriole

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Renin release: l afferent arteriolar pressure (baroreceptor), l Nacl at macula densa, sympathetic Fl. The JG apparatus, primary role is renin secretion and tubuloglomerular feedback.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Renin is released in a hypovolaemic patient and acts on its plasma substrate. Which substance is formed when renin acts on angiotensinogen. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Angiotensinogen (liver) ￿ renin ￿ angiotensin l (decapeptide) ￿ ACE (mainly lungs) ￿ angiotensin 11 (octapeptide) ￿ vasoconstriction, aldosterone, ADH, thirst, efferent constriction.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic kidney disease has normocytic anaemia. Which cells in the kidney secrete erythropoietin. [LHR 25]

options.B: Peritubular interstitial fibroblast-like cells of the cortex

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: EPO is produced by interstitial (peritubular) fibroblast-like cells in the inner cortex/outer medulla in response to hypoxia (HIF-2a); CKD ￿ EPO deficiency anaemia (treat with recombinant EPO).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher studies prostaglandin production in the juxtaglomerular region that stimulates renin release when Nacl delivery falls. Which cells produce these prostaglandins. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked extraglomerular mesangial cells. Low Nacl at the macula densa induces COX-2 4 PGE, (and NO) 4 renin release from JG cells; renomedullary interstitial cells also make PGS.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with heart failure has high atrial natriuretic peptide levels. What is the main stimulus for ANP release. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ANP from atrial myocytes when atria are stretched ￿ natriuresis, diuresis, vasodilatation, t GFR (afferent dilatation, efferent constriction), inhibits renin. aldosterone and ADH.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher studies the renal effects of ANP. ANP acts mainly through which receptor. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Natriuretic peptides (ANP, BNP) bind NPR-A, a membrane guanylyl cyclase ￿ t CGMP. NO acts through soluble guanylyl cyclase.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with volume overload has high ANP, which reduces Na" reabsorption. On which part of the nephron does ANP act mainly. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ANP inhibits ENaC/CNG channels in the medullary collecting duct and increases GFR 4 natriuresis; it also blocks renin and aldosterone secretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A healthy 25-year-old man is evaluated as a kidney donor. What is his expected normal GFR? [Prof 24. CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GFR = 125 mL/min (180 Uday),. RPF = 625-650 mL/min." RBF = I. 1-1.2 Umin (-22% of cardiac output)." filtration fraction = 20%.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A medical student calculates net filtration pressure: glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure 50 mmHg, Bowman's space pressure 12 mmHg, glomerular oncotic pressure 30 mmHg, no protein in the filtrate. What is the net filtration pressure. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NFP = PGC- PBS - JTGC (+ NBS) = 50 - 12 - 30 + 0= 8 mmHg. Normal values (Guyton): 60 - 18 - 32 = 10 mmHg.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with nephrotic syndrome has low plasma proteins and a raised filtration rate early in the disease. Which change increases glomerular filtration. [Prof 24]

options.A: Decreased glomerular capillary colloid osmotic pressure

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GFR = Kf x NFP. T GFR: t PGC (afferent dilatation, efferent mild constriction), l JtGC (hypoproteinaemia), t Kf. l GFR: t PBS (obstruction), afferent constriction, l Kf.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Intense sympathetic stimulation during haemorrhage constricts the afferent arterioles. What is the effect on glomerular filtration pressure and GFR? [AMC 25. KIMS 26]

options.A: Decreased GFR due to decreased glomerular capillary hydrostatic

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Afferent constriction lowers PGC downstream ￿ l NFP and l GFR," renal plasma flow also falls.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student is asked how afferent arteriolar constriction changes GFR and filtration fraction (FF = GFR/RPF). What is the effect? [AMC 26]

options.C: GFR I, FF l or unchanged (both GFR and RPF fall)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source recorded a disputed alternative ( I GFR, t FF). Afferent constriction reduces both RPF and GFR roughly proportionally, so FF is unchanged or slightly I . efferent constriction T FF.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman with CKD has increased resistance in her afferent arterioles. What effect does this have on GFR? [KIMS 25. BWP 26]

options.C: Decreased GFR ( I glomerular capillary pressure)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Isolated t afferent resistance ￿ I PGC and l RBF 4 l GFR. Isolated t efferent resistance 4 t PGC, t GFR (mild), I RBF.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology question asks which arteriolar change increases GFR. When does GFR increase. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Afferent dilatation (prostaglandins. NO, high-protein meal, tubuloglomerular feedback in hypoperfusion) raises PGC and RBF 4 GFR t. NSAIDS block afferent dilatation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient taking an ACE inhibitor becomes dehydrated and his serum creatinine rises. Which renal haemodynamic effect contributes to the fall in GFR? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Angiotensin 11 preferentially constricts the EFFERENT arteriole to maintain PGC when perfusion falls: ACE inhibitors/ARBs remove this ￿ GFR drops (dangerous with bilateral renal artery stenosis or volume depletion).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Renal perfusion falls during hypotension, yet GFR is relatively maintained. Which mechanism helps maintain GFR? [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Autoregulation (75-160 mmHg) via myogenic response and tubuloglomerular feedback (macula densa l Nacl 4 afferent dilatation + renin angiotensin I1￿ efferent constriction).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with severe dehydration has decreased glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure, increased plasma oncotic pressure and normal Bowman's pressure. What is the net effect on GFR? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Both changes reduce NFP: I PGC (hypovolaemia) and t TTGC (haemoconcentration) 4 prerenal fall in GFR ( t BUN."creatinine ratio > 20).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with long-standing hypertension has falling GFR. How can hypertension decrease GFR over time. [BWP 26]

options.B: By increasing glomerular capillary pressure acutely
options.C: By damaging glomeruli (nephrosclerosis) and reducing filtration
options.D: By increasing the filtration coeff icient surface area

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chronic hypertension 4 hyaline arteriolosclerosis and glomerulosclerosis 4 loss of nephrons and l Kf 4 reduced GFR (hypertensive nephrosclerosis).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with hypertension and diabetes has raised serum urea and creatinine. What is the main renal defect? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Creatinine and urea rise when GFR falls," plasma creatinine roughly doubles for each 50% fall in GFR.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old with long-standing diabetes has rising creatinine and proteinuria. What is the major cause of decreased GFR in diabetic nephropathy. [BWP 25]

options.B: Thickening of the glomerular basement membrane with mesangial expansion (glomerulosclerosis)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Diabetic nephropathy: early hyperfiltration 4 GBM thickening, mesangial expansion, nodular Kimmelstiel-wilson lesions 4 microalbuminuria overt proteinuria 4 falling GFR.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A renal biopsy in diabetic nephropathy is stained to examine the glomerular basement membrane. Which type of collagen forms the GBM? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Type IV collagen (sheet-like network) with laminin and heparan sulphate forms basement membranes; mutations ￿ Alport syndrome; antibodies to its a3 chain 4 Goodpasture syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child with heavy proteinuria and pedal oedema has normal glomeruli on light microscopy. Which structural change in the glomerulus is most likely responsible. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Minimal change disease." diffuse podocyte foot-process effacement on electron microscopy 4 loss of charge/size selectivity 4 selective proteinuria; steroid-responsive.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has generalised oedema, heavy proteinuria (> 3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminaemia and hyperlipidaemia. What is the primary defect in nephrotic syndrome. [KIMS 26]

options.C: Increased glomerular basement membrane permeability to proteins
options.D: Increased f iltration of red cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nephrotic: damaged filtration barrier 4 proteinuria 4 hypoalbuminaemia 4 l oncotic pressure 4 oedema: liver t lipoprotein synthesis hyperlipidaemia; hypercoagulability.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old has periorbital puffiness, oliguria, cola-coloured urine and hypertension after a sore throat. Why does oedema develop in nephritic syndrome. [QIMS 25]

options.C: Increased capillary hydrostatic pressure from salt and water
options.D: Decreased plasma oncotic pressure (heavy proteinuria) retention

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked decreased oncotic pressure - that is the mechanism in NEPHROTIC syndrome. In nephritic syndrome, reduced GFR causes Na'/water retention ￿ hypervolaemia and hypertension.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient presents with haematuria (dysmorphic RBCS, RBC casts) and mild proteinuria. Which syndrome is most likely. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nephritic: haematuria. RBC casts, oliguria, hypertension, mild proteinuria (< 3.5 g/day) - inflammatory glomerular injury (post-streptococcal, IgA nephropathy, RPGN).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient on diuretics has changes in GFR, yet the fraction of filtered Na" reabsorbed by the proximal tubule stays nearly constant. Which mechanism is responsible. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glomerulotubular balance: when GFR rises, filtration fraction t 4 peritubular oncotic pressure t 4 more PCT reabsorption, keeping~65A reabsorbed and buffering distal Na. delivery.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology student studies Starling forces in peritubular capillaries. Which change increases fluid reabsorption into the peritubular capillaries. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Peritubular reabsorption t with I peritubular hydrostatic pressure (efferent constriction, low arterial pressure) and t peritubular oncotic pressure ( t filtration fraction).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has urine creatinine 196 mg/dL, urine flow I mL/min and plasma creatinine 1.4 mg/dL. What is the creatinine clearance. [AMC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: C = (U x V)/P = (196 x l)/1.4 = 140 mumin. Creatinine clearance slightly overestimates GFR because -10-20% is secreted.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A substance has urine concentration 100 mg/mL, urine flow 2 mumin and plasma concentration 10 mg/mL. What is its renal clearance. [MUL26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: C = UV/P = (100 x 2)/10= 20 mumin - far below GFR (125), so the substance must be reabsorbed.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher wants to measure GFR using a substance that is freely filtered, neither secreted nor reabsorbed, and not metabolised. Which substance should be used? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inulin clearance = GFR (gold standard). Clinically: creatinine clearance or eGFR (CKD-EPI). Clearance < GFR 4 net reabsorption; > GFR 4 net secretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher uses inulin concentration in tubular fluid samples to determine how much water has been reabsorbed along the nephron. Why is inulin used to assess tubular fluid flow/water reabsorption. [BWP 26]

options.C: It is filtered but neither reabsorbed nor secreted, so its concentration
options.D: It binds plasma proteins rises only as water is removed

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TF/P inulin ratio: e.g. 3 at the end of the PCT means 2/3 of filtered water has been reabsorbed. Fraction of filtrate remaining = l/(TF/P inulin).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A nephrologist wants to estimate effective renal plasma flow. Which substance is used? [MUL 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PAH is filtered and almost completely secreted (- 90AO extraction) in one pass 4 PAH clearance ~ effective RPF (-625 mumin). RBF = RPF/(l - Hct).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In a healthy volunteer, inulin clearance is 125 mumin while PAH clearance is 600 mL/min. What can be concluded about PAH? [KIMS 25. KIMS 26]

options.A: Inulin is reabsorbed while PAH is only filtered
options.C: PAH is freely filtered and actively secreted

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: A substance cleared almost completely in one renal pass must be filtered AND secreted (organic anion transporters in the PCT). Filtration fraction = 125/600 = 0.2.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A person has a glucose Tm of 350 mg/min, GFR 100 mumin, plasma glucose 150 mg/dL, urine flow 2 mL/min and no glucose in urine. What is the approximate rate of glucose reabsorption. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note: the source key marked 350 mg/min (the Tm). Filtered load = GFR x P = 100 mL/min x 1.5 mg/mL = 150 mg/min; with no glucosuria, all 150 mg/min is reabsorbed. Tm is reached only above the threshold (~200 mg/dL).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 26-year-old man with glomerulonephritis has a sustained 50% fall in GFR. For which substance would you expect the greatest increase in plasma concentration. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Creatinine excretion depends almost entirely on filtration, so plasma creatinine doubles when GFR halves. Na., K. and glucose are regulated by tubular adjustments and stay near normal.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A long~standing diabetic man has a large flaccid bladder with high residual volume and passes frequent small amounts by overflow. Which condition is this? [Prof 24. AMC 25. MUL 26]

options.B: Automatic bladder due to cord transection
options.D: Atonic bladder due to sacral dorsal root (afferent) damage

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Atonic bladder: destruction of sensory afferents (tabes dorsalis, diabetic neuropathy, crush injury of sacral roots) 4 no stretch signals ￿ bladder fills to capacity and overflows ( overflow incontinence").

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has a large flaccid bladder, high residual urine and absent bladder sensation after a cauda equina/conus lesion. Where is the lesion most likely located? [HITEC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Damage to the sacral cord or its roots abolishes the micturition reflex 4 autonomous/atonic bladder. Lesion above the sacral cord (after spinal shock) ￿ automatic reflex bladder; frontal lesion 4 uninhibited bladder.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has a spinal injury at SI-S2; the bladder is distended although the pontine centre is intact. Which mechanism is affected? [KIMS 26]

options.C: Voluntary relaxation of the external sphincter
options.D: Parasympathetic efferent activation of the detrusor

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Detrusor contraction requires parasympathetic preganglionic neurons in S2-S4 travelling in the pelvic splanchnic nerves; their damage prevents emptying 4 retention.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist explains the reflex control of micturition. Where is the sacral micturition centre located? [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Micturition reflex." stretch receptors 4 pelvic nerves 4 S2-S4 4 pelvic nerves 4 detrusor contraction," facilitated/inhibited by the pontine micturition centre (Barrington's) and cortex.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A pharmacologist explains drugs that act on the detrusor. Which nerves provide parasympathetic supply to the detrusor muscle? [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4): Ach on M3 ￿ detrusor contraction (antimuscarinics treat overactive bladder). Hypogastric (sympathetic) ￿ relaxes detrusor. contracts internal sphincter. Pudendal 4 external sphincter.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A man lost in a desert drinks no water for days and his kidneys concentrate urine maximally. What is the maximum urine osmolality achievable by human kidneys. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Range: 50 (max dilution) to 12CK)-14CK) mOsm/L. Obligatory urine volume = 600 mOsm/day . 1200 mOsm/L = 0.5 Uday.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A patient in renal failure becomes oliguric; the doctor calculates the minimum urine needed to excrete daily solutes. What is the approximate minimum obligatory urine volume in a healthy adult? [AMC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Normal solute load-600 mOsm/day at max concentration 1200 mOsm/L ￿-0.5 L/day. Oliguria < 4CK) muday; anuria < 100 muday.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A patient with hypertension has increased blood flow through the vasa recta and cannot concentrate urine well. What is the underlying mechanism. [AMC 26]

options.B: Washout of the medullary osmotic gradient

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Slow vasa recta flow is essential to preserve medullary hyperosmolarity," increased flow (vasodilators. hypertension, osmotic diuresis) washes out solutes 4 reduced concentrating ability.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A student is asked how the high medullary interstitial osmolarity is GENERATED. Which mechanisms create it? [MUL 26]

options.A: Water secretion by the collecting duct
options.B: Countercurrent multiplication by the loop of Henle and urea recycling

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Generation: active Nacl transport in the thick ascending limb (NKCC2) multiplied by countercurrent flow in the loop + urea recycling from inner medullary collecting ducts (ADH t UT-AI).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A student is asked how the medullary osmotic gradient is MAINTAINED once formed. Which mechanism maintains it? [MUL 26. BWP 26. KIMS 26]

options.A: Na, secretion by the collecting duct
options.D: Countercurrent exchange in the vasa recta with slow blood flow

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vasa recta are countercurrent EXCHANGERS: hairpin shape and sluggish flow (1-2% of RBF) remove reabsorbed water and solute without dissipating the gradient.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A physiology student identifies the segment acting as the countercurrent multiplier. Which part of the nephron is it? [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loop of Henle (especiallyjuxtamedullary nephrons with long loops) creates a vertical gradient from 3CK) mOsm/L in the cortex to 1200 in the inner medulla.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A student asks what role the loop of Henle plays in conserving water. What is its key contribution? [AMC 25]

options.B: Creates a hyperosmotic medullary interstitium (thick limb pumps Nacl out without water)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key ("increases permeability of water") is incorrect. The descending limb is water-permeable, the thick ascending limb is water-impermeable and actively removes Nacl 4 medullary gradient that lets ADH concentrate urine in the collecting duct.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A student follows tubular fluid along the nephron in a dehydrated patient. In which segment does tubular fluid become concentrated as water leaves by osmosis. [CKMC 26]

options.A: Thin descending limb of the loop of Henle

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Descending limb: highly water-permeable (AQPI), poor solute permeability 4 fluid reaches- 1200 mOsm/L at the hairpin. PCT fluid stays isosmotic (_300).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A physiology student identifies the segment that reabsorbs Na", K" and Cl- but is impermeable to water, diluting the tubular fluid. Which segment is this "diluting segmentll? [WMC 26. CKMC 26]

options.A: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TAL: NKCC2 (l Na,. l K,, 2 Cl-) + ROMK K. recycling (lumen-positive potential drives Ca" and Mg" paracellular reabsorption); fluid leaves at-100 mOsm/L.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A nephrologist explains that fluid in the early distal tubule near the macula densa has a characteristic tonicity. What is true of this tubular fluid? [QIMS 25]

options.C: It is hypertonic only when GFR falls by 50%

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Because the TAL removes solute without water, early distal fluid is ALWAYS hypotonic, regardless of ADH or hydration status.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A dehydrated patient has high ADH levels. In which part of the nephron is hypotonic fluid still found? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked the collecting tubule - but with high ADH, collecting-duct fluid becomes iso- then hypertonic. Early distal tubule fluid remains hypotonic in all states.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A patient has complete lack of ADH due to central diabetes insipidus. Which part of the renal tubule would have the lowest tubular fluid osmolality. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked early distal tubule. Without ADH. Nacl reabsorption continues in the late distal tubule and collecting ducts with little water 4 osmolality falls further. to -50 mOsm/L in the medullary collecting duct.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A healthy 29-year-old man runs a 10-km race on a hot day and becomes very dehydrated, with very high ADH. In which part of the tubule is the MOST water reabsorbed? IQIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Even with maximal ADH, the PCT reabsorbs-65% of filtered water (obligatory, isosmotic); the collecting duct reabsorbs only a few % of the filtrate but determines final concentration.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: Without ADH, which nephron segment shows the greatest reduction in water reabsorption? Choose the segment. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ADH acts on the late distal tubule and collecting ducts (V2 4 AQP2); absence 4 large volume of dilute urine (up to 20 L/day).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: An uncontrolled diabetic man passes a large volume of urine containing glucose. In which condition is a large volume of isosmotic (or relatively concentrated) urine excreted? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Osmotic diuresis (glucose, mannitol) carries water with the unabsorbed solute 4 high~volume urine with relatively high osmolality. DI - high-volume HYPOTONIC urine.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A patient with pulmonary oedema treated with furosemide later cannot concentrate urine. Why does furosemide impair urine concentration. [QIMS 25]

options.A: It inhibits Nacl transport in the thick ascending limb, abolishing the medullary gradient

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loop diuretics block NKCC2 4 dissipate the medullary osmotic gradient 4 both concentrating and diluting abilities fall; side effects.. hypokalaemia, alkalosis, hypocalcaemia. ototoxicity.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A patient with renal medullary damage (analgesic nephropathy, sickle cell) passes large volumes of dilute urine. Damage to which structure reduces the ability to form concentrated urine? [BWP 26]

options.C: Renal medullary concentrating mechanism (loops, vasa recta)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Medullary injury disrupts countercurrent multiplication/exchange ￿ isosthenuria (urine fixed near 300 mOsm/L) - an early sign of CKD and sickle nephropathy.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.topicName: Genitourinary: Formation of Dilute and Concentrated Urine
mcqs.question: A physiology student measures interstitial osmolarity at different depths of the kidney. What is the osmolarity of the renal cortical interstitium. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cortex is isosmotic with plasma (~300 mOsm/L)." osmolarity rises progressively through the outer medulla to 1200- 1400 mOsm/L at the papillary tip (half Nacl, half urea).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with central diabetes insipidus is given desmopressin. At which site does ADH act? [Prof 24]

options.A: Descending limb of the loop of Henle
options.C: Late distal tubule and collecting duct

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ADH (V2 receptors on principal cells) -> cAMP -> insertion of AQP2 into the apical membrane of late distal tubule and collecting ducts; also increases urea permeability of the inner medullary collecting duct.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A dehydrated patient has very concentrated urine. Which hormone increases the facultative water permeability of the collecting ducts. [AMC 26. WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Obligatory water reabsorption: PCT and descending limb (~85%); facultative (ADH-dependent): collecting ducts (up to ~15%) - determines final urine volume.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher studies how ADH increases water permeability at the cellular level. ADH causes insertion of which channels into collecting~duct cells: [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: V2 -> Gs -> cAMP -> PKA -> AQP2 vesicle fusion with the apical membrane; water exits basolaterally via AQP3/AQP4. Nephrogenic DI: V2 or AQP2 mutation, lithium.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A severely dehydrated patient has low urine output. Increased secretion of which hormone explains this, and what is its renal effect? [HITEC 26 . KIMS 26] efferent dilatation

options.B: Antidiuretic hormone - increased water reabsorption by the collecting tubules

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dehydration -> increased plasma osmolality (osmoreceptors in the anterior hypothalamus, OVLT) and decreased volume (baroreceptors) -> ADH from the posterior pituitary -> small volume of concentrated urine.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After several hours outdoors on a hot day, a woman passes a very small volume of dark, concentrated urine. Which mechanism explains this. [KIMS 26]

options.A: Increased water permeability of the collecting duct

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sweat loss -> hyperosmolality -> ADH -> AQP2 insertion -> maximal water reabsorption in the collecting duct along the medullary gradient.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology student explains the regulation of plasma osmolarity. Which system mainly regulates ECF osmolarity. [WMC 25]

options.D: ADH with hypothalamic osmoreceptors (supraoptic/paraventricular nuclei) and thirst

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Osmoreceptor-ADH and thirst mechanisms keep osmolality ~285-295 mOsm/kg; a 1% rise triggers ADH release. Aldosterone mainly regulates ECF volume (Na+ content), not concentration.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient develops polyuria and serum sodium of 152 mmol/L after a head injury. Deficiency of which hormone is most likely? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Central DI after head trauma/pituitary surgery: dilute polyuria (urine osm < 300) with hypernatraemia if thirst/access to water is impaired; corrects with desmopressin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with a tumour of the posterior pituitary develops large urine volumes. What type of urine will be passed? [AMC 25]

options.A: Excessive volume of hypotonic urine (diabetes insipidus)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loss of ADH (synthesised in SON/PVN, stored in the posterior pituitary) -> central DI. Water deprivation test: urine stays dilute; responds to desmopressin (vs nephrogenic DI, which does not).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with central diabetes insipidus is started on a hormone analogue. Vasopressin analogues (desmopressin) are useful in treating: [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Desmopressin (V2-selective) treats central DI, nocturnal enuresis and haemophilia A/von Willebrand disease. Nephrogenic DI is treated with thiazides and low-salt diet.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has a mutation that reduces the sensitivity of renal tubules to ADH. What is the expected effect? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nephrogenic DI: high ADH levels but no response 4 polyuria of dilute urine, thirst, rising plasma osmolality; causes include V2 receptor (X-linked) or AQP2 mutations, lithium, hypercalcaemia, hypokalaemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 16-year-old has polyuria and polydipsia with glycosuria and blood glucose of 400 mg/dL. Polyuria and polydipsia with glycosuria are characteristic of which condition. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Both DM and DI cause polyuria/polydipsia," glycosuria and hyperglycaemia identify DM (osmotic diuresis). SIADH causes concentrated urine and hyponatraemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An elderly patient with weakness has urine Na" 600 mmol/L, urine osmolality 1200 mOsm/L, plasma Na" 167 mmol/L, high renin, very high ADH and raised aldosterone. What is the most likely reason for the hypernatraemia. [QIMS 25]

options.B: Dehydration caused by decreased fluid intake

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Maximally concentrated urine + appropriately high ADH, renin and aldosterone = hypovolaemic hypertonic dehydration (inadequate intake, common in the elderly with impaired thirst). Primary aldosteronism would suppress renin.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studying renal tubular cells notes that the basolateral Na"/K"_ATPase uses ATP directly to move ions against their gradients. Which type of transport is this. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary active transport uses ATP directly (Na'/K'_ATPase, H'_ATPase, H'/K'_ATPase, Ca"_ATPase). Secondary active uses the Na, gradient it creates (SGLT. NHE3, NKCC2).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with pulmonary oedema is given furosemide. Which part of the nephron does it act on and which transporter does it block? [Prof 24. AMC 26. HITEC 26. CKMC 26]

options.B: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle - Na'/K'/2CI- cotransporter

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loop diuretics (furosemide, bumetanide) block NKCC2 in the TAL - the most potent diuretics (the TAL reabsorbs ~25% of filtered Na,). Thiazides: NCC in early DCT. Amiloride: ENaC. Spironolactone: aldosterone receptor.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A hypertensive patient is started on hydrochlorothiazide. Which part of the nephron does it act on. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thiazides inhibit the Na'/CI- cotransporter (NCC) of the early DCT 4 mild diuresis; l urinary Ca" (used in stone formers), cause hypokalaemia. hyponatraemia, hyperuricaemia. hyperglycaemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient receives a diuretic that inhibits Nacl reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule. What is the expected effect on urine. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source recalled "increased output with relatively increased osmolarity" Blocking DCT Nacl reabsorption raises solute and water excretion; the DCT is part of the diluting segment, so diluting ability falls while modest diuresis follows.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with acute kidney injury develops hyponatraemia; the team checks hormonal regulation of Na". Which hormone primarily promotes Na. reabsorption in the distal nephron. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aldosterone (zona glomerulosa) acts on principal cells: t ENaC, t Na'/K'_ATPase, t ROMK 4 Na, reabsorption, K. and H. secretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with an adrenal adenoma has excess aldosterone. Which electrolyte pattern is most likely. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hyperaldosteronism." hypertension, hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis, mild hypernatraemia (aldosterone escape limits oedema). Low renin in primary (Conn's).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A medical student studies aldosterone's effect on urine composition. Aldosterone increases the urinary excretion of: [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aldosterone t Na, reabsorption (and water passively) and t K, and H, excretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman has BP 230/120 mmHg, hypokalaemia and low renin due to Conn's syndrome. Which hormone is responsible for her condition. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked renin. Conn's syndrome = primary hyperaldosteronism (adrenal adenoma/hyperplasia) with SUPPRESSED renin," high aldosterone:renin ratio is the screening test.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has primary aldosteronism (Conn's syndrome). Which zone of the adrenal cortex is involved? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cortex "salt. sugar, sex - the deeper you go, the sweeter it gets": glomerulosa - aldosterone; fasciculata - cortisol; reticularis androgens. Medulla - catecholamines.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 38-year-old woman with hyperpigmentation has low aldosterone and high ACTH. Which effect is most consistent with her condition. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency)." l aldosterone 4 natriuresis, hypovolaemia. hyperkalaemia. mild metabolic acidosis; T ACTH/MSH 4 pigmentation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic hypertension (and diabetes) is found to have high serum potassium. Which mechanism best explains the hyperkalaemia. [KIMS 25]

options.A: Decreased Na. reabsorption (and K, secretion) in the distal tubules
options.B: Increased RAAS activity due to low aldosterone effect

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hyporeninaemic hypoaldosteronism (type 4 RTA) in diabetic/hypertensive nephropathy, or ACE inhibitors/ARBs/K'_sparing diuretics, reduce distal Na. reabsorption and thus K. secretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man eats a high-potassium diet; plasma K" remains normal because renal excretion rises. Which nephron segment primarily increases K. secretion. [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]

options.B: Late distal tubule and cortical collecting duct (principal cells)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: K. filtered is mostly reabsorbed in the PCT and TAL regardless of intake," regulation occurs by SECREtION in principal cells of the late DCT and collecting ducts (stimulated by aldosterone, high plasma K., high flow and Na, delivery).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man doubles his dietary salt intake. What change in plasma potassium concentration generally follows? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: High Na. intake l aldosterone (tends to l K. secretion) but t distal flow and Na, delivery (tends to t K, secretion) - the effects cancel, so K, excretion and plasma K, stay stable.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with metabolic alkalosis develops hypokalaemia. Which mechanism causes potassium to fall? [BWP 26. QIMS 25]

options.D: Increased cellular uptake of K. (H. leaves cells) and increased renal K, secretion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alkalosis: H. moves out of cells in exchange for K, entering; high intracellular K, in principal cells increases K, secretion. Insulin, F2-agonists and alkalosis all shift K. into cells.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A nephrologist explains acid-base effects on renal potassium handling. Which disturbance increases renal K. secretion (and can lower plasma K,)? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked metabolic acidosis. Acute acidosis REDUCES K, secretion and shifts K. out of cells (hyperkalaemia); alkalosis increases K, secretion and causes hypokalaemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with hyperkalaemia from a crush injury is found to have a low arterial pH. Hyperkalaemia tends to cause which acid-base change. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: High plasma K. drives K. into cells and H. out, and impairs ammoniagenesis in the PCT 4 reduced acid excretion 4 metabolic acidosis (and vice versa: hypokalaemia ￿ alkalosis).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A newly diagnosed type I diabetic in DKA has serum K" 6.2 mmol/L despite total body potassium depletion. What causes the hyperkalaemia. [CKMC 26]

options.A: Insulin deficiency (and hyperosmolality) shifting K. out of cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin drives K, into cells via Na'/K'_ATPase; deficiency plus hyperosmolality (solvent drag) and acidosis move K, out, while osmotic diuresis depletes body K,.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Two hours after starting insulin infusion for DKA, the patient's potassium falls to 3.0 mmol/L. How does insulin cause hypokalaemia. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin stimulates Na'/K'_ATPase in muscle and liver ￿ K, enters cells; therefore K. must be monitored and replaced during DKA treatment.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old on a loop diuretic develops muscle weakness and U waves on ECG. Hypokalaemia is commonly associated with which acid-base disturbance. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypokalaemia and metabolic alkalosis coexist (vomiting. diuretics, hyperaldosteronism): K. depletion increases H. secretion and HCO, reabsorption, and alkalosis promotes K. loss.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher measures magnesium handling along the nephron. Which segment is the primary site of Mg" reabsorption. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Mg" ~65% in TAL (paracellular, claudin-16/19. driven by lumen-positive voltage), 20A PCT, IO% DCT (TRPM6). Loop diuretics cause hypomagnesaemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with recurrent renal stones, bone pain, hypercalcaemia and high PTH has increased urinary phosphate. Which nephron segment mediates PTH-induced phosphaturia. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PTH reduces NaPi-Ila/llc cotransporters in the PCT ￿ phosphaturia,. PTH increases Ca" reabsorption in the DCT (TRPV5) and stimulates la-hydroxylase in the PCT.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient is started on an SGLT2 inhibitor (blocks Na"_glucose cotransport in the proximal tubule). Which substance shows increased urinary excretion. [MUL 26]

options.D: Glucose (with Na. and water - osmotic diuresis)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source options/key (H,PO,-) were unclear. SGLT2 (Sl segment) reabsorbs - 90% of filtered glucose," gliflozins cause glycosuria, natriuresis and mild osmotic diuresis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with acute kidney injury after rhabdomyolysis develops peaked T waves. Which life-threatening electrolyte abnormality may occur in AKI? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AKI: I K, excretion + release from damaged cells + acidosis 4 hyperkalaemia; also hyperphosphataemia, hypocalcaemia, metabolic acidosis, fluid overload.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient in acute renal failure has a rising blood urea nitrogen. Why does BUN increase in acute renal failure? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Urea is freely filtered and partly reabsorbed," a fall in GFR reduces its excretion. In prerenal states, t tubular reabsorption raises the BUN:creatinine ratio above 20..1.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man has dizziness and low BP after severe vomiting; urea 50 mg/dL and creatinine 0.8 mg/dL. What is the most likely explanation. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Disproportionate rise in urea (BUN:Cr > 20) with hypovolaemia = prerenal; urine Na. < 20, FENa < 1%, concentrated urine. ATN." FENa > 2%, muddy brown casts.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with CKD has fatigue and weakness. Which mechanism most contributes to his fatigue. [KIMS 25]

options.B: Deficiency of erythropoietin leading to anaemia
options.C: Increased water reabsorption in the PCT

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CKD anaemia: l EPO from peritubular fibroblasts, plus iron deficiency, uraemic inhibition of marrow and shortened RBC survival - normocytic normochromic anaemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient on haemodialysis has the dialysate potassium kept low. Why is potassium kept low in dialysis fluid? [MUL 26]

options.C: To promote removal of K. from blood by diffusion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dialysate mimics normal plasma for Na., Ca" and HCO,- but contains low K, (0-3 mmol/L) and no urea/creatinine, so these diffuse out down their gradients.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During haemodialysis, the blood urea falls steadily. Which mechanism mainly reduces blood urea. [KIMS 26]

options.A: Diffusion of urea along its concentration gradient

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Small solutes cross the semipermeable dialysis membrane by DIFFUSION (countercurrent flow maximises gradients); water removal is by ultrafiltration (hydrostatic pressure).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child ingests a large dose of aspirin and breathes rapidly; hours later blood shows a high anion gap acidosis. What acid-base pattern does salicylate poisoning classically cause? [AMC 25 . CKMC 26]

options.C: Initially respiratory alkalosis, then metabolic acidosis

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Salicylates stimulate the medullary respiratory centre (early respiratory alkalosis) and uncouple oxidative phosphorylation (lactic and ketoacids high-AG metabolic acidosis); adults often have a mixed picture.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 20-year-old has a severe acute asthma attack with exhaustion and rising PCO,. Uncompensated respiratory acidosis may occur in which situation. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Acute hypoventilation (severe asthma, opioid overdose, airway obstruction) raises PCO, before renal compensation develops (takes 3-5 days); HCO,- rises only~1 mEq/L per 10 mmHg PCO, acutely.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: ABG in a patient: pH 7.33, PCO, 56 mmHg, PO, 65 mmHg, HCO,- 30 mEq/L. What is the primary acid-base disorder. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low pH with high PCO, respiratory acidosis; elevated HCO3 shows renal compensation (chronic." HCO,- T -3.5 per 10 mmHg PCO,).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: ABG: pH 7.32, PCO, 48 mmHg, HCO,- 25 mEq/L. What is the acid-base disorder? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Raised PCO2 explains the acidaemia and HCO3 IS Still normal ￿ acute (uncompensated) respiratory acidosis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A COPD patient has pH 7.32, PCO, 60 mmHg and HCO,- 29-30 mEq/L. What is the acid-base status. [MUL 26. KIMS 26]

options.A: Chronic respiratory acidosis with renal compensation

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCO, t 20 ￿ expected chronic HCO,- rise ~ 7 (24 4 31)," measured 29-30 fits chronic compensated respiratory acidosis (kidneys t H. secretion and HC03 generation).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old smoker with obstructive lung disease has acute breathlessness; ABG pH 7.22, PCO, 70 mmHg, HCO,- 22 mEq/L. What is the likely diagnosis. [BWP 26]

options.A: Respiratory acidosis due to COPD exacerbation

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Severe acidaemia with very high PCO2 and no HCO3 rise = acute (decompensated) respiratory acidosis - the HCO3 of 22 suggests a superimposed mild metabolic acidosis may also be present.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic bronchitis is drowsy. ABG pH 7.29, PCO, 58, HCO,- 27. What is the diagnosis. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CO2 narcosis: hypercapnia causes drowsiness, flapping tremor and headache (cerebral vasodilatation). Avoid high-flow 02 in CO2 retainers.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A young man comatose after an unknown dose of sleeping pills has pH 7.02, HCO,- 14 mEq/L and PCO, 68 mmHg. How is his acid-base status best described? [QIMS 25]

options.D: Respiratory acidosis with complete renal compensation

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: High PCO, (hypoventilation) AND low HCO,- (lactic acidosis from hypoxia/shock) both lower pH - a mixed disorder produces extreme acidaemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student faints during an examination after anxious overbreathing; ABG shows low PCO2 and high pH. What is the likely cause. [HITEC 26. HITEC 25]

options.D: Hyperventilation due to anxiety (acute respiratory alkalosis)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hyperventilation blows off CO, ￿ respiratory alkalosis ￿ cerebral vasoconstriction (dizziness, syncope) and l ionised Ca" (perioral tingling, carpopedal spasm).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 20-year-old develops light-headedness and tingling fingers while hyperventilating; ABG pH 7.55, PCO, 28, HCO,- 24. What is the disorder? [QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alkalaemia with low PCO2 and normal HCO, acute uncompensated respiratory alkalosis. Treat the cause (panic, pain. PE, hypoxia, salicylates, sepsis).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A mountaineer arrives at 4000 m altitude. What is the immediate respiratory response. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low PO2 Stimulates carotid bodies 4 hyperventilation 4 respiratory alkalosis: over days the kidneys excrete HCO,- (acetazolamide accelerates acclimatisation).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with type I diabetes has vomiting, dehydration and deep breathing; ABG pH 7.22, Paco, 24, HCO,- 10. What is the disturbance. [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]

options.B: Primary metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation
options.D: Primary respiratory alkalosis with renal compensation

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Winter's formula: expected PCO, = 1.5 x HCO,- + 8 + 2 = 23 + 2 ￿ appropriate respiratory compensation (Kussmaul breathing) for DKA.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has ABG pH 7.10, PCO, 38 mmHg and HCO,- 15 mEq/L. What is the disorder? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low pH and HCO, metabolic acidosis. Expected PCO, 1.5 x 15 + 8 = 30.5," a PCO2 of 38 is too high 4 concomitant respiratory acidosis (failing compensation).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with profuse diarrhoea has pH 7.28, PCO, 30 mmHg, HCO, 16 mEq/L. What is the most likely interpretation? [KIMS 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Diarrhoea loses HCO, normal anion gap (hyperchloraemic) metabolic acidosis," hyperventilation lowers PCO, (compensation is never complete).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has pH 7.13, HCO, 15 mEq/L, CI- 118 mEq/L, Na" 141 mEq/L, with low PCO,. What is the most likely cause of his acidosis. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anion gap = 141- (118 + 15) = 8 (normal) with hyperchloraemia ￿ Gl HCO,- loss (diarrhoea) or RTA. DKA gives a high anion gap.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A hospitalised patient has had profuse diarrhoea for 4 hours and is hypovolaemic. Which laboratory result best fits. IQIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Acute diarrhoea: low pH, low HCO, , slightly reduced PCO, (early respiratory compensation).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child with severe diarrhoea is breathing rapidly and deeply. Which respiratory response helps maintain blood pH? [KIMS 26 . MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Respiratory compensation for metabolic acidosis: chemoreceptors sense t H. 4 hyperventilation 4 I PCO, 4 l H,CO,. raising pH within minutes to hours.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with gastric outlet obstruction vomits repeatedly for several days. Which acid-base disorder most commonly results. [MUL 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loss of HCI ￿ HCO,- retained; volume depletion ( t aldosterone) and hypokalaemia maintain the alkalosis ￿ hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis with paradoxical aciduria.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with prolonged vomiting has ABG pH 7.50, HCO,- 35 mEq/L and PCO, 45 mmHg. What is the most likely disorder. IQIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: High pH and HCO, metabolic alkalosis; PCO, rises by~0. 7 mmHg per I mEq/L HCO,- as compensation (hypoventilation, limited by hypoxia).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with nausea, rapid breathing and low HCO3 is evaluated. Rapid (Kussmaul) breathing with nausea is associated with which acid-base disorder. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Deep sighing (Kussmaul) respiration is the compensatory response to metabolic acidosis (DKA, uraemia, lactic acidosis); nausea and vomiting are common accompaniments.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has an acid-base report showing I pH, I HCO3 and a compensatory I PCO,. What does this pattern indicate. [HITEC 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rule." if pH and PCO2 move in the SAME direction ￿ metabolic primary; if OPPOSITE ￿ respiratory primary.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient's ABG shows I PCO2 and t pH due to hyperventilation. What does this indicate. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: pH up, PCO, down (opposite directions) 4 primary respiratory alkalosis. Chronic compensation." HCO,- falls~4-5 per 10 mmHg PCO, drop.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient in chronic diabetic ketoacidosis is studied by a renal physiologist. Which pattern would you expect? [QIMS 25]

options.A: Increased HCO3 production with decreased anion gap plasma anion gap
options.B: Decreased renal HCO3 excretion, increased NH4 excretion, increased
options.C: Increased NH4 excretion with increased urine pH

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Kidneys compensate for metabolic acidosis by reabsorbing all filtered HCO,-, increasing titratable acid and markedly increasing NH,, excretion (glutamine metabolism); ketoanions raise the anion gap.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In metabolic acidosis, the proximal tubule secretes large amounts of H". With which process are most of the H. ions secreted by the proximal tubule associated? [QIMS 25]

options.D: Excretion of K. ~80_90AO of H. secreted by the PCT (via NHE3) combines with filtered HCO,- (carbonic

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note: the source key marked "excretion of hydrogen ions" anhydrase) 4 HCO3 reabsorption: new HCO3 is generated by NH4 and titratable acid excretion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist explains how non-volatile acids (sulphuric, phosphoric) from protein metabolism are handled. How are H. ions from non-volatile acids primarily buffered and eliminated? [HITEC 26]

options.C: Bicarbonate buffering and increased renal acid excretion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fixed acids (~1 mEq/kg/day) are immediately buffered by HCO,-; the kidneys then excrete the H, (as NH4 and titratable acid) and regenerate HCO,-

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A renal biopsy study looks at collecting-duct intercalated cells. What is the major acid-base function of a-intercalated cells. [HITEC 26]

options.D: Secrete H. into the tubular lumen (H'.ATPase, H'/K'_ATPase)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: a-intercalated cells: apical H'_ATPase and H"/K'_ATPase, basolateral Cl-/HCO3 exchanger (AEI) 4 acidify urine, reabsorb K". Defects 4 distal (type I) RTA.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In metabolic alkalosis, collecting-duct cells excrete the excess base. What is the function of F-intercalated cells. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: F-intercalated cells are the mirror image: apical pendrin secretes HCO,-, basolateral H'_ATPase - active in alkalosis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A medical student records a neuronal action potential from a resting potential of -70 MV that overshoots to about +30 mv. What is the approximate amplitude of a typical neuronal action potential? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: I: Action potential." resting -70 to -90 MV ￿ overshoot +20 to +40 MV ￿ amplitude = 100- 120 mv; due to voltage-gated Na, influx then K, efflux. (Reconstructed item.)

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old on antihypertensives feels dizzy every time he stands up from bed. Which bedside examination is most appropriate. [LHR 26]

options.A: Measurement of blood pressure lying and standing

mcqs.explanation: Orthostatic hypotension." fall of > 20 mmHg systolic or > 10 mmHg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing," causes include hypovolaemia, drugs, autonomic neuropathy (diabetes).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A textile-mill worker exposed to loud noise for years has high-frequency sensorineural deafness. Which structures are damaged? [BWP 25]

options.A: Hair cells of the organ of Corti (cochlear trauma/noise)

mcqs.explanation: Exa Noise-induced hearing loss damages outer hair cells of the basal cochlea first (4 kHz notch on audiometry). (Block 6 topic asked in a Block 4 paper.) BIOCHEMISTRY

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student chews a piece of bread for a long time and notices it starts to taste sweet as starch breaks down in the mouth. Which enzyme is responsible? [Prof 24 . KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Salivary a-amylase hydrolyses a-1.4 glycosidic bonds of starch 4 maltose, maltotriose and a-limit dextrins; optimum pH 6.8, inactivated by gastric acid. Lingual lipase starts fat digestion.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on long-term proton pump inhibitors has poor protein digestion. What is the main digestive role of hydrochloric acid in the stomach? [Prof 24. KIMS 25 . BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: HCI: converts pepsinogen ￿ pepsin (autocatalytic below pH 5), denatures proteins, kills microbes, helps iron (Fe" ￿ Fe") and B12 release from food proteins.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old with epigastric pain at night relieved by antacids is told his gastric acid rises after meals. Which hormone is the most potent stimulator of gastric acid secretion after eating. [KIMS 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gastrin (released by peptides, amino acids, distension. vagal GRP) 4 ECL histamine 4 parietal cells. Histamine (H2), Ach (M3) and gastrin act synergistically," somatostatin inhibits.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient has steatorrhoea after a problem with bile flow; a student asks which digestive juice contains no digestive enzymes. Which secretion does not contain any enzymes? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bile contains bile salts, phospholipids, cholesterol, bilirubin and HCO,- but NO digestive enzymes - it emulsifies fat and forms micelles.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with defective bile production has bulky pale stools. Digestion of which nutrient is mainly impaired? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bile salts emulsify fat and form mixed micelles that carry monoglycerides, fatty acids and fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) to the brush border steatorrhoea and vitamin K deficiency if absent.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains how dietary fat is digested and absorbed in the small intestine. Which secretions are essential for fat digestion. [HITEC 25]

options.D: Bile salts and pancreatic lipase (with colipase)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bile salts emulsify and expose surface,. colipase anchors pancreatic lipase to the emulsion droplet," products enter micelles 4 enterocytes re-esterified ￿ chylomicrons 4 lymph.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with Crohn's disease of the ileum has fat malabsorption due to loss of bile salts. Which process is essential for efficient absorption of dietary lipids? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Micelles (bile salts + phospholipids + lipid digestion products) solubilise lipids in the unstirred water layer; bile salts are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum (enterohepatic circulation).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An obese patient is started on orlistat and develops oily stools. What is its mechanism of action. [Prof 24. CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Orlistat covalently inhibits gastric and pancreatic lipases 4 -30% of dietary fat is excreted; side effects: steatorrhoea, faecal urgency. fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 12-year-old with cystic f ibrosis has steatorrhoea and poor weight gain despite adequate intake. Deficiency of which pancreatic enzyme is the main cause. [KIMS 25. CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CF: thick secretions block pancreatic ducts 4 exocrine insufficiency; lipase deficiency causes steatorrhoea first (no alternative lipase source, unlike amylase/proteases).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains protein digestion beyond the stomach. Which enzyme digests proteins in the small intestine. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pancreatic proteases." trypsin, chymotrypsin, elastase (endopeptidases), carboxypeptidases A and B (exopeptidases),. brush-border aminopeptidases and dipeptidases complete digestion.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A person develops bloating and diarrhoea after drinking skim milk but tolerates yogurt. Which enzyme deficiency is most likely. [CKMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lactase (brush border F-galactosidase) declines after weaning in most populations; undigested lactose 4 osmotic diarrhoea and colonic fermentation (gas, bloating. T breath hydrogen). Yogurt bacteria predigest lactose.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemistry practical tests the action of brush~border sucrase on table sugar. Into which products does sucrase convert sucrose? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Disaccharidases: sucrase 4 glucose + fructose; lactase ￿ glucose + galactose," maltase ￿ 2 glucose," isomaltase cleaves a- 1,6 bonds of limit dextrins.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains the end products of carbohydrate digestion that are absorbed. After complete digestion, carbohydrates are broken down into: [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Only monosaccharides (glucose, galactose, fructose) are absorbed: glucose/galactose via SGLTI (Na'_dependent), frurtose via GLUT5.' all exit via GLUT2.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with glucose-galactose malabsorption has severe diarrhoea; fructose is tolerated. Which transporter absorbs glucose and galactose from the lumen. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SGLTI (2 Na. secondary active transport," oral rehydration solution exploits it (glucose enhances Na. and water absorption). I glucose)

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A physiologist records a lumen-negative potential during glucose absorption in the jejunum. Sodium-glucose cotransport in the small intestine is: [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SGLTI carries net positive charge (2 Na.) into the cell ￿ electrogenic secondary active transport, driven by the Na. gradient of the basolateral Na'/K'_ATPase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An infant has seizures, developmental delay and low CSF glucose with normal blood glucose due to a transporter defect. Which organ is most affected by GLUTI deficiency. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GLUTI carries glucose across the blood-brain barrier (and into RBCS); deficiency ￿ hypoglycorrhachia, seizures - treated with a ketogenic diet (ketones use MCTI).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies passive transport of solutes across cell membranes. On which property does diffusion of a substance across a membrane partly depend? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fick's law: rate concentration gradient x surface area x permeability (lipid solubility, small size) - membrane thickness.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies the end products of nucleic acid digestion in the intestine. What are the final products absorbed? [HITEC 25]

options.A: Nucleosides and free bases (plus pentoses and phosphate)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pancreatic nucleases 4 nucleotides 4 brush-border nucleotidases and phosphatases 4 nucleosides 4 nucleosidases 4 bases + pentose. Most purines are degraded to uric acid in enterocytes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks what stimulates the intestinal glands to secrete succus entericus. Which factor increases secretion from the crypts of Lieberkuhn. [AMC 25]

options.B: Secretin (and local enteric reflexes from distension)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Intestinaljuice (- 1.8 L/day) is driven mainly by local enteric reflexes to tactile/irritative stimuli; secretin and CCK (and VIP) increase it.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with gallstones is told a hormone released when fatty food enters the duodenum stimulates gallbladder contraction. Which hormone is this. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CCK (I cells): gallbladder contraction, sphincter of Oddi relaxation, pancreatic enzyme secretion, inhibits gastric emptying, satiety via vagal afferents.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Gastric emptying slows after a fatty meal because of a duodenal hormone. Delayed gastric emptying is caused mainly by which substance. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CCK is the strongest hormonal brake on gastric emptying (with secretin and GIP); enterokinase activates trypsinogen.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old woman with Crohn's disease of the terminal ileum has fatigue, glossitis and tingling feet. Which vitamin deficiency is most likely. [MUL 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: B12-intrinsic factor complex is absorbed only in the terminal ileum (cubilin receptor): ileal disease/resection 4 macrocytic anaemia with hypersegmented neutrophils + subacute combined degeneration. Liver stores last 3-5 years.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with pernicious anaemia has vitamin B12 def iciency. Which substance is essential for B12 absorption, and where is the complex absorbed? [AMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dietary B12 binds haptocorrin (R protein) in the stomach 4 released by pancreatic proteases in the duodenum 4 binds intrinsic factor 4 absorbed in the terminal ileum.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 56-year-old woman has fatigue and a smooth red tongue; Hb and vitamin B12 are low with antibodies to gastric cells. What explains the biochemical defect? [QIMS 25]

options.A: Failure of parietal cells to secrete intrinsic factor

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pernicious anaemia: autoimmune destruction of parietal cells and anti-IF antibodies 4 B12 malabsorption," treat with lifelong IM hydroxocobalamin.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on methotrexate for leukaemia develops mouth ulcers and megaloblastic marrow changes. Which enzyme is directly inhibited by methotrexate. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Methotrexate inhibits DHFR ￿ no tetrahydrofolate regeneration ￿ I dTMP and purine synthesis. Rescue with folinic acid (leucovorin), which bypasses DHFR.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares hepatic bile with gallbladder bile. In gallbladder bile, the concentration of which substance is DECREASED compared with hepatic bile? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked protein. The gallbladder actively absorbs Na. with Cl-/HCO,- and water, concentrating bile salts, cholesterol, lecithin and bilirubin 5-20x; Guyton lists Na. 145 4 130, CI- 100 4 25, HCO,- 28 4 10 mEq/L.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies gallstone formation and the solubility of cholesterol in bile. What is the approximate normal ratio of cholesterol to bile salts in bile: [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cholesterol stays dissolved when bile salts + lecithin are in excess (~1:20 to 1."30 cholesterol.bile salt). A lower ratio (lithogenic bile) favours cholesterol crystals.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 58-year-old woman with jaundice, dark urine and pruritus has an obstructed common bile duct on ultrasound. Which serum enzyme is most suggestive of this condition. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cholestasis: t t ALP and GGT (canalicular enzymes induced by bile); hepatocellular injury: t t ALT/AST. ALP also rises in bone disease - GGT confirms hepatic origin.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old with long-standing liver cirrhosis has oedema and drug toxicity. Which biochemical change is characteristic of cirrhosis. [HITEC 25]

options.B: Decreased albumin synthesis and detoxification capacity

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cirrhosis: l albumin (oedema, ascites), I clotting factors ( t PT/INR), l urea synthesis ( t ammonia 4 encephalopathy), I drug metabolism, t bilirubin.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with Wilson disease has low serum levels of a copper-containing plasma protein. Which of these is a metalloprotein. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ceruloplasmin (a2-globulin) carries-90A of plasma copper and has ferroxidase activity. Wilson disease (ATP7B): I ceruloplasmin, t urinary copper, Kayser-Fleischer rings, liver and basal ganglia damage.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with bronze skin, diabetes and cirrhosis is diagnosed with haemochromatosis. Which laboratory value is raised? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hereditary haemochromatosis." t ferritin, t serum iron, transferrin saturation > 45%, 1 TIBC,. treated by venesection.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: The haemochromatosis patient has an HFE gene (C282Y) mutation. How does this cause iron overload? [Prof 24]

options.C: Inappropriately increased intestinal iron absorption (low hepcidin)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: HFE mutation ￿ I hepcidin ￿ ferroportin stays active on enterocytes and macrophages ￿ unregulated duodenal iron absorption 4 deposition in liver, pancreas, heart, skin. pituitary.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old smoker has early-onset emphysema and a low al-globulin band on serum electrophoresis. Which protein is deficient? [Prof 24. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: al-antitrypsin (serine protease inhibitor from the liver) protects alveoli from neutrophil elastase; deficiency 4 PANACINAR emphysema (lower lobes) and liver cirrhosis (misfolded Piz protein retained in hepatocytes).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old alcoholic has recurrent epigastric pain radiating to the back, steatorrhoea and weight loss for two years; X-ray shows pancreatic calcification. What is the likely diagnosis. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chronic pancreatitis: alcohol is the commonest cause: triad of pain, calcification and exocrine (steatorrhoea)/endocrine (diabetes) insufficiency,. faecal elastase is low.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient's duodenal pH stays low after meals because bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice is not released. Which hormone normally triggers bicarbonate-rich pancreatic secretion? [BWP 26 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Secretin (the first hormone discovered, 1902) ￿ ductal HCO,- secretion via cAMP/CFTR,. CCK ￿ acinar enzymes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient replaces saturated fats with oils whose fatty acids contain one double bond (e.g. olive oil). Which type of fat is being consumed? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MUFA (oleic acid - olive, canola oil) and PUFA (linoleic w-6. a-linolenic CL)-3) lower LDL; trans fats (partially hydrogenated oils) raise LDL and lower HDL.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A dietitian recommends low-Gl foods to a diabetic patient. What does the glycaemic index of a food indicate? [AMC 26]

options.A: Its blood glucose response compared with a reference food (glucose/white bread)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gl = area under the 2-h glucose curve for 50 g available carbohydrate - that of glucose x ICK). Low Gl < 55, high > 70. Glycaemic load = Gl x carbohydrate per serving/lOO.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic patient eats lentils (low glycaemic index) instead of white rice. What is the effect of a Iow-Gl food? [HITEC 25]

options.C: Slow, gradual rise in blood glucose

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low-Gl foods (high fibre, intact grains, legumes. fat/protein co-ingestion) are digested slowly -> smaller postprandial glucose and insulin peaks, better glycaemic control and satiety.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A nutrition lecture defines the intake meeting the needs of 97_98% of healthy individuals of a given age and sex. Which term is this? [AMC 26. MUL 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: RDA = EAR + 2 SD (covers 97.5%). EAR meets the needs of 50% of a group," Al is used when data are insufficient for an RDA; UL is the maximum safe intake.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A public health nutritionist plans and assesses the adequacy of intakes in a whole population. For what purpose is the Estimated Average Requirement (EAR) used? [AMC 25]

options.A: To plan an individual clinical diet
options.B: To determine the tolerable upper intake
options.C: To analyse and plan population (group) intakes

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: EAR (meets the requirement of half the population) is used to assess prevalence of inadequate intakes in groups and to derive the RDA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A dietitian asks a healthy adult to keep protein intake at the recommended level. What is the approximate RDA for protein in a normal adult? [QIMS 25]

options.A: About 0.8-1 g/kg body weight per day

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Protein RDA ~ 0.8 g/kg/day for adults (higher in pregnancy, lactation. growth, illness-l- 1.5 g/kg). Should provide~10- 15% of energy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A nutritionist evaluates protein quality using the Protein Digestibility Corrected Amino Acid Score (PDCAAS). What is its upper limit? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PDCAAS = limiting amino acid score x true digestibility, truncated at 1.0 (casein, egg white. whey, soy ~ l). Wheat ~ 0.4 (limited by lysine).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A vegetarian is advised to obtain adequate essential amino acids. Which of these is an essential amino acid? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Essential.. PVT TIM HaLL - Phenylalanine, Valine, Threonine, Tryptophan, Isoleucine, Methionine, Histidine, Leucine, Lysine (arginine conditionally). Tyrosine is made from phenylalanine.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks about the recommended share of daily energy from fat in a balanced diet. What percentage of daily calories should come from fat? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AMDR: carbohydrate 45-65%. fat 20-35% (saturated < IO%, trans fat minimal), protein 10-35% of energy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
