mcqs.question: A dietitian counsels a patient on dietary fibre. What is the recommended daily dietary fibre intake for an adult? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fibre: soluble (oats, pectin - lowers cholesterol and glucose) and insoluble (bran - adds bulk, prevents constipation/diverticular disease).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient fasting for surgery is given dextrose infusion; the surgeon explains that carbohydrate reduces muscle breakdown. What is this effect of carbohydrate called? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Adequate carbohydrate/energy intake means amino acids are not diverted to gluconeogenesis or oxidation ￿ protein is spared for tissue synthesis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A physiologist measures energy expenditure in a resting, awake, post-absorptive subject. Which statement best describes resting metabolic rate (RMR)? [MUL 26]

options.A: Lower per kg in children than adults
options.B: Energy required to maintain vital functions at rest
options.C: About equal to total daily energy expenditure
options.D: Higher per kg in women than men

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: RMR/BMR accounts for~60-70A of total energy expenditure," thermic effect of food~IOA; physical activity the rest. BMR = I kcal/kg/h (24 kcal/kg/day).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A physiology class compares basal metabolic rate between groups. In which group is BMR higher. [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: BMR is higher in men (more lean muscle), children (per kg - growth), cold climates, fever, hyperthyroidism, pregnancy; lower in women, elderly, starvation, hypothyroidism, sleep.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with weight loss, heat intolerance and tremor has a raised BMR. Which condition increases basal metabolic rate. [HITEC 26. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thyroid hormones T Na'/K'_ATPase activity, mitochondrial number and uncoupling 4 BMR rises up to 60- IOOA in thyrotoxicosis; falls 40-50% in myxoedema.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 5.4-ft, 50-kg woman doing light work needs-2140 kcal/day; she joins a football team with moderate-to-heavy activity. What is her approximate new daily energy requirement? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Energy requirement = BMR x physical activity level (PAL): sedentary 1.4-1.5, light- 1.6, moderate - 1.8, heavy > 2.0. Raising PAL from - 1.6 to -2.0 adds-25-40%.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher measures the respiratory quotient while a subject oxidises only fat. What is the RQ of fat? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: RQ = CO2 produced/O2 consumed: carbohydrate 1.0, protein ~0.8, fat-0. 7, mixed diet-0.8; > 1.0 indicates net lipogenesis (overfeeding).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student measures gas exchange in a person eating a normal mixed diet. What is the respiratory quotient of a mixed diet? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the source key marked 0. 7 (the RQ of fat) and did not list 0.8. A typical mixed diet gives RQ ~ 0.82.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During a community screening programme, a 40-year-old man has a BMI of 34 kg/m'. Why do clinicians use BMI in health assessment? [QIMS 25]

options.B: To identify individuals with weight problems (underweight/ovenNeight/obesity)
options.C: To calculate exact lean body mass

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: BMI = weight (kg)/height' (m,): < 18.5 underweight. 18.5-24. 9 normal. 25~29.9 overweight, > 30 obese (Asian cut-offs 23 and 27.5). It does not distinguish fat from muscle.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with a BMI of 32 and a sedentary lifestyle asks for dietary advice. Which recommendation is best? [KIMS 26]

options.A: Reduce caloric intake and increase fibre (with more activity)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sustainable weight loss: energy deficit of ~500-600 kcal/day, high-fibre, low energy-density foods, plus 150-300 min/week of activity 4 ~0.5 kg/week loss.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An obese student feels hungry before meals; a circulating hormone from the stomach rises during fasting. Which hormone stimulates appetite. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ghrelin (gastric fundus) 4 hypothalamic NPY/AgRP neurons 4 hunger. Leptin (adipocytes), CCK, PYY, GLP-I and insulin promote satiety.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 4-year-old boy fed mainly polished rice has swollen feet, irritability, sparse light-coloured hair, fatty liver and low serum albumin. Which condition is most likely? [QIMS 25 . HITEC 25 . HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Kwashiorkor: protein deficiency with relatively adequate calories 4 l albumin (oedema), fatty liver ( l apolipoprotein synthesis), flaky-paint dermatosis, flag sign of hair. apathy. Marasmus." severe wasting. no oedema.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A malnourished child has oedema, a distended abdomen and fatty liver. Which plasma protein is low in kwashiorkor. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low albumin reduces plasma oncotic pressure 4 oedema," reduced apoB-100 synthesis impairs VLDL export 4 fatty liver.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A paediatrician asks when kwashiorkor typically develops. Kwashiorkor usually occurs during: [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: "Kwashiorkor" (Ga language) = the disease of the displaced child when a new sibling arrives and the older child is weaned onto a starchy, protein-poor diet (1-4 years).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 14-month-old child has poor weight gain, visible ribs, reduced muscle mass, loose wrinkled skin and NO oedema. What is the diagnosis. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Marasmus: severe energy (and protein) deficiency ￿ loss of fat and muscle, "old-man" face, alert and hungry. no oedema, normal albumin. Marasmic kwashiorkor has both wasting and oedema.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A pregnant woman in the second trimester has pallor, fatigue and breathlessness. Which nutrient intake most needs to be increased? [KIMS 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Iron requirement rises to~27 mg/day in pregnancy (fetal stores, expanded RBC mass, placenta); iron deficiency is the commonest cause of anaemia in pregnancy - supplement with folic acid.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient recovering from major illness receives adequate nutrition and rebuilds muscle. What nitrogen balance is present? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Positive N balance: growth, pregnancy, recovery, bodybuilding. Negative: starvation, trauma, burns, sepsis, uncontrolled diabetes, essential amino acid deficiency.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on a prolonged fast loses muscle mass. In which condition does negative nitrogen balance occur. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: In starvation, muscle protein is broken down for gluconeogenesis. so nitrogen excretion exceeds intake.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with hepatic encephalopathy is counselled about diet to reduce nitrogenous waste. Which dietary substance has traditionally been restricted? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Clinical note (from source): routine severe protein restriction is no longer recommended - it worsens malnutrition; adequate protein (1.2-1.5 g/kg) with lactulose/rifaximin is preferred.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with decompensated cirrhosis has tense ascites. Which dietary modification is most important? [AMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ascites is driven by renal Na" retention (secondary hyperaldosteronism),. dietary Na. restriction (-2 g/88 mmol per day) plus spironolactone + furosemide is first-line therapy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic kidney disease and hyperkalaemia is given dietary advice. Which food is a rich natural source of potassium that may need restriction. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: High-K' foods: dates. dried fruits. bananas, potatoes, tomatoes, oranges, coconut water, nuts; leaching/boiling vegetables reduces K" content.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A breastfed infant has fewer gut infections; a milk protein binds iron so bacteria cannot use it. Which milk protein has antibacterial activity. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Breast-milk protective factors: secretory IgA, lactoferrin (iron sequestration), lysozyme, bifidus factor, oligosaccharides, leukocytes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemistry student draws a polypeptide chain and labels the bond joining adjacent amino acids. Which bond maintains the primary structure of a protein. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary structure = amino-acid sequence held by covalent peptide bonds (planar, partial double-bond, trans). Secondary - backbone H-bonds; tertiary - side-chain interactions (disulphide, ionic, hydrophobic, H-bonds); quaternary - subunit association.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies a protein segment in which hydrogen bonds between backbone C=0 and N-H groups form a right-handed coil (3.6 residues per turn). Which level of structure is the a-helix. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Secondary structures: a-helix, F-pleated sheet, F-turns - stabilised by backbone hydrogen bonds. Proline breaks helices.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A hair-straightening chemical (thioglycolate) breaks the disulphide bonds of keratin. Which level of protein structure is mainly affected? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Disulphide bridges between cysteine side chains stabilise TERTIARY (and inter-chain quaternary) structure; perming breaks and re-forms them.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: The O,-binding function of myoglobin depends on how its single polypeptide chain folds into a compact globule around heme. Which level of structure is this. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Myoglobin has only one chain, so its highest level is tertiary." haemoglobin (a2F2) has quaternary structure, giving cooperative O, binding and the sigmoid curve.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher studies heat-shock proteins that help newly synthesised polypeptides fold correctly. How do molecular chaperones assist protein folding? [HITEC 26. HITEC 25]

options.B: By preventing inappropriate interactions and aggregation of unfolded chains
options.C: By degrading all misfolded proteins immediately

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chaperones (Hsp70, Hsp60/chaperonins) bind exposed hydrophobic regions and use ATP to allow correct folding; failure ￿ misfolding diseases (Alzheimer, prion disease, al-antitrypsin deficiency).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 72-year-old woman has progressive memory loss and confusion for two years; MRI shows cortical atrophy. Which misfolded protein forms the extracellular plaques in this condition. [QIMS 25 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alzheimer disease: extracellular amyloid-F plaques (from APP cleavage, F-pleated sheets) and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles of hyperphosphorylated tau. Parkinson's - a-synuclein (Lewy bodies).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child's nappies turn black on standing in air; he later develops dark ear cartilage and arthritis. Which enzyme is deficient in alkaptonuria. [HITEC 26. HITEC 25. WMC 25. BWP 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alkaptonuria (autosomal recessive).. homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase deficiency 4 homogentisic acid accumulates 4 urine darkens on standing (oxidation), ochronosis, arthritis. Nitisinone reduces production.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient develops dark urine on standing due to an inborn error of aromatic amino acid catabolism. Defective degradation of which amino acid is associated with alkaptonuria? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Phenylalanine 4 (PAH) tyrosine 4 p-hydroxyphenylpyruvate 4 homogentisate 4 (HGD) maleylacetoacetate 4 fumarate + acetoacetate. Alkaptonuria blocks tyrosine degradation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A newborn with vomiting, eczema, fair skin and a musty (mousy) urine odour has a positive Guthrie test. Which enzyme is deficient in classic phenylketonuria? [WMC 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Classic PKU.. PAH deficiency (or BH4 deficiency in variants) 4 t phenylalanine and phenylketones 4 intellectual disability if untreated,. tyrosine becomes essential,. I melanin (fair).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A girl with phenylketonuria asks which artificial sweetener to avoid in soft drinks. Which sweetener should she avoid? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aspartame = aspartyl-phenylalanine methyl ester 4 releases phenylalanine; products carry a "contains phenylalanine" warning.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A young woman has hypopigmented patches; testing shows impaired melanin synthesis. Which enzyme catalyses the rate-limiting first step of melanin production. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tyrosinase (copper enzyme in melanocytes): tyrosine 4 DOPA 4 dopaquinone 4 melanin. Deficiency = oculocutaneous albinism type l.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An infant has failure to thrive, liver failure and a cabbage-like urine odour. With which disorder is cabbage-like odour classically associated? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Urine odours: cabbage/boiled cabbage - tyrosinaemia type l (fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase deficiency)," mousy - PKU; maple syrup/burnt sugar MSUD; sweaty feet - isovaleric acidaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 5-day-old newborn has poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy and seizures, with elevated leucine, isoleucine and valine and sweet-smelling urine. What is the diagnosis and deficient enzyme. [KIMS 26. KIMS 25. HITEC 25]

options.A: Maple syrup urine disease - branched-chain a-ketoacid

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MSUD: BCKAD complex deficiency (needs thiamine. lipoate. COA. FAD. NAD) ￿ branched-chain a-ketoacids accumulate 4 encephalopathy, cerebral oedema. Leucine is the most neurotoxic.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A tall boy with lens dislocation (downward), osteoporosis and thrombosis has high plasma homocysteine. Deficiency of which enzyme causes homocysteine to accumulate. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Classic homocystinuria." CBS deficiency (B6-dependent) ￿ t homocysteine and methionine, I cystine; some respond to pyridoxine. Homocysteine also rises in B12/folate deficiency (methionine synthase).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child has recurrent renal stones; urine shows hexagonal crystals and excess cystine, ornithine, lysine and arginine. Which disorder causes excretion of these amino acids, including sulphur-containing cystine. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cystinuria: defective dibasic amino-acid transporter (SLC3AI/SLC7A9) in PCT and gut - "COLA" (Cystine, Ornithine, Lysine, Arginine); cystine is insoluble 4 stones (positive cyanide-nitroprusside test).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies which amino acid gives proteins buffering capacity at physiological pH. Which amino acid acts as a buffer near pH 7.4? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Histidine's imidazole side chain has a pKa near physiological pH 4 main buffering group of haemoglobin and plasma proteins.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student classifies amino acids by the products of their carbon skeletons. Which amino acid is purely ketogenic. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Purely ketogenic: leucine and lysine (yield acetyl-CoA/acetoacetate only). Both ketogenic and glucogenic: phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan, isoleucine, threonine. All others are glucogenic.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student traces amino-acid carbon skeletons that enter the TCA cycle as succinyl-CoA. Which amino acid can be degraded to succinyl-CoA? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Succinyl-CoA formers: methionine, valine, isoleucine, threonine (via propionyl-CoA 4 methylmalonyl-CoA, B12-dependent mutase) - MVIT"

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies conversion of noradrenaline to adrenaline in the adrenal medulla. Which cofactor donates the methyl group in this reaction. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PNMT uses SAM (induced by cortisol from the cortex). SAM is the universal methyl donor (creatine. phosphatidylcholine, melatonin. DNA methylation) 4 becomes S-adenosylhomocysteine.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks which amino acid acts as the main collector of amino groups in transamination. Which amino acid is central to transamination. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aminotransferases (ALT, AST,. PLP-dependent) transfer amino groups to a-ketoglutarate 4 glutamate," glutamate dehydrogenase then releases NH, for the urea cycle. Lysine and threonine do not transaminate.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies how ammonia from muscle reaches the liver during prolonged exercise. In what form is ammonia mainly transported from muscle to liver. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Muscle: pyruvate + glutamate 4 alanine (ALT) 4 liver: alanine 4 pyruvate (gluconeogenesis) + NH, (urea). Most other tissues and the brain export ammonia as glutamine.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks how extrahepatic tissues (brain, kidney) handle and release ammonia. What is the main source of ammonia released in the kidney/extrahepatic tissues. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ammonia is carried in blood as non-toxic glutamine (glutamine synthetase); renal glutaminase releases NH, 4 NH4 excretion (important in acidosis).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with hepatic failure becomes confused. Which organ is extremely sensitive to ammonia toxicity. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ammonia depletes a-ketoglutarate ( I TCA cycle/ATP), increases glutamine in astrocytes (osmotic swelling, cerebral oedema) and disturbs neurotransmission 4 hepatic encephalopathy (asterixis).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist explains where the two nitrogen atoms of urea come from. Which enzymes generate the immediate nitrogen donors (ammonia) for urea synthesis. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Urea N: one from free NH, (glutamate dehydrogenase, glutaminase) ￿ carbamoyl phosphate (CPS-I. mitochondria); the other from aspartate (made by AST) entering via argininosuccinate synthetase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student draws the urea cycle and labels the step joining citrulline and aspartate. Which enzyme catalyses this reaction. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Urea cycle: CPS-I ￿ OTC (ornithine + carbamoyl phosphate -> Citrulline) 4 ASS (citrulline + aspartate 4 argininosuccinate, ATP4AMP) 4 ASL ( arginine + fumarate) ￿ arginase (4 urea + ornithine).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A newborn develops lethargy, seizures and respiratory alkalosis with markedly elevated plasma ammonia. Which metabolic process is primarily defective. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Urea cycle disorders: hyperammonaemia stimulates the respiratory centre 4 respiratory alkalosis (vs organic acidaemias 4 metabolic acidosis). Treat with protein restriction. sodium benzoate/phenylbutyrate. dialysis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 2~month-old boy has lethargy, vomiting and seizures; labs show hyperammonaemia with markedly elevated urinary orotic acid and low citrulline. Which enzyme is most likely deficient? [KIMS 26 . QIMS 25 . CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: OTC deficiency (commonest urea cycle defect): carbamoyl phosphate accumulates 4 enters pyrimidine synthesis 4 orotic aciduria; citrulline is NOT formed. CPS-I deficiency: no orotic aciduria.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A geneticist counsels the parents of a boy with a congenital hyperammonaemia; the mother is a carrier. Which urea cycle enzyme deficiency is X-linked? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: OTC deficiency is X-linked recessive (severe in males, variable in carrier females); all other urea cycle defects are autosomal recessive.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An infant has hyperammonaemia with markedly increased plasma citrulline and argininosuccinate in urine, plus friable hair. Which enzyme is deficient? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Citrulline accumulates when the cycle is blocked after it: ASS deficiency (citrullinaemia very high citrulline) or ASL deficiency (argininosuccinic aciduria - high argininosuccinate, trichorrhexis nodosa).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies the synthesis of creatine and its excretory product used to estimate GFR. What is the immediate precursor of creatinine. [HITEC 25]

options.B: Creatine (made from arginine, glycine and methionine/SAM)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Creatine (kidney: arginine + glycine 4 guanidinoacetate; liver." + SAM methyl) ￿ creatine phosphate in muscle 4 spontaneous non-enzymatic cyclisation to creatinine (-2%/day, proportional to muscle mass).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man taking an arginine supplement asks about nitric oxide. Arginine is converted to NO, which performs all the following functions EXCEPT: [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NO synthase." arginine + O, + NADPH 4 NO + citrulline. NO activates soluble guanylyl cyclase 4 CGMP 4 smooth-muscle relaxation (vasodilatation, erection), inhibits platelets; macrophage NO kills microbes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In the kidney, arginine availability (regulated by arginase11) determines production of a vasodilator. Which compound requires arginine as its substrate. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arginase11 (kidney, mitochondria) and NOS compete for arginine; arginase activity reduces arginine available for NO synthesis - relevant to endothelial dysfunction.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man develops f lushing, headache and urticaria after eating spoiled tuna (scombroid poisoning). Which vasodilator, formed by decarboxylation of an amino acid, is responsible. IQIMS 25 . BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Histidine decarboxylase (PLP): histidine 4 histamine. Other decarboxylations: glutamate 4 GABA, tryptophan 4 serotonin, DOPA ￿ dopamine.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child has elevated blood histidine and low urocanic acid in sweat. Which enzyme is defective in histidinaemia. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Histidase converts histidine 4 urocanate 4 ... 4 FIGLU ￿ glutamate. Histidinaemia is usually benign.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In a histidine-load test for folate deficiency, a metabolite accumulates in urine. N-formiminoglutamate (FIGLU) is a metabolite of: [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: FIGLU transfers its formimino group to tetrahydrofolate; in folate deficiency FIGLU accumulates and is excreted after histidine loading.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A healthy man eats a carbohydrate-rich meal and two hours later feels energetic and full. Which pathway is most active in his liver. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fed state ( t insulin/glucagon): glycogenesis, glycolysis, lipogenesis. protein synthesis; insulin dephosphorylates/activates glycogen synthase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks which fuel the liver mainly uses and stores in the fed state. What is the major fuel taken up by the liver in the fed state. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fed liver: glucose enters via GLUT2 (insulin-independent), phosphorylated byglucokinase ￿ glycogen and fatty acids (exported as VLDL)," its own energy largely comes from amino-acid oxidation and glycolysis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In the fed state, adipocytes take up glucose under the influence of insulin. What do adipocytes mainly make from this glucose. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Adipose tissue lacks glycerol kinase, so it needs glucose (GLUT4) ￿ dihydroxyacetone phosphate ￿ glycerol-3-phosphate to esterify fatty acids into TAG.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: About four hours after a meal, a person's blood glucose is still normal. What mainly maintains blood glucose in this early post-absorptive state. [CKMC 26. MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Early fasting (4-16 h): hepatic glycogenolysis dominates," gluconeogenesis rises progressively and takes over after-24 h when liver glycogen (- 100 g) is exhausted.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 17-year-old has not eaten since 8 pm and is seen at 11 am with blood glucose 70 mg/dL. Which process primarily maintains his blood glucose at this time (-15 hours)? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Key note." the answer was marked in the source key. At-12- 16 h both processes contribute (roughly equally)," glycogenolysis is still the main source in the overnight fast, gluconeogenesis dominates after 24-36 h.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After a 24-hour fast, an elderly patient keeps normal blood glucose. Which hormones mainly stimulate gluconeogenesis at this stage. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucagon ( T PEPCK, F-1.6-bisphosphatase via l F-2,6-BP) and cortisol ( t PEPCK, muscle proteolysis supplies amino acids) drive gluconeogenesis; epinephrine acts in acute stress.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Which tissue can release free glucose into the blood during glycogenolysis? Choose the tissue. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Only liver (and kidney) have glucose-6-phosphatase; muscle G6P is used locally for glycolysis - muscle glycogen cannot support blood glucose.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A frightened student's blood glucose rises sharply before an exam. Which pathway does epinephrine stimulate to increase blood glucose? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Adrenaline (F ￿ CAMP ￿ PKA," al 4 Ca") activates phosphorylase kinase ￿ glycogen phosphorylase in liver and muscle," also stimulates lipolysis and glucagon, inhibits insulin (a2).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After a meal, insulin shuts down lipolysis in adipose tissue. How does insulin inactivate hormone-sensitive lipase? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin activates phosphodiesterase 3B ( I CAMP) and protein phosphatase-l ￿ dephosphorylated (inactive) HSL. Glucagon/adrenaline phosphorylate (activate) it via PKA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An obese man with insulin resistance has high circulating TNF-a and resistin from adipose tissue. How do these adipokines mainly contribute to insulin resistance. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TNF-a and FFAS activate serine kinases (JNK, IKKF, PKC) 4 serine phosphorylation of IRS-I 4 blocks P13K/Akt 4 l GLUT4 translocation. Adiponectin (low in obesity) improves sensitivity.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During prolonged fasting, a patient's brain adapts its fuel use. Which fuels can the brain use. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The brain cannot use fatty acids (do not cross the BBB well, low F-oxidation capacity); after -3 days of starvation ketone bodies supply up to 2/3 of brain energy, sparing protein.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student is asked about the slowest form of metabolic regulation, taking hours to days. Which type of regulation is slowest? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Speed: allosteric (seconds) > covalent modification/phosphorylation (minutes) > induction/repression of enzyme synthesis (hours-days), e.g. insulin induces glucokinase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with sickle cell anaemia has jaundice; urine shows increased urobilinogen but no bilirubin. Which combination is characteristic of prehepatic (haemolytic) jaundice? [HITEC 26]

options.A: t conjugated bilirubin, bilirubinuria and pale stools
options.C: t conjugated bilirubin with l urobilinogen
options.D: T unconjugated bilirubin, no bilirubinuria and t urine urobilinogen

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Unconjugated bilirubin is albumin-bound and not filtered ￿ no bilirubinuria; increased bilirubin load to the gut ￿ t urobilinogen reabsorbed and excreted in urine.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old with mild jaundice during fasting has unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with normal liver enzymes and no anaemia. What does unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with normal liver enzymes suggest? [BWP 25]

options.B: Haemolytic jaundice (or Gilbert syndrome if no haemolysis)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia: haemolysis ( T LDH, reticulocytes, I haptoglobin) or Gilbert syndrome (I UGTIAI activity. worse with fasting/stress, benign). [BWP 25]

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old has conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with clay-coloured stools and dark urine. What does this indicate.
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Obstructive pattern: t conjugated bilirubin. bilirubinuria, absent urobilinogen. pale stools. t ALP/GGT. pruritus: causes - stones, carcinoma head of pancreas, cholangiocarcinoma, strictures.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A dehydrated patient with suspected glycosuria has a negative Benedict's test on concentrated urine. Which substance in urine can cause a false-negative result? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Benedict's test detects reducing sugars (Cu" ￿ Cu.). High ammonium salts can keep cuprous oxide in solution (false negative)," ascorbic acid, salicylates, uric acid and creatinine give false positives.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks which body fluid compartment contains the largest share of total body water. Which compartment is largest? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ICF ~ 40% of body weight, ECF ~ 20% (interstitial 15%, plasma 5%), transcellular (CSF, synovial, Gl) - 1-2%.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains why water is vital for nutrient transport and waste excretion. Which function of water is involved? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Water is the universal biological solvent (polar, high dielectric constant) - dissolves nutrients, electrolytes and wastes for transport and renal excretion; also regulates temperature (high specific heat).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab technician measures plasma osmolality in a healthy adult. What is the normal osmotic pressure (osmolality) of plasma. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Normal plasma osmolality 285-295 mOsm/kg," calculated = 2[Na'] + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8. Osmolal gap > 10 suggests methanol, ethylene glycol, ethanol.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A post-operative patient needs IV fluid isotonic with plasma to avoid fluid shifts. Which solution should be given. IQIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 0. 9% Nacl (308 mOsm/L) expands ECF only. 5% dextrose is isotonic in the bag but becomes free water once glucose is metabolised (distributes to all compartments).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient is given IV 0.9% Nacl. What is the effect on body fluid compartments. [KIMS 25]

options.D: ECF volume increases with no change in ICF

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Isotonic expansion: osmolality unchanged 4 no water shift into cells; _25% stays intravascular, -75% enters the interstitium.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient accidentally receives 3% Nacl intravenously. What happens to his red blood cells. IQIMS 25]

options.A: They shrink (crenate) due to water loss

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypertonic ECF draws water out of RBCS 4 crenation; hypotonic solutions 4 swelling and haemolysis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with hypovolaemic shock after severe diarrhoea has BP 80/50 and pulse 130/min. What is the most appropriate initial fluid? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Resuscitate with isotonic crystalloid boluses (0. 9% saline or Ringer's lactate) to restore ECF volume." dextrose water provides no volume expansion.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient in septic shock needs large-volume resuscitation. Which IV fluid is generally preferred? [HITEC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Balanced crystalloids (RL, Plasma-Lyte) cause less hyperchloraemic acidosis and AKI than large volumes of 0. 9% saline; lactate is converted to HCO, by the liver.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man with 30% second~degree burns receives IV 5% albumin. How is this solution classified? [KIMS 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Colloids (albumin, gelatin, starches, dextran) contain large molecules that stay intravascular and exert oncotic pressure," crystalloids (saline, RL. dextrose) contain small solutes that cross capillaries.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient receives several litres of 0.9% saline after surgery and develops a normal anion gap acidosis. With which situation is hyperchloraemia most associated? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 0. 9% saline contains 154 mmol/L CI- (vs plasma ~100) ￿ dilutional hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis. Vomiting and diuretics cause hypochloraemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab report lists plasma anions. What is the most abundant anion in plasma. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Plasma anions: cl-_ 100-105, HCO,-_24, proteins (albumin) - 16 mEq/L, phosphate~2. ICF: phosphates and proteins.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient has a serum sodium of 128 mmol/L. What is this condition called? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Normal Na, 135-145 mmol/L; hyponatraemia < 135 (severe < 125). Assess volume status and serum osmolality to find the cause.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has confusion, lethargy and seizures with Na" 118 mEq/L. What is the most likely consequence of severe hyponatraemia. [KIMS 26]

options.B: Cerebral oedema due to water influx into brain cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypotonic ECF 4 water enters neurons 4 cerebral oedema 4 headache. seizures. coma. Correct slowly (< 8- 10 mmol/L per 24 h) to avoid osmotic demyelination.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An athlete drinks large volumes of plain water during a marathon without electrolyte replacement. What may result? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Exercise-associated/psychogenic water intoxication: free water excess dilutes Na,; ADH released by exercise worsens retention.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with Addison's disease has low serum sodium. Which condition causes a decrease in serum sodium (which mechanism is impaired)? [BWP 26. QIMS 25]

options.A: Adrenocortical insufficiency - impaired distal Na. reabsorption

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aldosterone deficiency ￿ renal Na. wasting," cortisol deficiency ￿ t ADH and impaired free-water excretion ￿ hyponatraemia with hyperkalaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man has severe dehydration from prolonged diarrhoea and serum Na, of 152 mmol/L. Which response helps restore water balance. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypernatraemia ( t osmolality) 4 thirst + ADH 4 water intake and renal conservation; volume depletion also activates RAAS.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old has severe gastroenteritis with vomiting and diarrhoea. What is an important cause of secondary (salt-and-water) dehydration. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary dehydration = pure water loss/deprivation (hypertonic); secondary dehydration = loss of salt and water (vomiting, diarrhoea, burns. diuretics) 4 ECF depletion.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic has Na" 120 mEq/L, measured plasma osmolality 290 mOsm/L and glucose 620 mg/dL. What is the diagnosis. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucose holds water in the ECF and dilutes Na.: corrected Na, measured + 1.6 (to 2.4) per ICK) mg/dL glucose above ICK) 4 -128-132. True pseudohyponatraemia (lab artefact) occurs with severe hyperlipidaemia/paraproteinaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man has nausea, vomiting, headache, fatigue, weakness, dizziness and muscle cramps after heavy sweating. Which biochemical parameter is primarily affected? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Electrolyte disturbances (hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia. hypomagnesaemia) cause neuromuscular and Gl symptoms; check serum electrolytes first.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on diuretics has an ECG with a prolonged QT (QU) interval, flattened T waves and U waves. Which electrolyte disturbance is responsible. [Prof 24. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypokalaemia: flat/inverted T waves, prominent U waves, ST depression, apparent QT (QU) prolongation, arrhythmias; muscle weakness, ileus, polyuria.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A dialysis patient has palpitations; ECG shows tall peaked T waves, widened QRS and bradycardia. Which electrolyte abnormality is present? [LHR 26. HITEC 26. QIMS 25. HITEC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hyperkalaemia ECG progression." peaked T 4 prolonged PR, flat P 4 wide QRS 4 sine wave 4 VF/asystole. Emergency: IV calcium gluconate (membrane stabilisation), insulin + glucose, salbutamol, then removal (resins, dialysis).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with CKD has serum K" of 6.5 mEq/L. What is the most serious clinical concern. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hyperkalaemia partially depolarises cardiac cells (inactivating Na, channels) -> conduction block and fatal arrhythmias; immediate ECG and treatment needed.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An accidental overdose of an IV electrolyte causes cardiac arrest in diastole. Overdose of which electrolyte may cause cardiac arrest? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: IV KCI must be diluted and infused slowly (< 10-20 mmol/h peripherally) - bolus K. causes asystole (used in lethal injection).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on furosemide develops muscle weakness and low potassium. Which mechanism explains the hypokalaemia. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Increased urinary K" loss ( t distal flow and Na. delivery, secondary

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loop and thiazide diuretics increase distal Na. delivery and flow 4 t principal-cell K, secretion; volume depletion adds aldosterone 4 hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student lists common causes of hypokalaemia. Which group commonly causes hypokalaemia. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypokalaemia: Gl loss (vomiting, diarrhoea), renal loss (diuretics, hyperaldosteronism, Cushing's, RTA), shift into cells (insulin, F2-agonists, alkalosis). Renal failure/Addison's/acidosis cause hyperkalaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with metabolic alkalosis has a falling serum potassium. How does potassium distribution between ICF and ECF change in metabolic alkalosis. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alkalosis: H. leaves cells to buffer the ECF and K, enters in exchange 4 hypokalaemia; the reverse occurs in acidosis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with type I diabetes in DKA has pH 7.15, HCO, 12, K" 5.8 mmol/L and glucose 420 mg/dL. What causes the increased extracellular K+? [KIMS 26]

options.B: Shift of K. from cells to ECF
options.D: Increased K, intake so K, falls rapidly once

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin deficiency. hyperosmolality and acidosis shift K. out of cells," total body K, is actually depleted by osmotic diuresis insulin is started.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains aldosterone's action on potassium at the cellular level. How does aldosterone increase potassium secretion? [QIMS 25]

options.A: Increases apical ROMK (renal outer medullary K.) channels and
options.B: Increases Na"/K' pump in intercalated cells only Na'/K'_ATPase in principal cells
options.D: Inhibits epithelial channels in the PCT

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aldosterone 4 mineralocorticoid receptor 4 SGKI 4 t ENaC, T basolateral Na'/K'_ATPase, t apical ROMK/BK channels 4 K, secretion into the lumen.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman has tingling around the mouth and carpopedal spasm after thyroid surgery; Chvostek's sign is positive. Which electrolyte imbalance causes tetany and Chvostek's sign. [AMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low ionised Ca" lowers the threshold of nerve Na. channels 4 spontaneous firing ￿ tetany (Trousseau, Chvostek), laryngospasm, seizures, prolonged QT. Causes: hypoparathyroidism, vitamin D deficiency, alkalosis. hypomagnesaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks which electrolyte is essential for both muscle contraction and nerve impulse transmission (neurotransmitter release). Which electrolyte is this. [HITEC 25 . BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ca" excitation-contraction coupling (troponin C, calmodulin), neurotransmitter exocytosis, coagulation (factor IV), hormone secretion, membrane stability.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A haematologist explains why citrate in blood bags prevents clotting. For which plasma function is calcium essential? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ca" (factor IV) is needed for several steps of the coagulation cascade (binding of vitamin K-dependent factors to phospholipid); citrate, EDTA and oxalate chelate calcium.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with polycythaemia has sluggish blood flow. Which factor has the greatest influence on blood viscosity. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Viscosity rises steeply with haematocrit (RBC concentration)," plasma proteins (fibrinogen, paraproteins) contribute less. High viscosity thrombosis, hypertension.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman has periorbital puffiness, oliguria, haematuria, hypertension, proteinuria and dysmorphic RBCS. Which renal syndrome is most likely? [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Haematuria with RBC casts/dysmorphic RBCS = glomerular bleeding (nephritic). Nephrotic: > 3.5 g/day proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia, oedema, hyperlipidaemia, lipiduria.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic patient has a chronic rise in serum creatinine over several years. What is the most likely cause? [BWP 25]

options.A: Diabetic nephropathy - thickened GBM and mesangial expansion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Diabetic nephropathy is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease; screen with urine albumin:creatinine ratio annually; ACE inhibitors/ARBs and SGLT2 inhibitors slow progression.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old hypertensive man has ankle swelling; BUN 40 mg/dL, creatinine 3.0 mg/dL. Which investigation best indicates renal excretory function (GFR)? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Creatinine clearance (24-h urine) or eGFR (CKD-EPI from serum creatinine, age, sex) estimate GFR; serum creatinine alone rises only after ~50% Ioss of function.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old with long-standing diabetes has ankle oedema and frothy urine; diabetic nephropathy is suspected. Which is the most appropriate test to assess kidney function (stage CKD)? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CKD staging uses eGFR (GI-G5) plus albuminuria category (Al-A3). Urine albumin:creatinine ratio detects early diabetic kidney damage.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with end-stage renal disease has confusion, tremors, pruritus and markedly raised BUN. These symptoms are most consistent with which condition. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uraemia." accumulation of nitrogenous wastes 4 encephalopathy, asterixis, pericarditis. nausea. pruritus, bleeding (platelet dysfunction) - indications for dialysis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A nephrology resident lists the dialysis options available for a patient with ESRD. Which are the two main types of dialysis used clinically. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Haemodialysis uses an artificial membrane (AV fistula access)," peritoneal dialysis uses the peritoneum as the membrane (CAPD). Both rely on diffusion and ultrafiltration.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains how small solutes are removed during dialysis. Which principle mainly moves small solutes across the dialysis membrane? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Solutes (urea, creatinine. K,) diffuse down concentration gradients; fluid is removed by ultrafiltration (pressure) in HD or osmosis (glucose dialysate) in PD.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with CKD has dangerously high potassium unresponsive to medical treatment. Which electrolyte abnormality is effectively treated by dialysis. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Indications for urgent dialysis (AEIOU).. Acidosis, Electrolytes (refractory hyperkalaemia), Intoxications (lithium, methanol), Overload (fluid), Uraemia (encephalopathy, pericarditis).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with CKD has low calcium, high phosphate and secondary hyperparathyroidism. What is the biochemical basis. [KIMS 26]

options.D: Decreased renal synthesis of active vitamin D (1,25-(OH),D,)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CKD: I la-hydroxylase 4 I calcitriol ￿ I Ca" absorption; phosphate retention ( t FGF-23) ￿ t PTH 4 renal osteodystrophy. Treat with phosphate binders and calcitriol/alfacalcidol.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with CKD has hyperkalaemia; the team considers possible causes. Which is the LEAST likely cause of hyperkalaemia in CKD? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aldosterone INCREASES K, excretion (protective). Hyperkalaemia in CKD results from l GFR/distal flow, acidosis (K. shift out), cell injury, drugs (ACEI, ARBS, spironolactone) and hypoaldosteronism.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with CKD has metabolic acidosis with low serum HCO,-. Which electrolyte imbalance is most likely associated? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CKD acidosis (l ammoniagenesis. l acid excretion) shifts K. out of cells and reduced nephron mass limits K. excretion 4 hyperkalaemia; also hyperphosphataemia and hypocalcaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemistry student checks the ABG of a healthy volunteer. What is the normal arterial blood pH range? [WMC 26. CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: pH 7.35-7.45 ([H'] 35-45 nmol/L)." Paco, 35-45 mmHg," HCO,- 22-26 mEq/L. Acidaemia < 7.35, alkalaemia > 7.45.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In an ICU, a patient's pH falls to 6.85. Blood pH below approximately which value is generally considered incompatible with life. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Compatible range = 6.8-7.8 ([H'] 160- 16 nmol/L). Severe acidaemia depresses myocardial contractility and causes arrhythmias and vasodilatation; severe alkalaemia causes tetany and seizures.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student relates hydrogen ion concentration to pH. What is the relationship between [H'] and pH? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: pH = _logiolH']; a fall of 0.3 pH units doubles [H'] (pH 7.4 = 40 nmol/L, pH 7. 1 = 80 nmol/L).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A COPD patient retains CO, due to hypoventilation. How does increased PCO2 affect blood pH? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CO, + H,0 H,CO, H. + HCO,- (carbonic anhydrase) - raised PCO2 shifts the equation right 4 t H" 4 I pH (respiratory acidosis).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student calculates the ratio of bicarbonate to dissolved CO, (carbonic acid) at normal blood pH. What is the normal HCO, H,CO3 ratio at pH 7.4? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Henderson-Hasselbalch." pH = 6. 1 + log(HCO,- / 0.03 x PCO,) = 6. 1 + log(24/1.2) = 6. 1 + log 20 = 7.4. pH depends on the RATIO, not absolute values.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab reports a normal bicarbonate value for a healthy adult. What is the normal concentration of bicarbonate in arterial blood? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Normal HCO, 24 mEq/L (22-26). Total CO2 content (HCO,- + dissolved CO, + carbamino) is- 1-2 mEq/L higher.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemistry report shows total serum CO2 content. What is the normal serum total CO2 content? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Total CO, on venous chemistry ~ HCO,- + 1.2 mmol/L dissolved CO, 4 24-29 mEq/L," used as a surrogate for bicarbonate.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student is asked which chemical buffer system is the most important in the extracellular fluid. Which buffer is it? [CKMC 26 . HITEC 26. HITEC 25. BWP 25. LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bicarbonate is the main ECF buffer despite its pKa (6. 1) being far from 7.4, because it is an OPEN system: CO, is regulated by the lungs and HCO,- by the kidneys. It is especially important when HCO3 is lost (diarrhoea).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist compares buffers within cells. Which is the most important intracellular buffer system. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Intracellular phosphate (pKa 6.8) and proteins are the major ICF buffers," haemoglobin is the major buffer in red cells," phosphate and ammonia are the major urinary buffers.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student studies how the kidney excretes acid in the urine. What is the main function of the phosphate buffer in the renal tubules. [QIMS 25]

options.C: Trap secreted H, for excretion as titratable acid (H,PO,-)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Filtered HPO, - accepts secreted H, 4 H,PO,- (titratable acid, -30% of acid excretion); NHdNH4 provides the rest and adapts in chronic acidosis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains haemoglobin's role in buffering CO, transport. Which statement best explains haemoglobin's buffer role? [QIMS 25]

options.B: It binds H. ions (via histidine) during CO, transport, especially when deoxygenated

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Deoxy-Hb is a weaker acid and binds more H, (Haldane effect), buffering H. formed from CO, in RBCS; HCO,- exits in exchange for Cl- (chloride shift).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks which non-bicarbonate buffers contribute most to blood pH regulation. Among these, which buffer system plays a primary role in blood (non-bicarbonate)? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Blood buffering: bicarbonate (-2/3), haemoglobin and plasma proteins (- 1/3), phosphate (small). "Renal" and "respiratory" are physiological compensations, not chemical buffers.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student titrates a weak acid with a strong base and records the pH. At the half-equivalence point, what is expected? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: At half-neutralisation [A-] = [HA] ￿ log(l) = 0 4 pH = pKa. A buffer works best within pKa + l.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: On a titration curve of a weak acid, a student identifies the f lattest region where pH changes least. Where is the buffering region observed? [KIMS 25]

options.A: Around the point where pH= pKa

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Maximum buffer capacity occurs at pH = pKa (equal acid and conjugate base)," the curve is steep near the equivalence point.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student rearranges the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation in a practical. What can it be rearranged to calculate? [KIMS 25]

options.B: The dissociation constant (pKa) or ratio of base to acid

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: pH = pKa + log([A-]/[HA]); knowing pH and the ratio gives pKa, or knowing pKa and pH gives the ratio of conjugate base to acid.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student calculates the anion gap from a patient's electrolytes. How is the anion gap calculated? [CKMC 26] ci-
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AG= Na. (Cl- + HCO,-) = 140- (104 + 24) = 12 (8-16,._12 + 4). Including K. adds-4.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab handbook lists the normal plasma anion gap. What is the normal anion gap. [KIMS 25. BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Normal AG 8- 12 mEq/L (older methods 12-16). High AG metabolic acidosis: MUDPILES (Methanol, Uraemia, DKA, Propylene glycol/Paraldehyde, Iron/lNH, Lactic acidosis, Ethylene glycol, Salicylates).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: The anion gap represents unmeasured anions. Which major unmeasured anion mainly accounts for the normal anion gap. [Prof24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Albumin (negatively charged) contributes most of the normal AG; each I g/dL fall in albumin lowers AG by-2.5 mEq/L - correct the AG in hypoalbuminaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A cirrhotic patient has an anion gap of 3 mEq/L. What is the most common cause of a decreased serum anion gap. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low AG: hypoalbuminaemia (commonest), IgG myeloma (cationic paraprotein), lithium, bromide intoxication (falsely high Cl-), hypercalcaemia/hypermagnesaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic in ketoacidosis has pH 7.1, low bicarbonate and a raised anion gap. In which other condition is the anion gap also increased? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Normal AG (hyperchloraemic) acidosis: diarrhoea, RTA, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, NH,Cl. saline. High AG: added organic acids (lactate. ketoacids, toxins) or uraemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A newly diagnosed type I diabetic has deep breathing and drowsiness. Which acid-base disturbance does uncontrolled type l DM cause. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Insulin deficiency + glucagon excess 4 lipolysis 4 hepatic F-oxidation 4 acetoacetate and F-hydroxybutyrate (strong acids) 4 high-AG metabolic acidosis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks what primarily causes acidosis in uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. What is the primary cause? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ketoacids (F-hydroxybutyrate > acetoacetate) exceed buffering," hyperglycaemia causes osmotic diuresis but not acidosis. Urine dipstick (nitroprusside) detects acetoacetate, not F-OHB.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 6-year-old girl has vomiting, rapid breathing and drowsiness; pH 7.18, HCO,- 12, PCO, 28, glucose 550 mg/dL, ketones positive. What is the acid-base diagnosis? [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DKA triad: hyperglycaemia (> 250), ketonaemia/ketonuria, metabolic acidosis (pH < 7.3, HCO,- < 18) with raised anion gap. Treat with fluids, insulin, K. replacement.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic woman has polyuria, abdominal pain and rapid breathing; pH 7.20, HCO, 10, anion gap 22, ketones positive. What is the diagnosis. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: High-AG metabolic acidosis with ketones and hyperglycaemia = DKA. RTA gives a normal AG," starvation ketosis rarely lowers HCO,- below 18.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with diabetic ketoacidosis has ABG pH 7.22, HCO,- 14, PCO, 32. What is the disorder. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: pH I with HCO, l = metabolic acidosis,. PCO, l is compensation (expected 1.5 x 14 + 8 = 29 + 2 - slightly inadequate).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man has pH < 7.3, HCO,- < 24 mEq/L and a low PCO,. Which disorder best describes his state. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stepwise ABG: (l) pH - acidaemia," (2) which variable explains it - low HCO, metabolic; (3) compensation - low PCO,; (4) anion gap," (5) delta ratio for mixed disorders.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient vomits repeatedly from gastric outlet obstruction and develops alkalosis. Loss of which ion mainly contributes to metabolic alkalosis in gastric vomiting. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Each H. secreted by parietal cells generates one HCO3 in blood (alkaline tide)," vomiting removes the H. so the HCO3 Stays. Cl- and volume depletion maintain the alkalosis (saline-responsive).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student lists causes of metabolic alkalosis. What is the most common cause of metabolic alkalosis (among these)? [MUL 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Metabolic alkalosis: vomiting/NG suction, diuretics, hyperaldosteronism, Cushing's, Bartter/Gitelman, milk-alkali syndrome. Diarrhoea, CKD, lactic acidosis and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors cause ACIDOSIS.
